summary: Official combining cellarer and terrar in smaller houses, or keeping internal accounts in larger ones.

label: Burst of the Sweeping Flames
summary: A Rego Ignem spell (Level 25) that causes a fire to explode outward along the ground as if blown, igniting anything in its path for +5 to +15 damage.

label: Burthred
summary: Young man betrothed and married to Christina of Markyate, who refused him.

label: Burthulet
summary: Frigid place.

label: Bury St. Edmund's
summary: A wealthy abbey town in West Suffolk wholly under the abbey's control, founded in 633 by King Sigebert and home to the tomb of St. Edmund, a major pilgrimage site.

label: Buss
summary: A small, long, narrow seagoing ship descended from the Viking knarr, carrying around 20 tons and used for coastal trade and fishing.

label: Busybody
summary: A useful minor Flaw representing a character compelled to meddle in others' affairs; listed as a resource increasing an agent's Resistance Strength.

label: Butatschah-iglis
summary: A Swiss lake faerie pretending to be a demon: a vast amorphous sack covered in fire-beaming eyes that eats fish and fishermen, guarding a supposed gateway to Hell.

label: Butler
summary: Nominally the king's wine steward, responsible for feeding the court.

label: Butterfly and Two-Pronged Fork
summary: Ancestral Tremere symbols of Aita's priesthood and Pluto.

label: Buying a Chair
summary: Alpine process by which a covenant pledges ten pawns of vis a year from a registered source to give a magus a vote at tribunal.

label: By evening ash and morning dew I send your charms away from you
aliases: By evening ash and morning dew I send your charms away from you
summary: Incantation/Malediction 50 removing a Major Virtue.

label: By His Works
summary: CrMe 5 spell refreshing a memory in the caster, used to recall sigils perfectly.

label: Byrek
summary: A clumsy but tireless grog from the Horse Clan of Crintera who wears a magical horse-bone amulet said to make him as swift and tireless as a horse.

label: Byrek's magical amulet
summary: A magical amulet carved of horse bone given to Byrek by his witch mother of the Horse Clan, said to make him as swift and tireless as a horse, though its true power is unknown.

label: Byzantine Empire
summary: The empire against which Sikelgaita of Sicily's husband fought; Norman conquests in Byzantium were lost after the war turned against her family.

label: Byzantine Priest
summary: Companion template: a married Eastern priest born in Constantinople who fled its sack.

label: Cú Chulainn
summary: Legendary hero cited for dangerous childhood stories.

label: Cîteaux
summary: The mother house of the Cistercian Order in France where the abbots meet annually in September; founded by Robert of Molesme in 1098.

label: Cabal
summary: A coordinated group of House Tytalus followers who anonymously join to pursue a shared goal of changing society, using esoteric names and identifying symbols.

label: Cabal Legacy
summary: Flaw that for the Fraternity merely means badgering by would-be Initiates.

label: Cabal of Frankish Gold
summary: Tytalan cabal supporting the Lotharingian Tribunal.

label: Cabal of the Crushed Viper
summary: Tytalus cabal opposing the chivalric ideal, members taking Arthurian pseudonyms.

label: Cabal of the Golden Coin
summary: Secret cabal, begun by Tytalus magi, that fixes the outcome of Hermetic Tourney contests to maximize prizes.

label: Cabal of the Laden Cart
summary: Tytalus cabal founded by Kybella to entrap Death, obsessed with the Ankeu.

label: Caballer
summary: Catalan vassal who rules a single castle.

label: Caballero
summary: Iberian mounted warrior whose status depends on keeping his gear and serving in the field.

label: Caballero Villano
summary: Caballero tied to a particular town who must live there and be ready to muster.

label: Cad Gadu
summary: The domus magna of House Ex Miscellanea on an island in a Welsh lake within a strong magical regio; site of the final battle against Damhan-Allaidh, formerly home of the Columbae.

label: Caduceus
summary: Symbol of Mercury/Hermes: a winged staff with entwined serpents.

label: Caecilius
summary: A Quaesitor of Durenmar and a contender for the oldest magus in the Tribunal, who ruled firmly that no wilderness had been invaded in the Crintera/Guardians of the Forests dispute.

label: Caelum
summary: Faerie realm of air and stars, associated with stone alignments.

label: Caen
summary: Town on the River Orne, William the Conqueror's effective capital, dominated by Caen Castle.

label: Caen Castle
summary: Enormous fortress begun in 1060, recently extended by Philip II.

label: Caereidyn
summary: Mynyddawg's seat, near Edinburgh.

label: Caerleon
summary: Welsh site near which one faerie Camelot was found.

label: Caerwent
summary: A place in Britain whose old lord imprisoned his young bride; the hawk-knight, father of Yonec, was killed there for love of the lady.

label: Caesar Tower
summary: Square watchtower and prison in Provins.

label: Caesarea
summary: Diocese in which Athlit is situated.

label: Caesarius of Arles
summary: Author of the first regulations specifically for nuns in the early sixth century.

label: Cagair an t-Aile
summary: Domnhull Beg's osprey familiar (Whisper of the Wind), who reads over his shoulder and loves courtly romances and Arthurian legend.

label: Cage of Change
summary: An iron enchanted cage (CrVi 30) that gives a captive animal 5 Warping Points in hope it becomes monstrous and can be harvested for Muto vis.

label: Cagliari
summary: Sardinian port near Verdi.

label: Cagoux
summary: Master-thieves who enforce the King of the Beggars' edicts as his chief nobles.

label: Cailleach
summary: An evil faerie hag that plagues the covenant of Circulus Ruber, unable to breach its Aegis of the Hearth and taking out its frustration on travelers.

label: Cailleach Bheur
summary: The blue hag of Ireland and Scotland representing winter, guardian of streams and wells, who spreads her plaid over the land until summer.

label: Cailleach Glioc
summary: Companion template: an elderly Highland wise woman who makes small potions and amulets with conditions attached.

label: Cailleach Magic
summary: Gruagach Virtue allowing Spontaneous Magic like Diedne Magic; integrated as a teachable Virtue with the Hedge Wizard Flaw instead of Dark Secret.

label: Cain
summary: Faeries are said by some to be his descendants, gone to Arcadia when banished to Nod.

label: Cairo
summary: City where al-Husayn's head and al-Shafi'i are interred.

label: Cairo Way
summary: An alleyway leading from Devil's Lane serving as a regio entrance to its eponymous city.

label: Caithlinn
summary: A maga of House Diedne of Oakdell covenant against whom Severus Maximus declared Wizard War in 1004 AD.

label: Caithness
summary: Northern province settled by Norsemen; site of a battle with Damhan-allaidh.

label: Caitlin Ex Miscellanea
summary: Aindread's filia, a young polite maga who sometimes represents Burnham at tribunal and refuses all negotiations; has mismatched eyes.

label: Caitlin of Crun Clach
summary: Major magus of the Loch Leglean Tribunal from the covenant of Crun Clach.

label: Caitlin Suil Uaine
summary: Maga who leads the covenant of Crun Clach, won the hill from the Prince of the Grey Jerkin at shinty, keeps a stable of faerie horses and maintains diplomacy with sith and neighboring tribunals.

label: Calabria
summary: Covenant in southern Italy weakened by a Verdi-instigated Mussulman invasion; its Magi fled to Novgorod.

label: Caladrius
summary: A magnificent all-white mystical bird of the Magic Realm, sought by royal households, which can draw a non-fatal disease out of a sick person into itself and burn it away by flying toward the sun.

label: Calatrava
summary: Fortress in Castile where the Order of Calatrava was founded.

label: Calc
summary: Additional Anglo-Saxon Futhorc rune meaning "Chalk", with no Elder Futhark equivalent.

label: Caledonian Forest
summary: Primeval hardwood forest covering much of the Highlands.

label: Calgacus
summary: Leader of the Caledonians killed at Mons Graupius in A.D. 84.

label: Caligula
summary: Tiberius' heir who did not inherit the title Antistes Mercuria.

label: Caliph
summary: Successor to the Prophet, religious and secular leader of the Muslim state; nominal head for Sunnis in Baghdad.

label: Call for Justice
summary: Greater ReVi ritual calling on Nemesis to deliver justice; never attempted.

label: Call of Morpheus
summary: Andru's group-target version of Call to Slumber.

label: Call of the Hunter
summary: Boar King power to appear anywhere in his forest.

label: Call of the Rushing Waters
summary: An Intellego Aquam spell (Level 15) that lets the caster locate any natural body of water to which they have an Arcane Connection by hearing it.

label: Call the Basilisk
summary: Kentigern's CrAn(Re) 50 spell that creates a basilisk so he can study them safely.

label: Call the Dream
summary: A Rego Mentem spell letting the caster determine the theme of a sleeping person's dream by touch.

label: Call the Fallen Eagles from the Mist
aliases: Call the Fallen Eagles from the Mist
summary: Rego Mentem level 65 Ritual used on ancient battlefields to summon and control up to 10,000 pagan dead.

label: Call the Flock
summary: Power (ReAn 35) summoning a cloud of mundane birds to gather around the singer.

label: Callanish Stones
summary: Great stone circle said to lead to Barathrum, Antrum and Tartarus; a gateway to Arcadia with aura 10.

label: Calliclean
summary: One of the two ethical viewpoints of House Tytalus's Philosophy of Conflict, represented by clockwise spiral symbolism indicating growth and perception.

label: Calliclean Ethics
summary: A branch of Tytalan philosophy named after the Sophist Callicles that champions physis over nomos, holding that the strong should throw off the restraints of custom; symbolized by a clockwise spiral.

label: Callicles
summary: An ancient Greek Sophist quoted in the Analects of Tytalus who championed natural justice of the strong over the laws of weaklings; the Calliclean view is named after him.

label: Calling on God's Aid
summary: Templar practice of calling God's aid before battle.

label: Calling the Council of the Trees
aliases: Calling the Council of the Trees
summary: A Rego Herbam ritual (Level 45) that compels all magical and potentially mobile trees within a woodland to gather to hold meetings and summon ancient powers; trees remain animated for a month.

label: Calling the Council of Trees
summary: A Hermetic ritual many magi believe to be of druidical origin, though House Merinita claims it for their Founder.

label: Calling the Khrafstar
summary: Naonhaithya's Power releasing swarms of noxious creatures from his body.

label: Calling the Odious Drought
summary: A Perdo Aquam Ritual spell (Level 50) with an Auram requisite that causes a drought over the surrounding area, drying streams and rivers.

label: Calm Temper
summary: Temper of tolerance and peace, tied to Hope and opposing the sin of Wrath.

label: Calm the Motion of the Heart
aliases: Calm the Motion of the Heart
summary: A spell that removes one emotion from the target until it appears again naturally, such as making an angry person stop being angry.

label: Calming Touch
summary: A power of the angel Nasir (3 points, Animal/Mentem) that, by touching the target, calms their fears and reassures them in the face of dangerous terrain.

label: Calorific Stone
summary: A Level 10 Alteration Reagent that, when dropped into water, makes the water boil within seconds; a single dose can affect a bathtub of water.

label: Calots
summary: A court of Parisian argotiers who sit slack-jawed as apparent dotards.

label: Caltis of Tremere
summary: A young Tremere magus among the members recruited to Nigrasaxa.

label: Calum
summary: A 135-year-old gruagach and magus Ex Miscellanea, effective head of the covenant of Mac Gruagach, who seeks to integrate Highland gruagach magic with Hermetic magic; gnarled, fur-covered and smelling of rotting vegetation.

label: Calvinus of Jerbiton
summary: A Florum magus with the Gentle Gift, posing as Piet's uncle, skilled in urban magic, illusions and spying; father of Petrus.

label: Calypso
summary: Figure in The Odyssey who wants to keep Odysseus from going home.

label: Camail
summary: Mail hood covering head, forehead, lower face.

label: Caman
summary: Walking stick and club used for shinty, like a golf club with a six-to-eight-inch head.

label: Camaret
summary: Village.

label: Camargue
summary: Large, flat, marshy delta region of the Rhône River, home of magical wild horses.

label: Camargue Delta
summary: The wild and inhospitable delta where the Rhone ends, home to a ghostly horse that keeps a larder of up to 100 wicked children.

label: Cambrian Mountains
summary: The mountain range in Wales where Aneirin's tomb lies and across which his spirit wanders, helping those who further his ideals and punishing those who oppose them.

label: Cambridge
summary: A medium-sized port town on the edge of the Fens with a young university and an unusual number of natural magicians, owing to the influence of Schola Pythagoranis.

label: Cambunian Mountains
summary: Mountains on the northern border of Thessaly where the Daughters of Erictho dwell in cliffside caves near Faerie regiones.

label: Camelot
summary: Legendary Arthurian site duplicated by faeries in several places, near Edinburgh, in Winchester and near Caerleon.

label: Camerlengo
summary: Director of the papal camera (finances).

label: Camille of Mercere
summary: Redcap whose messages were read; later fined for using a knight to harvest vis.

label: Camuel
summary: Camuel the Dark Angel, a Throne who wrestled with Jacob; once an archangel, he was reduced after trying to prevent Moses receiving the Torah and now mediates prayers of the faithful.

label: Canaan
summary: Land promised to Abraham, which became Israel.

label: Canaanite Necromancy
summary: Long-forgotten tradition of necromancy sought by a magus through an Elysian quest.

label: Canals that Accommodate Seagoing Vessels
summary: CrTe 20 ritual creating a stone-lined canal wide and deep enough for seagoing ships, up to 909 paces long.

label: Cancer
summary: Sign of the Zodiac with its own element, temperament and decans in astrological correspondences.

label: Candida Casa
summary: St. Ninian's whitewashed church at Whithorn.

label: Candidus
summary: A powerful chalk-white eyeless faerie of Fontainebleau who grants wishes through bargains and trapped Lapis Crudus.

label: Cannophori
summary: Third rank of magi Bonisagi ('reed-bearers'), eligible for the Colentes Arcanorum.

label: Canon
summary: Member of a chapter of clergy serving an urban church who share common table and property.

label: Canon court
summary: Church courts held by archdeacons, bishops, and the curia, with no jury and no power to shed blood.

label: Canon Episcopi
summary: Church document declaring night rides illusions of faithless minds.

label: Canon Fulbert
summary: Canon of Notre Dame and uncle of Héloïse who hired Abelard as her tutor.

label: Canoness
summary: Woman who takes vows of chastity and obedience under a rule, usually Augustinian, but may own property and is more urban and active than nuns.

label: Canonesses
summary: Female religious living under a rule as canons.

label: Canonization
summary: Formal Church recognition of a saint, requiring two genuine miracles and a cultus.

label: Canons
summary: Cathedral administrative staff who elect a new bishop.

label: Canons of Patrick's Island
summary: Order of canons ('Black Canons') established on Inisphadraig by Saint Malachy who tend the Purgatory of Saint Patrick.

label: Cantations
summary: A low-level formulaic spell, from the Latin cantamen (little spell), especially when cast by an apprentice; it usually succeeds.

label: Canterbury
summary: Capital of Kent and metropolitan see of the English church; site of Becket's martyrdom and his shrine, the fourth main pilgrimage site in Europe.

label: Cantled Saddle
summary: Saddle used in tournaments or warfare giving +3 to resist being unhorsed by a charge.

label: Cantores
summary: Primarily Christian holy tradition dedicated to worshipping God through music, gathering in cities and great abbeys; opposed to bawdy secular music.

label: Cape Pachynus
summary: Site of the storm destroying a Roman fleet in 255 BC.

label: Cape Tainaron
summary: Southernmost point of mainland Greece in Achaea; its church was a nekromanteion to Hades and a cave beneath leads to Purgatory or the pagan dead.

label: Capellani
summary: The college of priests, deacons and sub-deacons serving in Rome; 70 in 1220.

label: Capetian Dynasty
summary: French royal dynasty descended from Hugh Capet, noted for piety, symbolized by gold lilies on blue.

label: Capital Messuage
summary: The lord's enclosed piece of land around his house, containing his hall, outbuildings and curtilage.

label: Capitulation of Neuss
summary: Agreement defining Papal lands.

label: Capnomancy
summary: Divinatory method using fumes from burning poppies, listed among Ceremonial Augury Phenomena.

label: Capo
summary: A game-defined merchant role: the leader of a merchant company who sets grand strategy, appoints factors, and engages in politics; characters must take the Capo Social Status Virtue.

label: Capocci Family
summary: One of Rome's great noble families.

label: Capons
summary: A court of Parisian argotiers who cheat marks at cards.

label: Cappadocia
summary: Home of wizards whose memoirs Bonisagus had.

label: Capra filia Bullfinch
summary: Bjornaer maga with an ibex heartbeast, a faerie midwife who believes she is destined to raise the new Jupiter Pennius.

label: Caprea
summary: A visiting Bjornaer maga who is a current guest at Crintera, working on a bestiary to present at the next Tribunal. She accidentally blinded the familiar of a visiting Jerbiton magus, Carolus.

label: Caprican of Merinita
summary: Leader and champion of Oleron, with Strong Faun Blood, hostile to Tytalus.

label: Capricorn
summary: Sign of the Zodiac with its own element, temperament and decans in astrological correspondences.

label: Captain of the Nightwalkers
summary: Leader of a nightwalker host, chosen by its supernatural patron, often marked by a pennant on the battlefield.

label: Captivating
summary: Bargaining art exchanging bodies with a faerie; warps the summoner but makes both immune to Faerie Calling.

label: Capuchonnes
summary: A movement begun by Durand in the 1180s to eradicate brigands, which massacred 3000 in Auvergne then became brigands themselves.

label: Caput
summary: The core lands at the center of a nobleman's affinity in England and France.

label: Caput Capra
summary: Easternmost Diedne covenant (981-1005) on the Loire near Fleury, first casualty of the Schism War in the Tribunal.

label: Cara filia Sigurd
summary: Bjornaer maga with a piest heartbeast who farms shellfish and lobsters in the lake beneath Sinews of Knowledge.

label: Carbuncle
summary: A gem said by some bestiaries to lie on the asp's forehead.

label: Carcassonne
summary: Siege site of the Albigensian Crusade.

label: Cardiff
summary: The most important town in Wales, in a country with few towns and a largely barter-based economy.

label: Cardinal-bishop
summary: Highest rank of cardinal: the bishops of seven small towns near Rome; the pope is ordained by a cardinal-bishop.

label: Cardinal-Bishop of Ostia
summary: Chief clergyman of Ostia who views magi as a great threat.

label: Cardinal-deacon
summary: Rank of cardinal; there can be up to 18.

label: Cardinal-priest
summary: Rank of cardinal; there can be up to 28.

label: Cardinal Robert Caurçon
summary: The cardinal who discovered the heresy of David of Dinant in 1215 after reading his book Quaternuli.

label: Cardinal Ugolino
summary: Cardinal appointed protector of Francis' followers who took control of the movement and tried to make the friars and Poor Sisters live more like Benedictines.

label: Cardus
summary: The east-west main street of the temple town bisecting the Decumanus.

label: Care of Souls
summary: Priest's seasonal activity of preaching giving willing congregants +1 to activities matching the sermon theme.

label: Carefree
summary: Virtue named in the text, associated with Larta chefs, smiths, minstrels or muses.

label: Careless Sorcerer
summary: A Minor Hermetic Flaw: the magus is slapdash with magical power and must roll two more botch dice than normal when casting spells.

label: Careless with (Ability)
summary: A Minor General Flaw: the character is reckless with a particular Ability, treating any rolled zero as a botch when using it.

label: Carhaix-Plouguer
summary: Settlement.

label: Carinthia
summary: Region suitable for Hermetic settlement.

label: Carissimus
summary: The captain of a mesnie, the lord's best friend or most skilled knight.

label: Carles
summary: A stone circle of forty-two stones about thirty meters across, surrounded by a bank, containing three round barrows and a rectangle of stones called the Porter's Lodge said to become a guarded house on certain nights.

label: Carlisle
summary: Town thirty miles southwest of Horsingas where the magi are wanted.

label: Carlo filius Innocu
summary: Merinita magus of Journeys End born of ice-distorted parents, with barbegazi features and powers.

label: Carlos
summary: Jerbiton magus of Literatus teaching at the University of Law.

label: Carmelite Nuns
summary: Order of female religious discussed in the chapter on women.

label: Carmelites
aliases: Order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel
summary: Order of Our Lady of Mount Carmel, originating from hermits on Mount Carmel in the Holy Land devoted to solitude and penance.

label: Carmentis
summary: The Cumaean sibyl, a Christian Magic Human with vast knowledge who guards a gate into Purgatory at Cumae.

label: Carmina Burana
summary: Famous work produced by the Goliards.

label: Carmine
summary: Follower of Flambeau of Iberian ancestry, Andru's model, mistress and wife, the only non-Jerbiton magus living permanently at Valnastium; a member of the lineage of Abydaros.

label: Carna
summary: Ancient Roman goddess who protected a princeling from vampires with hawthorn.

label: Carnac
summary: Stone monument site in Brittany to which the stones may allow travel.

label: Carneades
summary: Early critic of astrology and divination (219-126 BC).

label: Carnutes
summary: Ancient Gaulish tribe giving Chartres its name, home near Orléans.

label: Carol
summary: Circle dance.

label: Carolingian Dynasty
summary: Frankish dynasty named after Charlemagne; its blood often carries the Mythic Presence Virtue.

label: Carolingian Empire
summary: The Frankish empire whose institutions underlie the French and German noble systems.

label: Carolinus
summary: Charlemagne's mage-smith, several of whose apprentices were adopted by the Founder Jerbiton.

label: Carolus
summary: A scatterbrained young magus of Oculus Septentrionalis posing as an eccentric scholar; his raven familiar was blinded by Caprea of Bjornaer at Crintera after being mistaken for a spy.

label: Carouse
summary: A General Ability for enjoying oneself without adverse effects, such as consuming alcohol without passing out and gaining friends among the lower classes.

label: Carpathian Mountains
summary: Rumored site of the Blessed One's fortified covenant.

label: Cartagena
summary: Diocese subject to Rome.

label: Carthage
summary: Ancient city whose men worshiped Adramelech as Moloch.

label: Carthaginian Magic
summary: Ancient magic studied at Sansaron, more personal and possibly beyond Hermetic bounds.

label: Carthusians
summary: Austere order of monks and nuns following the Statutes of Saint Bruno, living in individual cells in complete silence.

label: Cartouche Magic
summary: Magic of ancient Egypt believed ancestral to learned magicians' magic.

label: Carve the Mystic Tower
summary: Jacinta's Perdo spell that etches away surplus rock to leave a building.

label: Cas-chrom
summary: The Highland footplow, a long-handled tool with an iron head used to turn soil.

label: Cas Corach
summary: Faerie hero said to have killed the daughters of Airitech.

label: Cascade of Rocks
summary: A Perdo Terram (PeTe 40) spell that can do great damage only if an opponent is on a steep hillside or cliff base, used by the School of Vilano; bypasses Magic Resistance.

label: Case Rulings
summary: Tribunal rulings arising from convictions or acquittals in criminal cases.

label: Casius
summary: 10th-century magus who invented Bellum.

label: Caspar
summary: One of the Three Wise Men whose body lies in the Shrine of Kings at Cologne Cathedral.

label: Cassiel
summary: Ruler of Araboth.

label: Cast away your mortal soul / And keep it safe in mortal bowl
aliases: Cast away your mortal soul / And keep it safe in mortal bowl
summary: Incantation/Consumption 50 transferring the caster's soul into a vis-containing vessel.

label: Castel Sant'Angelo
summary: Fortress used by the Papal court in need.

label: Castennac
summary: Village.

label: Castile
summary: A region of Mythic Europe with distinctive inheritance customs, including an example of a bride continuing to rule her own land except for her dowry, and where a widow may guard her son's lands.

label: Casting foci
summary: Items used by Verditius-trained magi in casting.

label: Casting Item
summary: Physical items in a Potent spell's design that the caster must touch to cast it.

label: Casting Tablet
summary: A variant Laboratory Text containing fixed instructions for casting a particular spell, usable by magi who have not learned the spell but dangerous and inflexible.

label: Casting Tokens
summary: Invested transport devices given to outer council members that serve as tokens for Magvillus's Aegis of the Hearth.

label: Casting Tools
summary: Tools that Verditius magi must use to cast Formulaic and Ritual spells; they can be enchanted via an Inner House Mystery and become permanent Arcane Connections.

label: Casting Total
summary: The total (Stamina + Form + Technique + Aura + stress die) determining whether a spell is cast, used notably when casting from a Casting Tablet.

label: Castle
summary: Fortification serving as refuge, staging ground and statement of status; described by Garrison, Defenses and Supplies.

label: Castle Defenses
summary: Castle characteristic describing walls, earthworks and moats, graded Shoddy to Excellent, giving a Defense Bonus and determining wall damage levels.

label: Castle Garrison
summary: Castle characteristic measured in combat groups of infantry, levies, knights, serjeants and archers; it sets a Weight of Numbers modifier and check interval.

label: Castle Kyburg
summary: Home castle of the Kyburgers.

label: Castle of Hapsburg
summary: Castle built by Bishop Werner of Straussburg.

label: Castle of the Grail
summary: Knights of the Green Stone headquarters, probably in a Rhine forest and possibly a regio with moving entrances.

label: Castle Rock
summary: The king of Scotland's seat in Edinburgh, where the Stone of Scone lies.

label: Castle Supplies
summary: Castle characteristic representing stored food, water and materials and the ability to resupply; it grants a Siege Conditions Bonus to supplies rolls.

label: Castles in Lieu of Halls
summary: On large estates a castle may replace the hall; castles are detailed in Covenants and summarized in Chapter Eight: Massed Combat.

label: Castra Solis
summary: The domus magna of House Flambeau in the Provençal Tribunal, a modest manor-house covenant founded by Kaeso atop a cave once sacred to Mithras, south of Bordeaux.

label: Castratus
summary: A Minor General Flaw: the character was castrated before puberty, suffering -3 social rolls in Latin culture; only available to characters born with testicles.

label: Castro Selvaggio
summary: Covenant castle whose magi created siege spells when besieged by a Milanese force; it was eventually sacked.

label: Castrum Antiquum
summary: Covenant founded in 852 in the ruins of a Roman fort on Hadrian's Wall; vanished without trace around 1030/1; home of Agricola of Tytalus.

label: Casual Augury (Numerology)
summary: Numerological augury used with Numbering the Flock to interpret numbers.

label: Casual Divination
summary: One-round divination observing signs in the immediate environment, rolled with Perception + Divination.

label: Casualty
summary: A group member with a Medium Wound or worse, unconscious, or unable to fight due to magic; casualties raise the Ease Factor to rally.

label: Cat
summary: A covered mobile shelter protecting attackers as they move to the base of castle walls.

label: Cat-Fish
summary: A Warped cat, fore-part black cat and back-part silvery fish, living in a tributary of the Seine.

label: Cat Like a Shadow
summary: Personal cat power, a version of Veil of Invisibility.

label: Catacombs of Rome
summary: Catacombs where Vespillo searched for the tombs of the Mercurian priesthood; his companions died there.

label: Catalaunian Fields
summary: Site of the 451 battle against Attila, with a Malevolent Infernal aura 3 and an Infernal regio yielding Perdo and Corpus vis.

label: Catalonia
summary: Iberian region whose chivalry follows the French model, with condes, viscondes, valvasores, cavallers and sotcastlàs.

label: Cataphract ghost
summary: Ghost of an Eastern Empire mounted warrior, Magic Might 15, recruited by House Tremere.

label: Cataplasm of Mandrake
summary: A Theriac of Level 5, Potency Moderate, a secret of the School of Salerno using mandrake and hyoscyamus; it numbs a body part and reduces Wound and Disease Penalties by 3.

label: Catapult of the Mighty Winds
summary: A Cr(Re)Au 30 spell that uses strong winds to hurl an object on an arched trajectory; once airborne the projectile's motion is natural and bypasses Magic Resistance, doing about +10 damage.

label: Cataracts
summary: A Minor Curse (Perdo Corpus effect) clouding the victim's eyes white and penalizing vision-based rolls and reading advancement by -3.

label: Catching Up On Masses
summary: Story seed where priests perform a marathon of backlogged masses, boosting the Dominion and disturbing faeries and demons.

label: Catechumen
summary: Adults undergoing instruction in Christianity prior to baptism.

label: Caterans
summary: Landless men adopted into a clan.

label: Cathach
summary: A trophy item Hibernian covenants need.

label: Cathars
summary: A heresy spreading in southern France (Languedoc) against which Brother Julian preaches and which the Church combats through the faculties of theology.

label: Cathedral
summary: The church of the bishop, usually the largest in the diocese's main town.

label: Cathedral Chapter
summary: A legal corporation of the canons of a cathedral, very influential in diocesan governance and electing the bishop by secret ballot.

label: Cathedral magic schools
summary: Icelandic clerical sorcery schools closed by investigation.

label: Cathedral of Bourges
summary: Half-built French-style cathedral begun 1195.

label: Cathedral of Chartres
summary: A cathedral nearing completion in 1220 where the Dreux and Capetian families compete to fund the most beautiful south-transept window.

label: Cathedral of Notre-Dame
summary: Paris cathedral begun 1163.

label: Cathedral of Sainte Croix
summary: Cathedral in Orléans whose priests were arrested.

label: Cathedral of St. Pierre in Beauvais
aliases: Cathedral of St. Pierre in Beauvais
summary: A new-style Gothic cathedral north of Paris standing over 150 feet tall, cited as an example of soaring cathedral architecture.

label: Cathedral of St. Étienne
summary: Second-earliest church in the new French style, in Sens.

label: Cathedral of St. Tryphaena
summary: Large ugly cathedral in Artakia holding St. Tryphaena's relics; Dominion aura 5.

label: Cathedral School Master
summary: A Major Social Status Virtue for a character who teaches at a cathedral school, requiring scores of 5 in Latin and Artes Liberales and granting 240 experience points.

label: Catinaccio
summary: Laurens's home.

label: Cato of Bonisagus
summary: A spectral Criamon Primus who was a Bonisagus magus before joining; he believes Criamon magi create the majority of all adulterations.

label: Cattle Raiding
summary: Major part of Highland life in which clans lift each other's cattle, especially at summer's end.

label: Catulus
summary: A Bjornaer apprentice ('cub'), the common property of the sept during the sleeping years of training.

label: Caucasus Mountains
summary: Likely location of the Tree Guarded by Michael.

label: Caudelix the Gaul
summary: A ghostly gladiator (Magic Might 20) of the Trier amphitheater, a burly giant of a man wielding a long-handled great axe.

label: Caul
summary: Hood of membrane with which most nightwalkers are born; kept by the nightwalker and in some traditions the source of his powers, granting caul-based Virtues.

label: Causabon
summary: A magus of House Bonisagus whose journal records his sense of the forests' primal power and his hope that the three domus magnae might share their secrets.

label: Cause Drowsiness
summary: Faerie power (Corpus or Animal) causing a touched human to fall asleep.

label: Cause Fatigue
summary: Faerie power causing a human to lose a fatigue level.

label: Cause Poisoning
summary: Silver Lady power coating objects in lead or arsenic.

label: Cause Sickness
summary: Faerie power (Corpus) causing a serious illness by touch or poisoning objects.

label: Causes And Cures
summary: Hildegard's summa on natural philosophy and Medicine.

label: Causimomancy
summary: Divinatory method using behavior of objects placed in a fire, listed among Ceremonial Augury Phenomena.

label: Cautious Sorcerer
summary: A Minor Hermetic Virtue letting a magus roll three fewer botch dice when casting spells or working in the laboratory.

label: Cautious with (Ability)
summary: A Minor General Virtue letting a character roll two fewer botch dice for a specific Ability.

label: Cautious with Chirurgy
summary: A Virtue commonly taken by empirici that reduces botch risk when using the Chirurgy Ability.

label: Cautious with Medicine
summary: A Virtue that enhances medical skill, reducing the risk of botches when using the Medicine Ability.

label: Cave of Cruachan
summary: Irish cave on Bricriu's Glen where the wolf-daughters of Airitech dwelt.

label: Cave of Polyphemus
summary: Foul cave atop a cliff, closed by a huge door stone, home of Polyphemus.

label: Cave of Sabinus
summary: Cave with a genius loci and Aquam vis, a luctatio.

label: Cave of the Inscription
summary: Cave under the Mendips with Magic aura 6 bearing the Inscription that binds Winter faeries; site of Averna's laboratory.

label: Cave of Twisting Shadows
aliases: Covenant of the Cave of Twisting Shadows
summary: A labyrinthine covenant serving as the domus magna of House Criamon, the largest and perhaps unfinished Great Work, whose structures embody the quest for the Enigma; its ghosts teach the Arts.

label: Cave of Twisting Shadows Lore
summary: Ability listed in the Alpine redcap template or Hera's statistics.

label: Caves of Naours
summary: Underground village with a Magic aura of 2, protected by a pact with a cave genius loci.

label: Cavillor
summary: Young Transitionalist Guernicus from the Roman Tribunal who defends accused magi.

label: Ceann cath
summary: The chief of a Highland clan.

label: Cehennem
summary: Sinkhole ('hell') linked by tunnel to Cennet; said to be bottomless, once a prison of Typhon, leading to Purgatory.

label: Ceilidh
summary: Gathering to tell stories and sing.

label: Celebratory Processions
summary: Nightwalker feasts and processions where spirits of animals are eaten to regenerate Long Term Fatigue.

label: Celeres of Bonisagus
summary: A Bonisagus magus living at Cunfin who strives to live by the chivalric ideals of the romances; next in seniority for Praeco after Renita, which worries Proctor.

label: Celestial Demons
summary: Demons who once inhabited Heaven and rejected it: angels who fell with Lucifer and the Watchers.

label: Celestial Disorientation
summary: Overwhelming effect on mortals entering a celestial regio, resisted with Stamina + Dominion Lore against regio rating x3.

label: Celestial Immunity
summary: Saint power making the recipient immune to physical damage while the threat lasts.

label: Celestial Magic
summary: Major Mystery Virtue replacing Planetary Magic; widens Laboratory Horoscopes, adds celestial Durations, favorable spellcasting hours and astrologically linked enchantments.

label: Celestine V
summary: Saintly Pope overwhelmed by intrigue and duped into resigning.

label: Cellarer
summary: Official responsible for provision of food and drink.

label: Cement (Reagent)
summary: A Level 5 alchemical Reagent, a dry powder that when sprinkled over loose earth or sand binds it as solid as granite, covering about three paces to six inches deep.

label: Cennet
summary: Sinkhole ('heaven') in Asia Minor in the Tribunal of the Levant with a monastery at its bottom founded by Saint Paulus.

label: Cenobite
summary: A magus living in an unrecognized covenant, as the Cherbourg magus is treated.

label: Censum
summary: Annual fee excusing a peasant from week work for a year, sometimes used as a punishment.

label: Centaur
summary: Faerie composite of horse and human that acts as a mentor guiding the young hero to adulthood; modern hippocentaurs are faerie duplicates of the ancient centaurs.

label: Centaury of Virtue
summary: Herb of Virtue listed with a +3 Flight shape and material bonus.

label: Centiloquium
summary: Aphorisms falsely ascribed to Ptolemy.

label: Central Massif
summary: Volcanic highland in eastern Aquitaine.

label: Centrus
summary: Target in the Line Range example who creeps round the wall to Lineus.

label: Centurions' Feast
summary: Honos's power that feeds 100 and heals those with Dutybound.

label: Cephalomancy
summary: Divinatory method using severing the head of a goat or donkey, listed among Ceremonial Augury Phenomena.

label: Cera
summary: Castle above Tomar, main Portuguese Templar chapterhouse.

label: Cerberus
summary: Guardian of the gate of Hades, whose statues guarded Roman cave taverns.

label: Cercistum
summary: A Primus of House Tremere during the Schism War, quoted observing that the Tytali fought a different battle on the Plain of Wolves than the Tremere pretended to.

label: Ceremonial Augury Phenomena
summary: Table of divinatory techniques (aeromancy through scrying) with bonuses for types of questions.

label: Ceremonial Divination
summary: Divination taking 15 minutes per 5 Ease Factor, using sympathetic magic and devices, rolled with Intelligence + Divination.

label: Ceremonial Figures
summary: Hermetic Geometry use of ceremonial casting with regular figures for +3 Casting Score.

label: Ceremonial Influence
summary: The ability of infernalists to inspire sinful Personality Traits in others via personal or ceremonial influence (simple die + Presence + Leadership).

label: Ceremonial Magic
summary: A method of increasing spellcasting power using natural correspondences, props, and prepared spaces, with casting time reduced by prepared spaces and the Mystical Choreography Virtue.

label: Ceremonial Spontaneous Magic
summary: A Minor Flaw possessed by all known members of the Mercurian lineage as part of the Mercurian Magic Virtue.

label: Ceremony
summary: Virtue and Ability allowing a leader to combine the efforts of several practitioners, granting a Ceremony bonus when awakening golems or seeking True Names.

label: Ceremony of Welcome
summary: Hermetic or setting concept referenced in the description of the Mythic Locations sites.

label: Ceres
summary: A goddess one of whose priestesses always serves as a hierophant of the Huntress in the Wood.

label: Ceridwen
summary: The witch whose cauldron gives Gwion Bach magical powers; example of a donor.

label: Ceroscopy
summary: Divinatory method using patterns of wax dripped in water, listed among Ceremonial Augury Phenomena.

label: Certamen
summary: The ritualized magical duel by which magi resolve disputes without resorting to Wizard's War.

label: Certamen Schools
summary: Distinct styles of certamen practiced mainly by Tremere magi, each with its own Finesse-based tricks; Harenarii pioneer most new schools.

label: Cerularius Bonisagi
summary: Tenth-century magus of Normandy who developed Lancea Magica.

label: Ceylan
summary: Verditius magus, amicus of Nerius, who gave him his mantle.

label: Châlons-en-Champagne
summary: Ecclesiastical city on the Marne with Notre-Dame basilica and Notre-Dame-de-Vaux.

label: Chaioth ha-Qadesh
summary: The four Angels of Judgement in Jewish tradition.

label: Chalcedon
summary: Council 451.

label: Chaldeans
summary: Ancient people whose secret lore was in Bonisagus's library.

label: Chalkydri
summary: Lion-bodied crocodile-headed sun creatures regulating heat.

label: Chalus
summary: Castle near Limoges where Richard was fatally wounded.

label: Chamber of Invisibility
summary: A Perdo Imaginem spell (Level 25) that makes a Group of creatures invisible; any affected character who moves or is touched makes everyone visible, and all still cast shadows.

label: Chamber of Spring Breezes
summary: A Creo Auram spell (Level 5) that creates a breeze of fresh air keeping a room's air breathable even if airtight.

label: Chamber of Summer Breezes
summary: A Creo Auram 10 spell with Ignem requisite creating a continual breeze of fresh, dry, warm air to keep a room's humidity and temperature constant, often cast on armarii and book chests.

label: Chamberlain
summary: Officer responsible for the king's chamber, retinue, and personal possessions.

label: Champ-Dolent
summary: Menhir marking the Schism War's final battle.

label: Champagne
summary: The pre-eminent fair cycle of Mythic Europe and a financial center, comprising fairs at Lagny, Bar-sur-Aube, Provins, and Troyes, guaranteed safe by the counts of Champagne.

label: Champagne Trade Fairs
summary: Six main fairs at Provins, Troyes, Lagny and Bar-sur-Aube where Redcaps run temporary Mercer Houses.

label: Champions
summary: Mercere magi who fight certamen on behalf of Redcaps.

label: Chamuel
summary: An archangel listed by Dionysus the Areopagite among the archangels.

label: Chancellor
summary: Master of the king's correspondence and chief advisor on foreign relations and the Church, almost always a priest.

label: Chancery
summary: A branch of the royal court headed by the chancellor Richard de Marsh, responsible for issuing documents under the Great Seal and keeping government records such as the Pipe Rolls.

label: Change Form
summary: Spirits of Deceit Power to change their shape to human or animal forms.

label: Change Size
summary: A Muto Terram effect (MuTe 10) enchanted into Falke's talisman that turns it into a leg-band, triggered by Perceive the Change.

label: Change the Nature of Vis
summary: MuVi 5 spell.

label: Changeling
summary: A story-seed faerie who comes regularly to a market for human food to sustain a stolen human child raised by her group living in nearby woodland.

label: Channel Islands
summary: Islands where a dialect close to Norman is spoken.

label: Chansons de geste
summary: Great romances with arcane lore.

label: Chantecler
summary: Cockerel caught by Reynard.

label: Chantry
summary: Minor Church Boon: income from reciting Masses for the dead.

label: Chaos of the Angry Wave
summary: Spell (ReAq 20) known by a template magus or referenced in the text.

label: Chaos of the Angry Waves
summary: A Rego Aquam spell (Level 30) that causes water to churn wildly in a circular area, overturning small craft and penalizing Swim rolls.

label: Chaotic
summary: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab or its outfittings are in constant flux or motion (-2 Safety, +1 Warping, +2 Muto or Rego).

label: Chaotic Magic
summary: A Major Hermetic Flaw: the magus's spontaneous magic is wild, and if it falls short of or exceeds the desired level by more than one, the storyguide decides the uncontrolled results.

label: Chapel That Cannot Sleep
summary: A chapel raised on an ancient battlefield where mythic death-roads converge, disturbing the sleeping dead near an unfortunate covenant.

label: Chaplain
summary: Priest serving a chapel, such as a covenant chapel.

label: Chapter House
summary: A small dependent covenant founded at a valuable site far from a covenant's main holding, tending to agitate for independence from its motherhouse.

label: Chapter of Canons (Church Boon)
summary: Minor Church Boon: the priests form a chapter holding benefices.

label: Chapter of Cherbourg
summary: Chapter house of Fengheld near Cherbourg, occupied by a single magus considered a cenobite in Normandy.

label: Character guide
summary: A summary of requirements for designing a magic character type, used instead of a full sheet.

label: CharacterType (Bjornaer Magus)
summary: A magus of House Bjornaer who possesses a heartbeast and belongs to a clan and sept within the ancestor cult.

label: Characteristic
summary: The eight inborn attributes (Intelligence, Perception, Strength, Stamina, Presence, Communication, Dexterity, Quickness) defining a character's potential.

label: Charge
summary: Combining movement with exertion on attack; mounted charges tire the horse instead.

label: Charge of the Angry Winds
summary: An Auram spell whose effect is duplicated by an air elemental power of the same name, adding the elemental's Strength to Ease Factors for acting within the wind.

label: Charged Item
summary: An enchanted item costing no vis that can be used a limited number of times, gaining one charge per five points the Lab Total exceeds the effect level.

label: Charger
summary: A war horse from the Book of Mundane Beasts used as Aeolus's base.

label: Chariot Mysteries
summary: Ancient mystical practice inspired by Ezekiel's vision of the divine chariot, seeking communion with angels.

label: Charism
summary: Gift given by God and stamped on the soul; Andru argues the Gift is one.

label: Charisma
summary: Ability appearing in character or covenant library statistics in the Roman Tribunal.

label: Charities
summary: Lands given to the Church in exchange for services such as masses for the donor; increasingly offered to nunneries.

label: Charity
summary: Theological virtue of complete love of God; at True Faith 5 the character radiates an Empyreal aura.

label: Charlemagne
summary: The Frankish ruler who attempted (and failed) to dig a canal linking the Main and Danube, and whose late-eighth-century monetary reforms fixed the pound-of-silver system used in Mythic Europe in 1220.

label: Charlemagne's Empire
summary: The historical Frankish empire whose civilizing forces helped wipe out the Gothic witch-cult tradition.

label: Charlemagne's Loaf
summary: A wondrous loaf of bread whose smallest nibble grants the eater incredible courage, giving a +3 on all Bravery rolls (Craft Level 17).

label: Charlemagne's Talisman
summary: Coronation relic in Reims believed to contain a fragment of the True Cross.

label: Charles III
summary: French king who made an accord with Rollo in 911.

label: Charles II the Bald
summary: Successor of Louis defeated by Nominoé.

label: Charles IV
summary: Holy Roman Emperor who wrote of a haunting at his castle in Prague.

label: Charles Martel
summary: The Frankish King who repulsed the Moorish army at the Battle of Tours in 732, the historical event that destroyed Flambeau's family estate.

label: Charles of Anjou
summary: French count crowned King of Sicily in 1266, bringing Windgraven Magi into Italy.

label: Charles the Bald
summary: Carolingian king who endowed Laon and built the palace at Compiègne.

label: Charles the Fat
summary: Emperor who reunited Charlemagne's empire in 881, deposed 887.

label: Charles the Simple
summary: King of the Franks from 898, driven out by Robert.

label: Charlotte filia Lupina
summary: Timid Merinita maga, daughter of a goose maiden, with latent skinchanging ability.

label: Charm
summary: Casting aids made by magi who study Faerie Magic that identify a magical effect through sympathetic magic; they may be objects, performances, or pronouncements, and can boost Penetration and Casting Totals.

label: Charm (Ability)
summary: Ability referenced in faerie rules and statistics.

label: Charm Against Capriciousness
summary: TuFa 20 charm treating stress rolls for Great Weapon as simple rolls.

label: Charm Against Magic
summary: Rego Vim spell enchanted into amulets of Imanitosi and Steris.

label: Charm against Putrefaction
summary: A Creo Corpus spell (Level 10) that prevents decay of a human corpse or severed body part; used by necromancers to preserve revived corpses.

label: Charm Against the Hex
summary: TuMa 10 charm raising Hex Ease Factor by +9.

label: Charm Magic
summary: A Minor Folk Inner Mystery (Virtue) allowing a Merinita to incorporate charms into her spells, granting Casting Total and Penetration bonuses through sympathetic magic.

label: Charm Magician
summary: Major Supernatural Flaw: the learned magician may not create amulets, only chartae.

label: Charm of Alacritous Fortune Against Earth
aliases: Charm of Alacritous Fortune Against Earth
summary: TuMa 10 charm adding +4 Defense vs magical earth attacks.

label: Charm of Protection Against Achilles' Bane
aliases: Charm of Protection Against Achilles' Bane
summary: TuSa 5 charm adding +8 Soak vs non-magical arrows; versions for other weapons.

label: Charm of Protection Against the Attacks of Semita Errabunda
aliases: Charm of Protection Against the Attacks of Semita Errabunda
summary: TuSa 15 charm giving +4 Defense vs nonmagical attacks by Semita Errabunda residents.

label: Charm of Protection Against the Faerie
aliases: Charm of Protection Against the Faerie
Charm of Protection against the Infernal
summary: VuMa general charm warding against Faerie creatures of lower Might; versions for other realms.

label: Charm of Quickness
summary: SuFa 20 charm improving luck with Quickness; exists for each Characteristic.

label: Charm of Warding Against Unwanted Pests
aliases: Charm of Warding Against Unwanted Pests
summary: TuSa 5 charm keeping pests away from the recipient.

label: Charm Offensive
summary: Andru's campaign to have the Church declare Hermetic magic enchantment rather than sorcery.

label: Charmed Life
summary: Virtue Sabastien may have and Andru has, which Andru wrongly attributes to his relic of Cyrian.

label: Charon
summary: Ferryman on the River Styx, after whom the Charon certamen trick is named.

label: Charon (certamen trick)
summary: Trick allowing two spells on an opponent at certamen's end.

label: Charta for Healing a Broken Limb
aliases: Charta for Healing a Broken Limb
summary: SuSa 4 charta giving +6 to Recovery rolls for a broken limb.

label: Chartae
summary: Single-use learned magician device created quickly, whose single charge is expended upon creation.

label: Charter Demon
summary: A typical demon with Infernal Might 15 (Mentem) that offers services such as disease relief or merchant bonuses to townsfolk in exchange for tithes or worship under a demonic charter.

label: Charter of the Forest
summary: A charter issued in 1217 alongside the Magna Carta reissue, restricting the king's forest rights and limiting forest officials from imposing penalties of life or limb.

label: Charter Strength
summary: Optional rule scoring each side's legal position in a charter (Intelligence + Civil and Canon Law + stress die).

label: Chase
summary: Land reserved for a lord's hunting; Nidi declares its key sites a chase to deter trespass and prevent the Dominion from spreading.

label: Chasidim
summary: German Jewish mystics who developed a cultural and religious renaissance after the First Crusade, emphasizing asceticism, martyrdom, and lifelong penitence.

label: Chassenon
summary: Roman city ruins with baths whose healing water has Creo vis.

label: Chaste
summary: Personality Flaw suitable for characters affected by vows.

label: Chastise the Disobedient
summary: Bordelon's Power making her switch strikes double Wound Penalties.

label: Chastise the Sinful
summary: Kolazonta's plague power.

label: Chateau Galliard
summary: Great Angevin castle fallen in 1204.

label: Chaudepysse
summary: A Minor Choleric Disease contracted from unclean women, notoriously difficult to cure, causing painful urination.

label: Chausses
summary: Mail leggings.

label: Chavin of Tytalus
summary: A magus of House Tytalus whose spells all promote or advocate war or violence per his sigil; his version of Voice of the Lake makes the lake sound arrogant.

label: Chearlach
summary: Gruagach used in the newid gornest example, taking bird form to escape Brude's lava.

label: Chearlach Mac Caolin
summary: Young gruagach once of the covenant of Eilean Beg, abducted and trained by Brude Deathless, bound by a geas to train a student before his forty-ninth year.

label: Cheating the Reaper
summary: A Creo Corpus ritual (Level 30) that resolves a major or lesser aging crisis; each application causes Warping.

label: Chef
summary: Folk magician using Free Expression, Knack and Craft Lesser Charm to cook magical food.

label: Cheiron
summary: A centaur who mentored Herakles and became the constellation Centaurus; a powerful astrological spirit aligned to Magic.

label: Chelm
summary: Mythical city of fools of Jewish folklore.

label: Cherbourg
summary: Town on the Cotentin near the ruined covenant Pagus, with a Fengheld chapterhouse.

label: Cherem
summary: Civic ostracism excommunication under Halakha.

label: Cherubim
summary: Angels with flaming swords guarding the entrances to Eden.

label: Cheshire
summary: One of the two English palatinates, where the Earl of Chester holds all the authority of the king.

label: Chess
summary: Game with Old, Prima and Expedition variants popular among Tremere.

label: Chess System
summary: Decimal vis currency (pawn, rook, queen) invented by the Tremere.

label: Chessed
summary: Sefirah meaning 'Love', level 7 on the Tree of Life; understood by a kabbalist with Kabbalah 7.

label: Chester
summary: A small walled city and capital of the palatine county of Cheshire where the earl of Chester is the highest authority, with a leather trade and a pagan shrine of Minerva carved into nearby rock.

label: Chevalier De Panne
summary: Knight who fought Pan Caudarax and lived.

label: Chevauchee
summary: Tactic of ravaging enemy territory; returning inhabitants suffer a –2 Living Conditions modifier and extreme cases may develop a Malevolent Infernal aura.

label: Cheviot Hills
summary: Hills along the Tyne where the covenant of Horsingas is located.

label: Chewstoke
summary: Village west of Stanton Drew below Pagan's Hill.

label: Child Killers
summary: Common faeries of folklore that kill children.

label: Child Stealers
summary: Faeries that steal children.

label: Child Virtues and Flaws
summary: New type of Virtue and Flaw reflecting childhood traits that must be exchanged by adulthood.

label: Childbed Fever
summary: A Major Sanguine Disease afflicting women who have just given birth, caused by the childbed fever demon.

label: Childbed Fever Demon
summary: A demon with Might 10 (Corpus) that attempts to enter a woman's body during birth, causing fever and rotting of the reproductive organs; its magical attack can be resisted with Magic Resistance.

label: Childebert
summary: Son of Clovis buried at St. Denis.

label: Childebert I
summary: Son and successor of Clovis who died childless in 558.

label: Childeric
summary: Son of Merovech, king of the Salian Franks who besieged Paris in 464.

label: Childeric III
summary: Last Merovingian king, shorn and retired to a monastery.

label: Childermas
summary: December 28th, when ghosts of dead apprentices are said to haunt their masters.

label: Children of Danu
summary: Celtic gods who drove the Fomoire beyond the Ninth Wave.

label: Children of Hermes
summary: Messianic mystery cult led by Hermes the Blessed One, who claims apotheosis; proselytizing and obsessed with conspiracies in the Order.

label: Children of Hermes Lore
summary: Organization Lore taught to new Children of Hermes.

label: Children of Odin
summary: A new, secretive Mystery Cult led by Queen Skuld claiming the heritage of Viking magic and seeking to restore Normandy to Norman rule.

label: Children's Crusade
summary: 1212 crusade started by a shepherd boy from Châteaudun.

label: Childwrite
summary: Tax on unmarried pregnancy, often absorbed into leywrite.

label: Chill Touch
summary: Water elemental power extracting heat for +10 damage.

label: Chilperic
summary: Frankish king buried in Tournai.

label: Chilperic I
summary: Son of Chlotar, king who died in 584.

label: Chimera
summary: A noble hybrid inner heartbeast combining features of two mundane creatures (such as a griffin, hippogriff, or unicorn), produced by the Mystery of the Chimera.

label: Chinon
summary: Town on the River Vienne with a great castle built by Henry II; given to Philip II by the Treaty of Chinon.

label: Chiron
summary: The figure who warned Jason that the Argonauts would be lost unless Orpheus accompanied them, a prophecy fulfilled at the sirens' island.

label: Chirurgeon
summary: A practitioner of chirurgy (surgery, bone-setting, phlebotomy, cautery, midwifery), considered a craft; includes barber-surgeons who assist medici in therapeutic procedures.

label: Chirurgy
summary: A healing Ability practiced by chirurgeons; the Surgical Empiricus Flaw restricts the character to a single specialization, halving the score for other applications.

label: Chivalrous Combat
summary: Example player-defined Pretense combining sword and lance use for a faerie knight.

label: Chloe
summary: Valnastium's chief minstrel, a composer of ethereal choral prayers that are magical when performed by others; possibly a unique Natural Magician.

label: Chloe filia Andru
summary: Lartan Jerbiton maga at Valnastium.

label: Chlotar
summary: Son of Clovis under whom Soissons was the Frankish capital.

label: Chlotar II
summary: Chlotar 'the Grand', reunited the Frankish kingdom in 613.

label: Chnoubis the Serpent
summary: A lion-headed serpent Daimon (Magic Might 30, Mentem) summoned for his abilities to scry and ferret out secrets, claiming to be a native of the Nile.

label: Chochmah
summary: Sefirah meaning 'Wisdom', level 9 on the Tree of Life; understood by a kabbalist with Kabbalah 9.

label: Chorazon
summary: Ruined city in the Holy Land where the Antichrist is to be born.

label: Chrétien de Troyes
summary: Author of epic poems about the Knights of the Round Table in which giants appear as brutish villains.

label: Chrétien of Troyes
summary: The most famous trouvère of northern France, whose Arthurian poems concentrate on Arthur and his peers.

label: Chrétien the Roamer
summary: Much-traveled monk seeking to lose Difficult Underlings who fails his pilgrimage by yielding to temptation.

label: Christian Mysticism
summary: Mystical state understood as a form of prayer imparting direct personal knowledge of God, with rules for play.

label: Christianity
summary: One of the three most important Divine religions in Mythic Europe; many magi are Christians and its relics are most common.

label: Christina of Markyate
summary: Noble Anglo-Saxon girl from Huntingdon who vowed virginity and resisted her forced marriage to Burthred.

label: Christmas
summary: Feast of Christ's nativity on December 25, beginning a twelve-day holy season during which realm boundaries blur.

label: Christopher of Romagna
summary: One of the early followers of Francis.

label: Chromatic Flames
summary: A Level 4 alchemical Reagent that, when sprinkled over flames or mixed with fuel, causes them to burn a different hue chosen by the alchemist until extinguished.

label: Chthonic Magus
summary: A magus attuned to both Magical and Infernal auras through Chthonic Magic.

label: Chur
summary: Rhaetian capital, a Roman colony with a bishop.

label: Church Auras
summary: Divine auras radiating from a church altar as far as the bells can be heard, levels 1 to 5.

label: Church Courts
summary: Courts dealing with priests and crimes against God or the Church.

label: Church Deacon
summary: Grog template: a proud deacon who assists the parish priest and reads from the Bible.

label: Church Knowledge
summary: Ability appearing in character or covenant library statistics in the Roman Tribunal.
