summary: A technique of deliberately casting a spell with Penetration Total of 0 so it cannot affect a magus's Magic Resistance, used in tournaments and group spellcasting.

label: Foreign Upbringing
summary: A Minor Personality Flaw marking the character as a foreigner from a remote corner of Mythic Europe with odd customs and a foreign Native Language.

label: Foremen Elves
summary: Four elves who command the worker elves.

label: Forest Cave
summary: Mistress Greta's remote cave with Magic aura 6, lying inside a regio.

label: Forest Law
summary: A separate legal system applying in royal forests, prohibiting hunting, wood-cutting, and fires, enforced by foresters and forest eyres.

label: Forest of Bart
summary: Forest in Anjou where Fontrevrault was founded.

label: Forest of Brix
summary: Forest south of Cherbourg haunted by packs of faerie wolves.

label: Forest of Broceliande
summary: Haunted forest in Brittany where numerous covenants have been founded but none survived.

label: Forest of Cuise
summary: A vast royal hunting forest south of Compiègne stretching to the Ardennes, with no known significant faerie presence.

label: Forest of Fontainebleau
summary: Rocky forest south of Paris with druidic groves, a Faerie regio, and the covenant of Lapis Crudus.

label: Forest of Luchon
summary: Forest at the foot of the Pyrenees in France where gem-faced serpents, children of a vouivre, are found.

label: Forest of Lyons
summary: Remnant forest favored for hunting by Norman nobles; a castle at its heart eliminated its forest spirit.

label: Forest of Shining Stone
summary: A Great Work at Durenmar where Bonisagus's epitome The Art of Magic has been etched into 36 clear crystals each six feet high.

label: Forest of Yvelines
summary: Forest south of Paris.

label: Forest Paths
summary: Mystical paths through the forests of the Rhine Tribunal that a magus may explore; ascending the Glade of the Seven Waterfalls grants deeper understanding of the Forest.

label: Forest Warden
summary: Royal officer inspecting the king's woodland and fining overgathering and illegal clearances.

label: Forester
summary: Lesser office caring for the lord's hunting wood.

label: Forfar
summary: Where the last Mac William was killed.

label: Forfeit Immunity
summary: Loss of legal protection under Hermetic Law, e.g. during Wizard War, when committing a crime, or when intruding in a sanctum.

label: Forge-Companion
summary: A Minor, Social Status Virtue for an unGifted craftsman attached to a Verditius magus and working in his lab, with extra experience for Crafts.

label: Forge of Hephaestus
summary: Sacred forges built by Hephaestus, the three Hermetic ones located at Verdi (Sardinia), Lemnos, and Mount Olympus, serving as Verditius Initiation chambers.

label: Forgery
summary: Ability listed in the Alpine redcap template or Hera's statistics.

label: Forgettable Face
summary: A Minor, General Virtue making a character hard to notice or describe, imposing -3 on rolls to identify him but incompatible with great beauty or charisma.

label: Forgotten God
summary: Hermetic or setting concept referenced in the description of the Mythic Locations sites.

label: Forgotten Gods
summary: Beasts and spirits once worshiped as gods who retreated into the Magic Realm or took living forms to survive the Dominion.

label: Forked Tongue of the Serpent
summary: Neqael's power making the target believe any lie until relating it to someone else.

label: Form and Effect Bonuses
summary: Enchantment bonuses from materials, e.g. Sardinian woods studied by Verdi.

label: (Form) Monstrosity
summary: A Minor Supernatural Flaw, mainly for animal characters, giving a monstrous feature corresponding to a magical Form, from which Muto vis may be extracted.

label: Form of Man
summary: Vessels of Iniquity Power to shapeshift into any human after Form of Wickedness.

label: Form of the Serpent
summary: Aethnici Power to become a snake, lizard or salamander.

label: Form of the (Temperament) Heartbeast
summary: A Muto Animal 20 spell with four temperament versions (sanguine, choleric, melancholic, phlegmatic) that enhances an animal form's humoral correspondences; modeled from Birna's innate abilities.

label: Form of the Zephyr
summary: MuCo(Au) 40 spell transforming the caster into a strong gale wind flying at 50 miles an hour.

label: Form of Wickedness
summary: Vessels of Iniquity variant of Coagulation, a shapeless form of visible sin overwhelming viewers.

label: Form of Woman
summary: Baal-Peor's Power to take a beautiful woman's form.

label: (Form) Resistance
summary: Supernatural Ability for characters with Magic Might, adding to Soak and Magic Resistance against a Form; e.g. Vim, Ignem, Animal, Terram Resistance.

label: Formed Stones
summary: Shaped stones, called lusus naturae, said to be formed by vis plastica, astral conjunctions or other causes; many are Objects of Virtue.

label: Formula
summary: A researched recipe of experimental philosophy, like a Laboratory Text, describing how to make astrological inceptions, alchemical reagents, or pharmaceutical theriacs.

label: Formulaic Magic
summary: A category of Hermetic spell with fixed parameters, distinct from Spontaneous and Ritual magic, affected by Virtues like Boosted and Flexible Formulaic Magic.

label: Formulary
summary: Large, poorly organized collection of hundreds or thousands of charms from which learned magicians may cast directly.

label: Fornax of Tremere
summary: Goliard's filia at Blackthorn, an ugly and rude mature maga rumored to specialize in Rego and Mentem to make people entertain her.

label: Forsaken Duration
summary: Infernal Duration lasting as long as the target is tainted by the Infernal; canceled by repentance; equal to Duration Year.

label: Fortification of the Memory Palace
summary: ReMe General protects the memory palace.

label: Fortitude
summary: Moral (Cardinal) virtue of willingness to take risks against insurmountable danger, helping resist fear.

label: Fortuito filius Circum Perfico
summary: Criamon Seeker who studies diviners and sends predictive letters to be delivered only after disasters.

label: Fortuna
summary: Goddess of luck invoked in Gift charms and the Curse of Fortuna.

label: Fortunam
summary: Learned-magician Form; Fortunam charms influence luck and actions of others.

label: Fortunata of Jerbiton
summary: A powerful eleventh-century spirit master of House Jerbiton who defeated many non-Hermetic enemies but was forced into exile and disappeared into Final Twilight after 1120.

label: Fortunatas of Jerbiton
summary: One of the two heads of Vardian's Tomb.

label: Fortunatus of Jerbiton
summary: A magus of House Jerbiton whose Creo Imaginem illusions often have a small religious icon worked into their structure due to how he invents his spells.

label: Fortune Favors the Bold
summary: SuFa 5 charm giving +2 to luck-based rolls.

label: Forum Boarium
summary: Place in Rome near Portunes's temple.

label: Forum (Temple of Mercury)
summary: A large open-roofed marble-flagged meeting area and market place in the temple town, with a raised pulpit at its northern end.

label: Fosterage
summary: Covenant Hook: magi educate a young noble, potentially spreading acceptance of Hermetic magic; also a way to seal supernatural alliances.

label: Fostered Apprentice
summary: Minor Story Flaw: the character was fostered and owes favors to the fostering magus and a fellow apprentice.

label: Fougères
summary: Frontier castle town.

label: Foul Weather made Fair
summary: Dindyméné's power cancelling Breath of the Angry Goddess or stopping storms.

label: Foundation Charm
summary: Charm placed in a hall's walls or foundations to protect the building, set by a hedge witch or via traditional sacrifice; may anchor a faerie guardian spirit.

label: Founding of the Order
summary: The historical establishment of the Order of Hermes, predating which some traditions held antipathies against House Diedne.

label: Foundling Child
summary: Sample seven-year-old Gifted orphan apprentice with a knack for books and an inherited Flexible Formulaic Magic.

label: Fountain of Barenton
summary: Fountain that yields Vim vis.

label: Fountain of Fair Waters
summary: Spring at the center of a Faerie regio (aura 6) in Fontainebleau, home of a nymph and white stag.

label: Fountain of St. Reina
summary: Divine-aura curative fountain at Mont Auxois.

label: Fountain of Youth
summary: A magical fountain deep in the forest sought by Alexander of Jerbiton; drinking from it infused his blood with the power of youth, enhancing his longevity rituals.

label: Fountains Abbey
summary: A great Cistercian abbey in Yorkshire, founded in 1132 by monks from York and a daughter house of Clairvaux, motherhouse of a wide filiation.

label: Four Estates
summary: Division of Mythic Europe into those who pray, rule and toil (Church, nobility, peasants/townsfolk), to which the Order would add a fourth.

label: Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse
summary: Biblical figures that may roam Mythic Europe in an apocalyptic saga.

label: Four Humors
summary: Choleric, phlegmatic, sanguine and melancholic humors corresponding to the four elements and the signs.

label: Four Worlds
summary: Kabbalistic scheme of four stages of emanation from the Divine: Atzilut, Beriyah, Yetzirah, Asiyah.

label: Fourth Crusade
summary: A late-12th-century crusade for which the Venetians built a fleet; unable to pay, the Crusaders were forced to sack Constantinople in 1204, and many cycled-out Venetian warships later mysteriously disappeared.

label: Fourth Estate
summary: Proposed end state in which the Order of Hermes becomes a recognized estate of society alongside clergy, nobility and commoners, with legal rights and obligations.

label: Fourth Lateran Council
summary: A Church council of 1215 that forbade clergy from cautery or surgical incision and obliged physicians to require patients to summon a confessor before treatment.

label: Foutins
summary: Large clan of local roustabouts, Iasper's mundane family.

label: Fox
summary: Cunning prey that gives good sport but little prestige.

label: Fox of Virtue
summary: A trickster fox that feigns death to lure carrion birds.

label: Fragile Constitution
summary: A Minor General Flaw making the character sickly with a -3 penalty on rolls to recover from wounds and diseases.

label: Fragments of the True Cross
summary: Common relics with 1 Faith Point and Divine Might 10.

label: Frail
summary: A Minor General Flaw making the character weak of build with a -3 penalty to Soak score.

label: Framlingham
summary: Castle with 13 mural towers.

label: François
summary: Elderly, powerful Larta blacksmith of the Village of the Vale whose smithy is intensely magical and whose kin serve as grogs across the Order.

label: France
summary: A kingdom of Mythic Europe whose king the king of England owes fealty for mainland possessions; home to Cluny, the Champagne fairs, and Laon, and which can be saved from demons in a saga.

label: Francis' Cave
summary: Cave high in a valley near Assisi where Francis meditated; site of Meditation and Purity Initiations.

label: Franciscan
summary: One of the two major new mendicant friar orders of the early thirteenth century, whose members take vows of poverty, chastity, and obedience and travel preaching.

label: Franciscan Friar
summary: Grog template for a young mendicant friar.

label: Franciscan Nun
summary: Grog template for a Poor Sister with Lesser Purifying Touch.

label: Franciscan Order
summary: A mendicant order of friars founded in Italy in 1209, found preaching in market places and public squares, which had not yet spread beyond Italy and France.

label: Franciscan Teacher
summary: Companion template: an indebted university master who became a Franciscan and seeks to convert pagans and the Order of Hermes.

label: Francisco
summary: Cowardly Shadow Senator.

label: Francois filius Alban
summary: Lartan Jerbiton magus at Valnastium.

label: Franconia
summary: A large and important region of the Rhine Tribunal containing some of the greatest German cities, with no single ruler; land shared between emperor and church.

label: Francs-mitoux
summary: A court of Parisian argotiers who feign fainting fits in public.

label: Frangarach
summary: Manannan's sword, the Answerer, which always kills his opponent.

label: Frangipane Family
summary: Roman family using the Colosseum as a fortress.

label: Frankfurt
summary: A trading city founded by Charlemagne at the 'Ford of the Franks' on the River Main, home to about 10,000 citizens and host of imperial elections.

label: Franks
summary: Historical Germanic people whose history, by Gregory of Tours, is a cited period source.

label: Franz
summary: A monk who investigated the Cursewood, was scared off, and hid a copy of De Operationes Daemonum Dialogos.

label: Frater
summary: Term meaning brother, used for a fellow male taught Hermetic magic by the apprentice's master; soror for a female.

label: Fraternity of Samos Lore
summary: Organization Lore of the Fraternity.

label: Frau Holle
summary: A modest Holzfrau who in the nine days before Walpurgis Night travels the land on a rickety wagon, pursued by the Wild Hunt, before ascending the Brocken and revealing herself as the goddess Walpurga.

label: Frau Wacholder
summary: A wood-wife who is the genius of the juniper tree, invoked to make thieves give up their booty.

label: Frau Wode
summary: The female leader of a Wild Hunt that haunts the Elbe river, accompanied by shadowy boatmen carrying invisible passengers.

label: Fredegisa the Quaesitor
summary: A reforming idealist quaesitor at Schola Pythagoranis, a brilliant young student of all laws who devises new structures of Hermetic law.

label: Fredegund
summary: Wife of Chilperic I and regent for Chlotar II.

label: Frederick Barbarossa
summary: The emperor who in 1190 granted Bolognese scholars freedom of movement throughout the Holy Roman Empire and safe residences, the root of universities' political autonomy.

label: Frederick of Harco
summary: One of Harco's three young Redcaps.

label: Frederico
summary: Parens of Gunther of the Cave.

label: Free Choice
summary: Flaw a bacheler knight may take instead of Oath of Fealty.

label: Free Expression
summary: A Minor Virtue prized by artistic Jerbiton magi; can be granted or doubled by a muse and grants familiarity bonuses with depicted objects.

label: Free House Virtue
summary: House Virtue that an apprentice studying long enough with his parens may acquire.

label: Free Peasant
summary: Peasants who are personally free; less than ten percent of most manors' population, most common on royal manors, assarts and new towns.

label: Free Study
summary: A Minor, Hermetic Virtue adding +3 to Source Quality when studying from raw vis.

label: Free the Devil's Servant
summary: Malachi's Power that frees a trapped demon after sunset until dawn.

label: Freedom of Movement
summary: A common automaton power (base effect 25, Mentem requisite) letting the automaton walk toward areas pointed out to it.

label: Freeing the Striding Tree
summary: A Rego Herbam spell (Level 30) like Lord of the Trees but enabling the tree to walk half as fast as a human; a botched Concentration roll causes the tree to attack the caster.

label: Freiberg
summary: The biggest of the mining towns in the Ore Mountains, founded in 1186 after silver and tin were discovered.

label: Freiburg
summary: The largest settlement around the Black Forest, founded in 1120 by Conrad Zähringen, lying in the valley of the River Dreisam with a cathedral under construction.

label: Freiceadanan
summary: Covenant guards (grogs); at Crun Clach ten who hunt the Prince's monsters, at Mac Gruagach the entire clan.

label: Freiherr
summary: German noble with an allodial holding, sometimes translated as baron.

label: French
summary: Living Language of most of the Tribunal (Langues d'Oil), with dialects Orleanais, Norman, Picard, Walloon, Champenois, Bourguignon, Lorrain, Poitevin.

label: French Lore
summary: Ability appearing in character or covenant library statistics in this text.

label: Freshly Sprung
summary: Minor Supernatural Flaw subtracting 50 experience points from Pretense pool.

label: Freya
summary: Norse goddess of love, marriage and fertility, for whom the first aett is named.

label: Freya's Aett
summary: The first aett of the Elder Futhark, named after the goddess Freya, containing Fehu through Wunjo.

label: Fria
summary: The goddess worshiped by the old Germanic tribes alongside Woden, Thunor, and Tius.

label: Friar
summary: Mendicant religious; friar characters take the Mendicant Friar Virtue.

label: Fribourg
summary: Town founded in 1157 by Berthold IV.

label: Friderich Invigilor
summary: The filius of Drogo Invigilor, similarly investigated by House Guernicus for his association with the Salian dynasty.

label: Friendly Gruagach Collective
summary: Major Covenant Boon in which the covenant controls a nearby gruagach collective that trades vis and gives aid.

label: Friesland
summary: A broad, flat, swampy territory bordering the North Sea, sparsely populated and home to the independent Friesian people and the Friesian Islands.

label: Frighten
summary: Sluagh power (PeMe 30) that drives a target insane with terror.

label: Frightful Presence
summary: A Minor, Supernatural Virtue letting a character instill dread or awe, forcing witnesses to make Brave Personality rolls.

label: Frisia
summary: Saxon-descended land where Sin-Eating is common.

label: Friuli of Quaesitor
summary: Full member of Magvillus and Transitionalist.

label: Frog Prince
summary: Fairy-tale figure who serves the princess, becomes a moral test, needs to be helped, and grants rewards.

label: From Hill to Hollow
summary: Loamwalker power to move instantly between trees within sight.

label: From Nag to Charger
summary: Aeolus's power (MuAn 15) to change himself into any kind of horse.

label: From This Line Descended
summary: InCo 30 spell revealing whether the target of an Arcane Connection descends from a given bloodline and how strong that blood is.

label: Frost Giant
summary: Giants dwelling on an icy peak that forms a tether.

label: Frost Giants
summary: Norse giants associated with Aquam that have Greater Immunity to cold.

label: Frosty Breath of the Spoken Lie
aliases: Frosty Breath of the Spoken Lie
summary: An Intellego Mentem spell (Level 20) that makes a target exhale misty breath with each spoken lie; House Guernicus brought it to the Order and it is essential to Quaesitors.

label: Frustration Week
summary: Late April when many Wizard's Wars begin; magi exchange gifts and vis treaties are delivered.

label: Fudarus
summary: The domus magna of House Tytalus, where the memory of Kalliste is ritually cursed each midwinter; it is currently occupied by both rival Primi and maintains an immense spy network.

label: Fuero
summary: Iberian town charter that sets out militia obligations, exemptions and the equipment required of caballeros.

label: Fugitive Stone
summary: Roaming mooring stone, Magic Might 10, chained in Artakia, longing for Jason.

label: Fulda
summary: An important pilgrimage site and home to a wealthy monastery, burial place of the martyred English monk St. Boniface.

label: Fulk Nerra
summary: Count of Anjou 987-1040, founder of Ronceray abbey.

label: Fulmen of Guernicus
summary: Quaesitor who disseminated a convict's mystery secrets, lost his familiar as punishment, and joined House Jerbiton as an advocate.

label: Fulmonious
summary: A magus of House Tytalus who, with Schwall of Bjornaer, founded the covenant of Rheinstein in the Rhine Gorge in 1123 AD.

label: Fumigant of Minor Demons
summary: PeVi General Boundary ritual, a variant of Demon's Eternal Oblivion, destroying minor infernal spirits on the island.

label: Furies
summary: Order of demons of wrath including Architectus, Bael, the Demons of the Fifth Trump, dibbukim and Sabaoth; led by Abaddon.

label: Furioso
summary: A Sorcerous Musician who lacks Subtle Magic, used as a contrasting example to Orlando in Performance Magic.

label: Furious Attacks
summary: Attacks usable against multiple opponents in a round without penalty.

label: Furled Pad
summary: Unfurled pad used as mooring point.

label: Furlong
summary: Long rectangular section of a field whose crop is chosen by the manor court.

label: Fury
summary: A Major Story Flaw in which a violent temper overwhelms the character, sending him into uncontrollable rage.

label: Fury of the Charging Bull
summary: A ReAn 20 spell that enrages a target animal (up to Size +3), sometimes used by School of Vilano followers to make animals attack enemies, though unpredictably.

label: Fylgja
summary: Guardian spirit that warns a galdrakona of approaching danger.

label: Gérard of Ridefort
summary: Grand Master (1185-1189).

label: Gâvre Forest
summary: Forest near Blain in which a leper hospital is hidden.

label: Gaap
summary: A demon of the False Gods who claims to be a great president and mighty prince of Hell commanding 66 legions; actually ineffectual but highly persuasive and knowledgeable of Hell's intrigues.

label: Gabai
summary: A Minor Social Status Flaw marking the character as the local Jewish tax collector appointed by the community council, with a negative Tax Collector Reputation.

label: Gabricon
summary: Maker of Gabricon's Doormat of Welcoming.

label: Gabricon's Doormat of Welcoming
summary: Enchanted doormat that senses and announces a visitor's name, and would reveal a demon's True Name.

label: Gabriel, the Archangel of Prophecy
summary: A Divine creature (Might 100, Mentem), the chief messenger of God known for teaching the prophet Daniel, announcing Christ's incarnation to Mary, and bringing the Qur'an to Muhammad.

label: Gadiel
summary: Seraph whose name wards devils.

label: Gaelic
summary: Predominant language of the Highlands brought by the Scotti from Ireland.

label: Gaia
summary: Primordial earth goddess, mother of Dindyméné.

label: Galatea
summary: Maga of House Guernicus from Antagonists who may watch the covenant for crimes.

label: Galconer
summary: Faerie whose statistics are used for the human form of seducing kelpies.

label: Galdor magic
summary: Icelandic spirit-invoking magic of the galdramen, possibly integrated into Hermetic Theory.

label: Galdrakona
summary: Female galdor practitioner.

label: Galdraman
summary: Icelandic magician who works galdor magic by bargaining with and summoning spirits.

label: Galdramen hreppur
summary: Association of Icelandic galdramen led by Biorn Egilsson, targeted by the crusade and possibly integrated into the Order.

label: Galen
summary: The ancient authority on medicine since whom chirurgy has held a less prestigious position; quoted on the distinction between knowledge by experience and by reason.

label: Galgilliel
summary: Authority overseeing the sun, Divine Might 70.

label: Galizur
summary: Ruler of Raqia.

label: Gallery
summary: A Minor laboratory Structure Virtue: an interior gallery or platform lets someone view the whole lab without disturbing it (+1 Safety, +1 Aesthetics, +1 Teaching).

label: Galley
summary: An oar-propelled single-masted vessel popular with Italian maritime powers and Byzantine states, designed to ram enemies and discourage piracy.

label: Galli
summary: A sect of nature worshippers once associated with the wild lands beyond the Roman Empire, later integrated into the Cult of Diana, said to be the origin of a True Merinitae Initiation Script.

label: Gallo-Roman Tower of Tours
summary: Windowless Roman brick tower west of Tours with Magic aura 1 at base and 5 at top.

label: Galloglaich
summary: Heavy infantry of the Danish islanders who wear cotte or chain hauberk and carry two-handed axes; a character template.

label: Galloglaichs
summary: Orcadian mercenaries fighting in chain mail with two-handed axes.

label: Galloway
summary: Region where the monk wandered before finding the covenant.

label: Gallowglaigh
summary: Grog template: a Hebridean mercenary trained to attack at a run in heavy chain armor, veteran of Irish wars.

label: Gallows Wood
summary: Wood where Svetlana harvested vis.

label: Gambeson
summary: Garment of padded material worn over, under or instead of armor; also aketon or arming jacket.

label: Ganelon
summary: A leading magus of the Ash Gild who declared Wizard War on Aschlaranda and Schadrit and pursued them into the Black Forest, never to be heard from again.

label: Gang Leader
summary: Virtue for leading a group, e.g. mortal shinty players.

label: Gang Member
summary: Grog vocation: a northern Italian city gang youth now serving magi as a warrior.

label: Gang Member (Virtue)
summary: Virtue appearing in a Roman Tribunal vocation template.

label: Gangrene
summary: A Minor Sanguine Disease in which evil spirits in an improperly cleaned wound putrefy the blood; common after a botched Wound Recovery roll.

label: Gar
summary: Additional Anglo-Saxon Futhorc rune meaning "Spear", with no Elder Futhark equivalent.

label: Garden of Eden
summary: Often equated with the Earthly Paradise; optionally lies within it in a Celestial regio of level 10, guarded by cherubim.

label: Garden of Gethsemane
summary: Where Camuel and Gabriel visited Jesus.

label: Gardens of Valnastium
summary: Gardens laid out by Jerbiton with snails, dormice, bees, magical plants and funerary monuments.

label: Gargantua
summary: Giant credited with throwing the Pierres de Niton and digging Lac Léman.

label: Gargouille
summary: Scaled magical beast from the Seine defeated in the seventh century by St. Romanus with the sign of the cross.

label: Garland of Prosperous Harvests
summary: A pole with a wreath enchanted to grow plants rapidly and nourish orchards.

label: Garotillo
summary: A Serious Choleric Disease from excessive exercise inflaming the choler; its second stage spreads to the windpipe causing suffocation.

label: Garrinchus
summary: A newly apprenticed magus of House Ex Miscellanea at Fengheld's Rheingasse chapter, companion of Wilhelm Weiss and a member of the Apple Gild; his master was an expert in physick.

label: Garron
summary: The small, surefooted Highland pony used to haul loads rather than for riding or war.

label: Garus
summary: The current Primus of House Flambeau in 1220, an aging former soldier-of-fortune and tournament champion who leads the milites and authored the Code of Garus.

label: Garvil
summary: Leader of Postestas who speaks of preserving order in the Tribunal.

label: Gascony
summary: A region of southwestern France, the probable birthplace of Flambeau the Founder around 715 AD.

label: Gate of Countless Vistas
summary: A stone arched doorway enchanted for instant transport to connected locations, keyed to individual users.

label: Gate of Eurydice
summary: Abyss beneath Coeris through which Orpheus entered the underworld; focus of Tremere funeral practice, possibly a regio.

label: Gate of Paradise
summary: Golden jeweled gate at the end of the Bridge to Paradise where angels heal and clothe visitors.

label: Gate spirit
summary: Spirit of Vindolanda's gateway that can swallow the gatestone to seal off Scartaris.

label: Gatehouse Keep
summary: Large building serving as gatehouse and keep.

label: Gates of Hell
summary: The entrance to Hell, guarded and rated as an Infernal aura of 9; some regiones are said to reach them.

label: Gatestone
summary: Stone of Vindolanda's gateway that the gate spirit can swallow to seal the passage.

label: Gateway
summary: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Virtue: the lab sits at a supernatural gateway such as a regio entrance, faerie realm, or Mercere Portal.

label: Gathas
summary: Divine hymns of Zoroaster revealing Ahura Mazda.

label: Gather the Essence of the Beast
aliases: Gather the Essence of the Beast
summary: A Touch-range, Momentary Vim spell that concentrates the raw vis in a corpse into one removable part, letting a magus gather vis without carrying entire corpses.

label: Gathering of the Stormy Might
summary: A Rego Auram spell (Level 40) like Clouds of Thunderous Might but producing a larger storm that can cover the entire visible sky.

label: Gathering of Twelve Years
summary: A periodic gathering of House Bjornaer (the Swan Clan performs a special ritual role at it); held in 1227 and figures in the Crintera Schism as each rival faction holds its own.

label: Gaudy
summary: A Free laboratory Outfittings Flaw: the lab's decoration is tasteless and excessive (+1 Upkeep, -1 Aesthetics, +1 Imaginem).

label: Gauls
summary: Ancient inhabitants of the region who revered the boar and sacrificed to spirits and faeries.

label: The Gauntlet
summary: The final test of apprenticeship, after which an apprentice becomes a full magus of the Order.

label: Gautier d'Arras
summary: Famous 12th-century trouvère of Arras, author of Eracle.

label: Gavi
summary: A dibbuk, the ghost of a greedy Jewish merchant, who possesses victims and forces them into mad acts of charity.

label: Gavrinis
summary: Tumulus gateway to Faerie.

label: Gawain
summary: Arthurian knight who beheads the Green Knight.

label: Gaze of Death
summary: A Corpus power of the basilisk Sordus (8 points) that inflicts an incapacitating wound on anyone his gaze rests upon.

label: Gaze of Gray Years

summary: The tree that holds the world together, climbed by taltós in vision quests to reach other worlds.

summary: Cult that came to Italy c. 700 B.C.

summary: Possible location of Bonisagus's lost books.

summary: Local role of Children of Hermes member collecting vis dues.

summary: Supplement with more information on Falke.

summary: Gulf.

summary: One of Henry II's constables who deprived St. Edmund of his rights; defeated in a 1163 trial by combat after seeing the vengeful vision of St. Edmund, he became a monk at Reading.

label: Henry of Lausanne
summary: Cluniac monk expelled for teaching Petrobrusian views; his Henrician heresy spread among Cluniac houses.

label: Henry of Saltrey
summary: Man who heard the knight Owein's tale and told it to Marie of France.

label: Henry the Fowler
summary: Duke of the Saxons who received the German crown in 919 and defeated the Magyar hordes at Riade in 933.

label: Henry the Lion
summary: The greatest Welf ruler in living memory, duke of both Saxony and Bavaria, stripped of most estates by Frederick Barbarossa; he beautified Brunswick.

label: Henry the Young King
summary: Son of Henry II, who took five hundred knights to Lagny-sur-Marne in 1179 and was tutored by William Marshal.

label: Henry V
summary: An emperor who deposed his father Henry IV, later sought his posthumous absolution, and was tormented on his deathbed by his betrayed father's apparition.

label: Henry VI
summary: An emperor who imprisoned Richard the Lionheart at Burg Trifels in 1193.

label: Heorot
summary: A covenant recently founded on Zealand to discover more about the wizards of the North; closely allied to Oculus Septentrionalis and in conflict with the martial Waddenzee.

label: Hephaestion
summary: An example Verditius magus, five years out of apprenticeship, used to illustrate enchanting casting tools for the spell The Crystal Dart.

label: Hephaestus
summary: The lame Greek god of smiths and divine artificer, founder of the Cult of Hephaestus, who built sacred forges and crafted famous magical items for the gods.

label: Hera
summary: Greek goddess and parthenogenetic mother of Hephaestus, who retrieved him to Olympus and was tortured by Zeus in a mechanized chair.

summary: Galena key ring whose keys open every lock in the Cave.

label: Hera's Gloves
summary: Pale gray leather magical gloves letting Hera handle material objects.

label: Heracles
summary: Legendary hero the Cult of Heroes believes descended from the gods and can be reborn.

label: Heraclitus
summary: Greek philosopher cited for conceptions of evil inherent in matter.

label: Herakles
summary: Hero said to have killed the lindworm near Klagenfurt.

label: Herald
summary: Tournament official who publicizes events, knows knights' devices, provides commentary and adjudicates.

label: Herbalism

label: Herbalism (Virtue)
summary: A Minor General Virtue granting skill in folk remedies and natural magic via the unique Herbalism Ability, plus 50 experience points and the ability to make theriacs and ligatures.

label: Herbam
summary: Form governing plants and products of plants.

label: Herbam province
summary: The Herbam-aligned province of the Twilight Void: growing plants seen brightly with seasonal colors and lush aroma.

label: Herbs of Virtue
summary: Plants that naturally contain vis and can be Enriched into charms that grant Virtues or powers.

label: Herbwife
summary: The poor man's answer to the apothecary; usually a woman who maintains a village's health with preserved garden products and often acts as local midwife.

label: Hercinia
summary: Creature suggested as an Ignem familiar.

label: Hercinia of Virtue
summary: A bird of the forests of southern Germany whose glowing feathers light travelers' paths.

label: Herculaneum
summary: Ancient ruins destroyed (with Pompeii) by a volcanic eruption, traditionally used as the strife-saturated investiture site for the Station of Blood and Bronze on the Path of Strife.

label: Hercules
summary: A god and hero of legendary strength, identified by the Romans with the Gaulish Ogmios and worshiped as protector of the magical springs at the Sanctuary of Hercules.

label: Hercynian Forest
summary: The vast primeval forest of Germany described by Caesar and Pliny; its single powerful spirit was fragmented by the Cult of Mercury and St. Boniface into many genii loci.

label: Hercynius
summary: A Bonisagus magus whose lineage, the Hercynian magi of the Waldherz chapter, maintained harmony with the Black Forest fae before being exiled and eradicated during the Schism War.

label: Hereditary priesthood of the dead god

summary: Pre-Hermetic priests who guarded the 'dead god' skeleton at Sinews of Knowledge and were exterminated during the Sundering.

label: Heretics
summary: Major Church Hook: priests with heretical beliefs.

label: Heriodas
summary: Faerie leader of processions of the dead, collecting the dead and leading them to pagan underworlds.

label: Heriot
summary: Death duty owed when a household head dies, often the peasant's best beast.

label: Herlichinus
summary: Demon jester in fool's motley who leads the best-known Infernal procession of punished souls.

label: Hermann

label: Hermas
summary: Narrator of the Shepherd of Hermas who has a vision of the Church as an aged lady.

label: Hermes Cord
summary: Spirit familiar cord corresponding to the golden cord, also adding to Enigmatic Wisdom rolls.

label: Hermes History
summary: Ability appearing in character or covenant library statistics in the Roman Tribunal.

label: Hermes Mercatorius & Hermes Furis
summary: Saga seed where the Order becomes the richest institution through banking by House Mercere.

label: Hermes Portal
summary: A high-level Rego Terram ritual that creates a magical portal for near-instantaneous travel between two locations, cast simultaneously at both.

label: Hermes the Blessed One
summary: Charismatic leader of the Children of Hermes claiming to be Hermes Trismegistus reborn.

label: Hermes Triceres
summary: Mercere's second apprentice and son, nicknamed 'Mutant', who specialized in Muto Vim metamagic.

label: Hermes Trismegistus
summary: The legendary sage to whom magi attribute the maxim 'As above, so below,' cited regarding astrology and the Stone of Death.

label: Hermetic Alchemy

label: Hermetic Architecture

label: Hermetic Arithmetic
summary: Secrets of number magic in the Arithmetic Magic chapter.

label: Hermetic Arts
summary: The fifteen Techniques and Forms of Hermetic magic, which can be opened in a character with The Gift and advanced through study from vis, books, or teaching but not by simple practice.

label: Hermetic Astrology
summary: Mystery school working astrological influences into general Hermetic magic.

label: Hermetic Charm
summary: Use of Sympathy Traits in Hermetic lab work and enchanted devices designed as charms that must be activated in secret.

label: Hermetic Crime
summary: Offence under the Code.

label: Hermetic Crusade
summary: The pro-war crusader faction and expedition led by Julius and Lavinia against Iceland's magicians.

label: Hermetic Dream Interpreter

label: Hermetic Elementalist
summary: Possible Hermetic mystery cult for which Elemental Magic may be an Outer Mystery.

label: Hermetic Empowerment
summary: Minor Mystery Virtue allowing a device to power Ritual/vis-requiring effects by draining a bound spirit's Might.

label: Hermetic Evocation
summary: Secrets of the Disciples of the Worm, taught to second-degree Initiates as spell binding.

label: Hermetic Experience
summary: A Minor, General Virtue for a character with experience among the magi of the Order of Hermes, granting 50 extra experience points for relevant Lore or Latin.

label: Hermetic Fair
summary: A gathering of the Order held in a vast twelve-sided quartz-walled hall in the Alps, supported by impossible ivory trees.

label: Hermetic Generans
summary: Lesser Enchantment (ReTe 15) of an iron disc producing rotary motion like one horsepower.

summary: Minor Mystery Virtue using Euclid's postulates for sympathetic magic, granting casting bonuses for perfect figures and new Line Range, Arcane Circle Target and Arcane Ring Duration.

label: Hermetic Gruagachan
summary: Gruagachan nominally members of the Order of Hermes, taking the Hedge Wizard Flaw and Arcane Lore Virtue.

summary: Research projects to integrate folk witch practices into Hermetic magic via breakthroughs.

label: Hermetic longevity ritual
summary: Ritual that expires when Pasiel inflicts an aging crisis.

label: Hermetic Maga
summary: Virtue listed in this text.

label: Hermetic Mercenaries
summary: Magi hired by communes as guardsmen, thieves or assassins, working covertly.

summary: Magic unable to question those given a Church burial.

label: Hermetic Numerology
summary: Minor Mystery Virtue letting a magus devise Rotes and enchant a Numerologist's Book; prerequisite for Divination (Numerology).

label: Hermetic phonotactics
summary: Study of the voice as a tool to cast magic, Bronwyn's field.

summary: Minor Hermetic Mystery Virtue allowing sacrifices on pagan altars to substitute for 1-6 pawns of vis in Ritual summoning.

label: Hermetic Sahir
summary: A tradition referenced as the model for relocating the Corrguineach; wizards who command spirits.

label: Hermetic Sigil
summary: Magical signature of a magus, which can be shrouded.

label: Hermetic Sihr
summary: Hermetic practitioner of Sihr who researches jinn.

summary: Major Hermetic Tainted Virtue: studying Goetic Arts also yields Rego experience, and studying supernatural Lores yields Vim experience.

label: Hermetic Speculum
summary: A rock-crystal sphere or mirror scrying device for seeing distant individuals; spread into general and civic use.

label: Hermetic Spirit Magic

label: Hermetic theurgist
summary: Magus practicing Hermetic Theurgy who could learn to summon landvaettir.

label: Hermetic Tourney

label: Hermetic Traditions
summary: Infernal societates within the Order of Hermes.

label: Hermetic True Names
summary: Virtue taught to Knights of the Green Stone.

summary: Virtues tied to Hermetic magic; they can be taught by a parens who has them, with a Target Level of 15 for Minor and 21 for Major, and converted from Supernatural Abilities.

label: Hermit
summary: One who renounces the world to live alone, celibate, observing the liturgical hours outside a formal monastic context.

label: Hermitage
summary: Lands around which Lord Goulis has area lore.

label: Hermitage Castle
summary: Castle in Liddesdale built on monks' bones, home of Lord David de Soulis.

label: Hernis
summary: Rhine magus convicted of endangering the Order through excessive Wizard War and hunted down.

label: Hero

label: Herodias
summary: Evil biblical woman; name given by the educated to the she-demon of the strigae.

label: Herodotus
summary: Ancient historian who wrote about Aristeas.

label: Heroes' Birthright
summary: Minor Heroic Virtue granting a special magical power of up to Level 15.

label: Heroic Gesture
summary: Maneuver (+4) of foolhardy bravery; if the leading character dies the event is won.

summary: Minor Heroic Flaw granting strong Personality traits and Confidence, but letting the storyguide sometimes dictate the character's heroic actions.

label: Heroic Virtues
summary: A category of Virtues (with associated Flaws) from Houses of Hermes: True Lineages that maestros may also choose.

label: Heron of Alexandria
summary: Ancient inventor whose works inspired the wonderful steam-rotator machines powering an Unnatural Law covenant.

label: Herr
summary: German title (generosus) for any noble without a higher title, equivalent to lord.

label: Herrit of Tytalus
summary: A young Tytalus magus among the members recruited to Nigrasaxa.

label: Herrod of Hohenbourg
summary: The most famous woman painter of 1220, recently deceased, whose book Hortus deliciarum showcases her illuminations.

label: Hersfeld
summary: A town dominated by a large imperial Benedictine abbey, whose springs are known for magical restorative powers.

label: Hertha

label: Hervé filius Évrard
summary: Redcap son of Évrard who runs the temporary Mercer House at the Champagne fairs.

label: Herzak of Verditius
summary: Member of Feritel.

label: Herzog
summary: German title equivalent to duke.

label: Herzog Ernst
summary: German epic hero.

label: Hesiod
summary: Greek poet whose Theogony lists the children of Eris.

label: Hesmed
summary: The angel of annihilation among the five angels of punishment.

label: Hespera
summary: The namesake of the enchanted lab item The Bookstand of Hespera.

label: Heusaff family
summary: Ancient Breton family owning the Isle of Ushant; Lord Heusaff is secretly a guise of the Primus.

label: Heuvelland
summary: Flanders' uplands.

label: Hex
summary: A Supernatural Ability to bring injury or ruin upon enemies via eye contact, occult signs, or sympathetic magic, often a false power tainted by the Infernal.

label: Hex Toys
summary: Releganta's wax figurines crafted into Arcane Connections to punish people.

label: Hexentanzplatz
summary: A rocky crag in the northeastern Harz with a Faerie aura of 2 where the witches of the Harz gather every April before proceeding to the Brocken.

label: Hexham Priory
summary: Priory headed by Abbot Geoffrey, frequently raided by Horsingas for supplies.

label: Hibernation
summary: Ritual power of Adranus letting the spirit stay inactive for a year and save Might for its awakening.

label: Hibernation of the Slumbering Turb
summary: A ReMe 35 ritual Texture-Target spell, invented by Odorpes, that puts anyone touching the caster to sleep until the Spring Equinox.

label: Hibernia Tribunal
summary: A region where the Daughters of Echo league's leader lives near Burnfoot and where The Single Ocean's headquarters are technically located.

label: Hicuccus of Criamon
summary: Author of The Babble Within Thought.

label: Hidalgo
summary: Ancestral caballero backed by his family in matters of honor, with the Knight Virtue.

summary: A laboratory Flaw that may be gained on a botched Refinement roll or spotted and corrected on a sufficiently good roll while increasing Refinement.

label: Hidden (Duration)
summary: Faerie ritual Duration lasting while the caster or target is hidden; ends if discovered.

label: Hidden Resources
summary: Covenant Boon representing vassal tithes to liege.

label: Hidden Shape
summary: An aspect of the heartbeast whereby, due to the Limit of Essential Nature, a transformed Bjornaer appears as a mundane animal to magic.

label: Hidden Virtues
summary: Fixed, occult qualities of objects granted by astral influences and ordained by God that cannot be explained by their substance.

summary: Amount of land (120-144 acres) required to maintain a family of affluent free peasants, producing four pounds for a lord.

label: Hide Flavor
summary: Gourmand's Power altering the flavor and texture of a substance.

label: Hide from Mortal Sight
summary: Forcas's Power of true invisibility lasting until the next Sunday.

label: Hide to Parchment

summary: MuTe(He) 15 spell softening stone or wood to hide a small item such as a Key to the Mystic Veil.

summary: A measure of an infernalist's or demon's repute in Hell, which protects against failed maleficia and modifies Goetic totals.

label: Hierophant

label: Hierophants
summary: The three mysterious leaders of the Magoi of the Star, greatest astrologers able to Initiate many astrological Virtues.

summary: A serious category of offense under the Code of Hermes, of which a Pralician obtaining excess scrying information could be convicted.

label: High Crime of depriving a magus of his magical power

summary: Crime committed by harvesting another's legacy or damaging magical resources.

summary: Serious Hermetic charges that the pirates of Waddenzee would face if the mundane authorities moved against them with no Tribunal support.

label: Higher Ground
summary: Height advantage giving +1 to Attack and Defense.

summary: A Personality Flaw of dedication to a cause, suggested for Mithraic characters and milites who take the Code of Garus seriously.

summary: A covenant that previously held the Motherhouse site and was destroyed in the Sundering of Tremere, leaving its resources unclaimed.

label: Highland Chieftain
summary: Companion template: chief of a sept responsible for forty families, embroiled in a blood feud.

label: Highland Giants

label: Highland Sailor
summary: Grog template: a former galley crewman from the western coast now serving a covenant ashore.

label: Highland Weather Witch
summary: Tradition of Highland witches able to call or dispel storms by whistling.

summary: Hilly, thickly wooded lands where clans rule and bow to no king; home to giants in their further reaches and to the Scottish Church's abbeys.

label: Highly Cognizant
summary: A Virtue held by the most dangerous faeries, allowing them to adapt and change their roles to feed on human emotional energy.

label: Highly Organized
summary: A Free laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab's contents are optimally arranged (+1 General Quality); gained by improving Refinement and lost in major accidents.

label: Highly Skilled
summary: Virtue appearing in a Roman Tribunal vocation template.

label: Hijra
summary: Muhammad's emigration from Mecca to Medina in 622.

label: Hilda
summary: An immense female covenant grog (custos) born and bred at Fengheld, a skilled mace-and-shield warrior with Great Strength and prime leadership material, given as a gift to young magi.

label: Hildebrand
summary: Dietrich of Bern's man-at-arms who kills Kriemhild after discovering the bodies of Gunther and Hagen.

label: Hildegard of Bingen
summary: Renowned Rhineland mystic and scholar (d. 1179), abbess at Rupertsberg, who recorded her visions in books like Scivias and wrote on medicine, music and natural history. Rumored to have been adopted into House Jerbiton despite being unGifted.

label: Hildesheim
summary: A splendid cathedral city of northern Germany famed for its civic buildings and churches, raised to greatness by St. Bernward, whose crypt lies in St. Michael's church.

label: Hill of Martyrs
summary: A hill in Paris to which Salvirius asks a magus to deliver a sealed message.

label: Himinis the Mad
summary: An 11th-century Verditius magus who developed the Inner Mystery of making cursed items and founded the Confraternity of Himinis the Mad.

label: Hind
summary: Semi-mythical source of diamonds and spices.

label: Hinder the Gift
summary: A Perdo Vim 55 enchanted effect in the Wizard's Bridle that reduces the Casting Total of any spells by 25 points as a constant effect.

label: Hippian school
summary: School of thought within House Tytalus that Eduardus supports.

label: Hippias
summary: A Sophist quoted in the Analects of Tytalus who believed in the fundamental unity of mankind through unwritten laws of divine provenance; the Hippian view is named after him.

label: Hippocrates
summary: The ancient physician associated with naming epilepsy the 'sacred disease' (the Falling Evil).

label: Hippogriff
summary: A faerie beast gifted by the queen Titania to the King of England, housed at the Tower of London, which is poisoned by the Divine aura of London's many churches.

label: Hippolytus of Rome
summary: Church Father whose Philosophumena recounts Simon Magus' death.

label: Hippomancy
summary: Divinatory method using behavior of horses, listed among Ceremonial Augury Phenomena.

label: Hipta the Nurse
summary: A powerful shapechanger Daimon (Magic Might 15, Animal), the nurse of Dionysus, who favors the form of a dove and is invoked for forgiveness from curses and magical harm.

label: Hired Sword
summary: Flaw appearing in a Roman Tribunal vocation template.

label: Hirsau
summary: The most powerful Benedictine monastery in Germany, founded 1059 with the relics of St. Aurelius and modeled on Cluny; with a Divine aura of 5, it has been immune to the faerie attacks beset other Black Forest monasteries.

label: His Master's Voice
summary: Rumael's power to summon lesser demons without controlling them.

summary: History of the Franks written by St. Gregory of Tours in 594.

label: Historia Normannorum
summary: History by William of Jumieges with an Area Lore: Normandy summa.

label: Historia rerum Anglicarum
summary: History by William of Newburgh with Area Lore: England summa and Area Lore: Normandy tractatus.

label: History of the Britons
summary: Tractatus by Nennius, earliest account of Arthur.

summary: Tome by the monk Aimon, official chronicle of the Capetians; summae on French Royalty, Ile de France, and Divine Lore.

label: History of the Kings of Britain

summary: Tractatus by Geoffrey of Monmouth including the Prophecies of Merlin.

label: History of the Normans
summary: History by Dudo of St Quentin containing Area Lore: Normandy summa and tractatus.

label: Histria
summary: Oppidum on the Istrian Peninsula in the Transylvanian Tribunal.

label: Hobble the Foul-Mouthed Wretch
summary: PeCo 40 talisman enchantment laming the target for a Sun duration.

label: Hobgoblin
summary: A creature often used as the form of the phantasmal being sent into a victim's mind by a Phantasm maleficium.

summary: Dynasty that received most of the Swabian pretender's lands.

summary: Minor Covenant Boon: the covenant holds parish benefices.

label: Holdfast
summary: Remora power duplicating any movement-inhibiting spell up to level 35.

label: Holstein

summary: Vial of the blood of Jesus held in the church of Heiligenblut.

label: Holy Forbears

summary: The ability of holy characters to instill Personality Traits in followers via personal or ceremonial influence (die + Presence + Leadership).

label: Holy Innocents Day

label: Holy Island
summary: Island seven miles up the coast from the Farnes, home to Lindisfarne Priory.

summary: Lore Ability of the Knight Templar template.

summary: Divine variant of Magic Theory taught by the book in the Uncovered Crypt story seed.

label: Holy Method of Meditation
summary: Holy Method with which the Holy Music Ability is associated.
