summary: A tradition of Karaite Jews with The Gift who practice Holy Magic and may join the Order so long as their magic comes directly from God.

label: Karamas
summary: Miraculous acts worked by zahids through pious contemplation.

label: Karantia
summary: Tremere member of Postestas.

label: Karbala'
summary: Site of al-Husayn's burial.

label: Karet
summary: Serious excommunication; the dead under it become dybbukim.

label: Karlotte
summary: Red-haired daughter and heir of Baron Schonburg with strong faerie blood; she lies in a coma after being attacked, and the fae of the Court of Dark Summer hold her cure.

label: Karreg an Tan
summary: Fire Rock with Ignem vis.

label: Karzełek
summary: Polish dwarfs with green grass for hair who ride diminutive horses over sleeping field hands; they aid diligent farmers but punish minor infractions violently.

label: Kashrut
summary: Dietary requirements codified in the Torah; kosher food complies.

label: Kaspar
summary: Mechthild's eldest son from a previous marriage, physically dominant but dimwitted, holding real power in the castle.

label: Kassala

label: Kassalan Dust

label: Kassalan Exorcism
summary: A Minor, Supernatural Virtue allowing minor exorcism spells via the rites of the Mortuary Society of Kassala, aligned to the Magic Realm and using Kassalan Dust.

label: Katadesmos
summary: A curse tablet, usually lead or a mirror's back, used to curse and control the individual named upon it; +2 penetration.

label: Kataphraktoi
summary: Byzantine armored horse archers whose horses wore scale armor.

label: Katrina of Bjornaer
summary: One of the Order's youngest hoplites, whose heartbeast is a wolverine; she serves the Quaesitores and allies with Adrasteia.

label: Kattenfeest
summary: Ypres ritual of hurling cats from the Cloth Hall belfry.

label: Katzenveit
summary: A Waldgeist (wood-spirit) who haunts the forests of the Fichtelgebirge (Spruce Mountains).

label: Kauno
summary: Elder Futhark rune "Pain" used as a vitkir Art. Rune of torches, fever and burning pain; affects fire and heat (Ignem) as well as sores and sickness.

label: Keen Sense of Smell
summary: A Minor General Virtue giving a +3 bonus to all rolls involving the sense of smell, including tracking with the Hunt Ability.

label: Keen Vision
summary: A Minor Virtue acquirable by a Bjornaer inner heartbeast, appropriate for an eagle heartbeast and possessed by crows, eagles, and wild goats.

label: Keeper of the Path
summary: The figure who tests aspirants at the Path of Strife's Initiation site, requiring them to negotiate the Labyrinth of Strife.

label: Keepers of a Thousand Tales
summary: Group focused on Arabic stories, of which Caprican is a member.

label: Kelledei
summary: The cele de ('servants of God'), communities of Scottish Church brothers who left monasteries ruled by greedy lay abbats; they have no formal rule.

label: Kelpie
summary: Carnivorous magical creature (Might 20 Aquam) of deep fresh-water pools, a mass of tentacles that can turn into a black stallion to lure and drown victims.

label: Kelpies
summary: Faerie horses that drown victims.

label: Kemuel
summary: Archangel whose servants guard the Treasury of the Four Winds.

label: Kennels
summary: Establishment for hounds whose size indicates noble prestige.

label: Kenneth MacAlpin
summary: King of the Scots who stood on the Stone of Destiny in 834 and conquered the Picts with the aid of House Diedne.

label: Kent
summary: County palatine that resisted after the Conquest.

label: Kentigern of Ex Miscellanea
summary: Quaesitor from a Hibernian beast-mage tradition with an affinity for dogs, controlling a pack of faerie hounds.

label: Ker
summary: Leader of the Keres.

label: Kerberos
summary: Merinita term for fearsome monster Guardians of the Threshold, always restrained and bypassable by trickery or courage.

label: Kerbourg
summary: Patch of firm ground in the Grande Brière with a covered alley of megaliths in a low Magic aura.

label: Keres
summary: Leti of violent death, led by Ker.

label: Kerguntuil
summary: Diedne vassal of Branugurix (920-1007) on the Rose Coast, interested in giant lore.

label: Kerotakis
summary: Closed vessel exposing metal leaves to vapors; credited to Mary the Jewess.

label: Kerry Mountains Pool
summary: A deep black pool in the Kerry Mountains of Hibernia where the ancient Irish cast votive offerings to their ancestors; a Bjornaer ancestor site.

label: Kerseenn
summary: Great Spirit of Ushant of misdirection, constantly shifting shape.

label: Kervus
summary: Ioannes Acer's faerie caricature, which has taken the form of a huge stag capable of bearing his weight, which he rides everywhere.

label: Keswick
summary: Place-name origin of Ealwynn of Keswick.

label: Keter
summary: Sefirah meaning 'Crown', level 10 on the Tree of Life; understood by a kabbalist with Kabbalah 10.

label: Kettle Hat
summary: Bowl-shaped iron cap with wide brim.

label: Ketuvim
summary: The Writings, final section of the Tanakh; a collection of tractatus.

label: Key of Solomon
summary: The greatest grimoire, key grimoire of the middle ages, attributed to Solomon.

label: Key to the Mystic Veil
summary: InVi 30 enchantment in a key embedded in a grove feature granting sight across a regio boundary to cultists.

label: Keynsham
summary: Village northeast of Bath named for Saint Keyne.

label: Khadija
summary: Wealthy widow who employed and married Muhammad; his first wife.

label: Khanqah
summary: Sufi convent.

label: Khawass al-Qur'an
summary: Special properties of the Qur'an, which may be invoked anywhere; Divine Might 100.

label: Kherion of Merinita
summary: Magus who defeated Lanval in 1028.

label: Khidr
summary: Immortal Muslim prophet, the Green One, who drank of the Water of Life and wanders giving advice.

label: Khrafstar
summary: Persian name for the noxious biting creatures that burst from Naonhaithya's body cavity.

label: Khshathra Vairya
summary: One of the Zoroastrian Immortals (Amesha Spentas): 'Desirable Dominion', associated with Just and Vim in the Blessing ritual.

label: Kiburg Family
summary: Noble family of the Alps, rival of the Zähringers, which followed a similar policy of founding towns.

label: Kidron
summary: River carrying Jerusalem's sewage from Hinnom.

label: Kiev
summary: City where Nicolai met the wandering merchant-summoner who became his teacher.

label: Kikimora
summary: Wife of the domovoi who helps with chickens and spinning; seeing her spin is a presentiment of death.

label: Kilkenny
summary: Irish town home to the Kilkenny Coven.

label: Kilkenny Coven
summary: A fractured folk witch coven in and near Kilkenny split between rival Gifted cousins Janine and Anne.

label: Kill the Living Air
summary: Spell cast spontaneously with vis that badly drains Vindsvall's Might.

label: Kind Temper
summary: Temper of love and mercy, tied to Charity and opposing Envy.

label: Kinderschrecker
summary: German child-eating ogress ('child guzzler'), a version of the Gello without exsanguinating breasts.

label: King

label: King Albion
summary: Lombard king under whom Pavia became capital.

label: King Alfonso I
summary: Aragonese king whose death brought the Templars great lands.

label: King Aurelius
summary: A king of Britain who sought to build a monument to his murdered people and was advised by Merlin to bring the Giant's Ring from Ireland.

label: King Baldwin I of Jerusalem
summary: King of Jerusalem; an encounter with him led the pirate-merchant Godric to repentance and pilgrimage.

label: King Clodio
summary: King of the Franks whose wife bore Merovech.

label: King Dagobert
summary: Seventh-century king who founded Saint Denis's Lendit Fair near Paris, once the most important fair in France.

label: King Edgar
summary: King legendarily said to have rid England of wolves in the 950s.

label: King Edward of England
summary: English king asked to adjudicate the Scottish succession after 1290.

label: King Gradlon
summary: Sixth-century King of Cornouaille whose city Is drowned; founded Quimper.

label: King Haakon
summary: Norwegian king whose invasion failed at Largs in 1263.

label: King Henry III
summary: Young English king whose treasury the Templars maintain in 1220.

label: King Herod
summary: King who beheaded John the Baptist at Salome's request.

label: King Hezekiah
summary: King who broke Nehushtan into pieces during his fight against paganism.

label: King Holly

label: King Jereboam
summary: Biblical king in I Kings 13.

label: King John

label: King Kyzikos
summary: Ruler of Bear Island killed by Jason; buried in a tumulus on the Leimonian Plain.

label: King Lothair
summary: King of Lotharingia whose kingdom split in 855.

label: King Louis of France
summary: King who led the Second Crusade; Templars took over command by Antioch.

label: King Lycurgus of Sparta
summary: Spartan king whose saying 'Obedience is of the highest benefit' is a Tremere moral touchstone.

label: King Mark of Cornwall
summary: One of Arthur's under-kings who later held Tintagel as his seat.

label: King Melchior
summary: One of the three Magi, possibly linked to Sal Almelke.

label: King Oak
summary: The faerie ruler of the southern Oak Forest among the Courts of the Seasons, a regal and generous Summer King who battles King Holly; touchy of honor and takes words literally.

label: King of Aragon
summary: Banished the Waldensians from his lands in 1194.

label: King of Atlantis
summary: Pavania's father, ruler of sunken Atlantis.

label: King of England
summary: England's monarch, who holds 15 to 20 percent of the kingdom's arable land and has 45 greater-baron vassals.

label: King of Fire (Power)
summary: Adramelech's Power to create any Ignem effect cheaply.

label: King of the Beggars
summary: Title of the ruler of the Parisian beggars and thieves, also the Grand Coësre; currently held by Anacrôn.

label: King of the Black Mountain
aliases: King Fir of the Black Forest
summary: The dread faerie ruler of the Black Forest with Faerie Might 90, dwelling atop the Feldberg; born from a rebellious splinter of the original genius locus and seeking the destruction of Durenmar.

label: King of the wolves
summary: Magical being whose blessing might grant a Skinchanger pelt.

label: King Philip II
summary: French king whose treasury is kept by the Paris Temple.

label: King Priam
summary: King of Troy alongside whom Duke Francio fought.

label: King Richard of England
summary: Crusader king who captured Cyprus and Acre and raised Robert of Sabloel to grand master.

label: King Richard's Ring
summary: A wondrous gold ring that protects the wearer from fire (+5 Soak), named after Richard the Lionhearted and the legendary ring he wore on crusade (Craft Level 16).

label: King's Bench
summary: One of the highest English courts of appeal, fixed at Westminster by Magna Carta, trying important civil and treason cases and issuing writs; its senior justice is Martin of Pattishall.

label: King Sancho II
summary: King of Portugal (1223-1245).

label: King Sel
summary: A king said to be buried on horseback with his treasury within Silbury Hill near Avebury, his tomb protected by a curse that strikes dead would-be robbers.

label: King Sigebert
summary: The king who founded the abbey at Bury St. Edmund's in 633.

label: King Stephen
summary: King who besieged John Marshal. He threatened to catapult the hostage William but spared him instead, which changed his Reputation.

label: King Stone
summary: A large stone standing apart from the Rollright Stones circle, the most magical of the lot, whose chips are supposed to ward against demons.

label: King Valdemar I of Denmark
summary: Danish king who invaded the island of Rügen in 1168, threatening Crintera's pagan aura.

label: King William Rufus
summary: A king of England who summoned Eadric Wilde and his faerie wife to London out of a wish to look upon them.

label: Kingdom of Asturias
summary: A kingdom in northern Spain where Laberius served as court magician and fought the Moors during the early Reconquista.

label: Kingdom of Burgundy
summary: Kingdom absorbed into the empire in 1033.

label: Kingdom of Denmark
summary: Homeland of Ogier, of interest to Rhineland and Norman magi who see potential to colonize it.

label: Kingdom of France Lore
summary: Area lore of France.

label: Kingdom of Jerusalem
summary: The Crusader state of the Holy Land whose major port and nominal capital is Acre, constantly at risk from Muslim forces.

label: Kingdom of Man and the Isles
aliases: Kingdom of Man and the Isles
summary: Kingdom ruled by the Norse king of Man, to which Kintyre belongs.

label: Kingdom of Tír Chonaill
summary: Irish kingdom in the northwest of Ireland containing Lough Dearg.

label: Kintyre
summary: Peninsula added to the kingdom of Man by Magnus Barelegs in 1098; rich in stone alignments.

label: Kirburgers
summary: Relatives-by-marriage who inherited the Zähringer lands, the most powerful indigenous nobles of the Western Alps.

label: Kirist of Flambeau
summary: A young, fiery-tempered Flambeau magus of Voluntas specializing in Ignem who is committed to the greater good of the Order.

label: Kiss of Forgetfulness
summary: Faerie power causing the person touched to forget his mortal life until he sees an object associated with his home.

label: Kiss of Frost
summary: Faerie power letting the person touched survive the cold above the snowline until he treads upon grass.

label: Kiss of the Mermaid
summary: Faerie power letting the person kissed breathe under water until he walks upon dry land.

label: Kitab al-Irshad
summary: Biography of the twelve imams by al-Shaykh al-Mufid.

label: Kitab al-Luma'
summary: Tractatus by al-Ash'ari defending mainstream theology against the Mu'tazilis.

label: Kitab ash-Shifa
summary: Ibn Sina's Book of Healing; summa on Artes Liberales and the four Elementalist Forms.

label: Kite Shield Parry
summary: Ability listed in a Roman Tribunal vocation template.

label: Klagenfurt
summary: Town listed in the Tribunal index.

label: Klaus
summary: A companion-level craftsman example character, master of the Swordsmiths' Guild, with the Virtue Touched by the Divine Realm, who makes greatswords and a wondrous flaming greatsword.

label: Kleité
summary: King Kyzikos' wife who hanged herself on his tumulus.

label: Kleon of Criamon
summary: A magus of House Criamon who spent years in the Thuringian Forest performing dangerous experiments with raw vis, became riddled with Warping, and likely perished in a Twilight episode.

label: Kloster Maria Laach
summary: A Benedictine monastery beside Laach Lake founded in 1093, with a Divine aura of 4 and a paradise-like gardened courtyard re-creating the Garden of Eden.

label: Kludie
summary: The most powerful faerie hound variant, from Belgium, able to take large forms of dog, cat, bat, horse or frog, walking on its back legs and preceded by supernatural blue flames.

label: Klymene
summary: Titaness who is the underworld's cavern.

label: Klynoites
summary: Pater of the magus who assassinated Prima Kalliste; he Marched his own filius and became the next Primus of House Tytalus, denouncing House Flambeau at Tribunal.

label: Knack
summary: Virtue named in the text, associated with Larta chefs, smiths, minstrels or muses.

label: Knife
summary: Brawl weapon that can also be thrown.

label: Knife of Human Bone
summary: Philippus Niger's talisman, a wickedly curved dagger of human bone enchanted to stay razor-sharp, with attunements for Precise Destruction, Destroy Body, and Destroying Minds.

label: Knight
summary: A Minor, Social Status Virtue for a member of the noble warrior class who may have high-quality weapons, armor, and a horse, and take Martial Abilities.

label: Knight Banneret
summary: A knight who leads other knights under his own banner. The rank can be claimed by arriving with ten liveried knights or bestowed by a liege.

label: Knight Errant
summary: +1 Background Virtue: you have been knighted and may bear arms and be addressed as sir, owing no fealty or service.

label: Knight Shield Parry
summary: Ability listed in a Roman Tribunal vocation template.

label: Knight Templar
summary: Companion template: a scarred Templar returned from the Holy Land who loves fighting and fine living.

label: Knight (title)
summary: A professional mounted warrior (miles, chevalier), who in some places must pay his overlord a fine for dubbing others.

label: Knighthood
summary: Ceremony creating a knight, often tied to vassalage since a knight usually joins the liege's household as a minor vassal.

label: Knightly Demands
summary: Optional Major Story Flaw that replaces Oath of Fealty. The storyguide can use it to pull knights into ballad-style plots such as quests, feuds and rescues.

label: Knightly Duties
summary: Flaw a caballero villano may take instead of Dependents.

label: Knights Hospitaller
aliases: Knights of the Hospital of St. John of Jerusalem
summary: A military order of monk-knights holding land across Christendom whose English houses gather funds and supplies for the Levant.

label: Knights of Alcantara
summary: Iberian military order based in Castile-Leon.

label: Knights of Blanik
summary: The sleeping army of St. Wenceslaus, knights seated motionless in stone chairs in an underground hall within the Divine regio of Mount Blanik, awaiting their call to arise.

label: Knights of the Green Stone
summary: A group of magi who believe the romances conceal the true story of the Grail and seek clues to a great artifact.

label: Knights of the Holy Stone
summary: Cult whose members often choose heraldically charged shields as talismans.

label: Knights of the Round Table
summary: Heroes of medieval romances who fight giants.

label: Knights of the Sword
summary: A military order founded in 1202 by Albert von Buxhövden, bishop of Riga, to crusade against pagan tribes; based at Fellin in Livonia and active in Pomerania, they control the slave trade and are notoriously brutal.

label: Knights Templar
aliases: Poor Knights of the Temple of Solomon
summary: A military order of monk-knights founded by Hugh de Payns and Godfrey of St. Omer in 1118, notable for banking and building round churches including one in London.

label: Knivestone
summary: Three knife-like rocks among the outer Farnes.

label: Knockers
summary: Cornish mine faeries said to warn miners of collapses by knocking, playing along with belief that they are souls of dead Jewish miners.

label: Know-It-All
summary: Major or Minor Child Personality Flaw: compelled to show off knowledge and superiority.

label: Know the Heavens
summary: InVi 29 constant enchantment in the magical armillary sphere that senses astrological time and the influence of the planets around it.

label: Know Then the Calloused Touch of Faerie Hands
aliases: Know Then the Calloused Touch of Faerie Hands
summary: Evocation/Grant 30 rite granting the target 5 Warping Points, a permanent effect.

label: Knowe
summary: Faerie hills where seelie faeries live; farmers avoid planting or grazing on them.

label: Known Hedge Wizard
summary: Major Story Flaw: the character is known to and watched by the Order.

label: Knows People
summary: A Minor, General Virtue letting a character act as a social middleman, requesting a 'bait' once per story to gain aid from a non-player character.

label: Knoxes Reef
summary: Inner Farne feature that remains above water at high tide.

label: Koblenz
summary: A fair-sized city where the Mosel joins the Rhine, owned by the archbishops of Trier; home to St. Kastor church and a Teutonic Knights chapter house.

label: Kobolds
summary: German mine faeries that lace mines with arsenical ore and cause minor trouble, though some are helpful.

label: Koerakoonlane
summary: Dog-human hybrid faeries of the frozen north who raid settlements on dog sleds to take slaves.

label: Koilios
summary: Magus of Montverte whose raid on Lapis Crudus established a precedent legalizing raiding.

label: Koios
summary: Titan who rules the axis of the heavens.

label: Kolazonta, the Chastiser
summary: A Divine angel (Might 30, Ignem) tasked to chastise the faithful for their failings, appearing as a dark cloud or man of white fire; he brought the plague upon the Israelites for rebelling against Moses.

label: Kolding
summary: A small trading town at the head of Kolding Fjørd on the border between the Kingdom of Denmark and the Duchy of Schleswig, with about 200 inhabitants relying on fishing and a weekly farm market.

label: Koldovali
summary: The kolduni's name for their oral magic, very similar to gruagach magic, in which water plays an important role.

label: Koldovali Theory
summary: Ability that replaces Pictish Language in koldun spell formulae.

label: Koldun
summary: Shamanic wizards from the Novgorod Tribunal who abandoned their pagan priesthood for sorcery; a Witches of Thessaly variant tradition.

label: Koldun Lore
summary: Lore studied by kolduni.

label: Kolkrabus
summary: The devious raven familiar of Murion that spied at Crintera and taunts Stentorius, believing he has usurped Murion's role as leader of the Oak Gild.

label: Kolossos
summary: Stone buried in place of an absent body, acting as an Arcane Connection anchoring the spirit; Aristeas's is a statue with a raven emerging from his mouth.

label: Kore
summary: A nature-oriented deity whose name eumolpids of the Huntress may learn through the Mysteries of Names of Power and Invocation Magic.

label: Korrigan
summary: Breton faeries: hunchbacked manikins with cat's claws and goat's hooves who dance and may take the form of a beautiful woman; dangerous in Brocéliande.

label: Koshchey the Deathless
summary: Powerful koldun whose soul is hidden in an egg in a duck in a hare in a chest under an oak on an island in a regio.

label: Kosmokrators
summary: A rank of primal spirit used to model primeval giants, beings the size of mountain ranges or larger.

label: Kostchei the Undying
summary: Villain in Maria Morevna, cited as an example of the villain role.

label: Krak des Chevaliers
summary: A real fortress cited as a forebear of the Superior Engineering concentric-castle style.

label: Kraken
summary: Sea monster form in which Pan Caudarax attacks the ships from below.

label: Kratos
summary: The Daimon of might, bodily strength, and sovereign rule, son of Styx and Pallas, referenced in the Analects of Tytalus as a constant companion of the Founder.

label: Kraxios Lord of Wrath
summary: A demon who could draw the remaining Infernal aura into a hidden regio and cause paranoid dreams among grogs.

label: Krems
summary: City near Vienna with a Luciferan community.

label: Kresnik
summary: Slavic nightwalkers, each a community's protector, fighting kudlaki with dappled phantastica.

label: Kresniki and Kudlaki
summary: Local nightwalker traditions.

label: Kriemhild
summary: Sister of King Gunther and wife of Siegfried in the Nibelungenlied, who avenges Siegfried's murder by orchestrating the deaths of Gunther and Hagen.

label: Krios
summary: An Elder Titan of leadership and father of Pallas the Titan of war-craft.

label: Kronos
summary: The Greek representation of time in serpent form, whose coils appear as scaly marks on the wrists of some Criamon ghosts.

label: Kropel
summary: A good-natured dwarflike creature of the Harz who travels abroad hidden by his hat of fog.

label: Kubu
summary: Infant-sized faerie, a child who died unnamed, who lures children away to die.

label: Kudlaki
summary: Slavic sorcerer nightwalkers who steal a community's fertility and become vampires after death.

label: Kunal Trow
summary: The 'king' trow, a more powerful trow that takes villages under its care in exchange for a bride or groom and may learn all gruagach powers.

label: Kupala
summary: A faerie lord who guards the Fire Flower in Slavic lands and from whom Richenda Spinosa is descended, source of her secret faerie blood.

label: Kushiel
summary: An Avenger of Evil whose angel-like name means Rigid One of God.

label: Kutna Mine
summary: A fantastically rich silver mine opened by the Cistercian monks of Sedlec, where a monk named Anton found silver rods sprouting; site of a story seed about a magus secretly mining silver with magic.

label: Kybella
summary: Tytalus theurgist of Exspectatio, Titanoi member, who maintains Fudarus's spirit enchantments and casts its Aegis.

label: Kyburgers
summary: Noble family with a home castle near Winterthur and about 100 vassal castles.

label: Kyffhauser Mountains
summary: A double line of hills on the Saxony-Thuringia border, legendary resting place of famous kings (notably Frederick Barbarossa) and site of Fengheld's Turris Acontiarum chapter.

label: Kyllénos
summary: A female Idaian Daktyl who remains on Bear Island with Titias.

label: Kyzikos
summary: Legendary king whose slaying is mentioned in the Golden Fleece legend; his staters are said to be buried on Bear Island.

label: Kyzikos staters
summary: Lost coins said to be buried in chests on Bear Island.

label: Lübeck
summary: The most important coastal port in Germany and a hub of Baltic trade, effectively founded in 1157 by Henry the Lion and home to the covenant Oculus Septentrionalis.

label: L'espurgatoire Seint Patriz
summary: Norman French tractatus by Marie of France on Area Lore: Purgatory, Quality 9.

label: La
summary: Prima of House Criamon and Praeco, an elderly Rego specialist once called Lucia who murdered a priest under the Black Mark and is cursed by God.

label: La Chaise-Dieu
summary: Monastery of St. Robert heading over 200 priories.

label: La Coloubre
summary: Dragon near Lalinde slain by St. Front.

label: La Rochelle
summary: Chartered port held by England with a Templar church.

label: Lab Mastery
summary: Cult of Mercury mastery ability adding mastery to Lab Totals for similar effects.

label: Lab Notes
summary: Laboratory records; Verdi holds 400 years of them.

label: Lab Text
summary: A written record allowing magi to research magical creations, most commonly to invent a Formulaic spell, far more quickly than without assistance; a key covenant library resource.

label: Lab Total
summary: The core laboratory work measure (Technique + Form + Intelligence + Magic Theory + Aura Modifier) used for all lab activities such as inventing spells, enchanting items, and binding familiars.

label: Laberius
summary: A hermit-wizard of the ancient Roman cult of Mithras who healed and trained the young Flambeau, later killed by sahirs in Iberia.

label: Labor Points
summary: Points describing business development, also applied to errant knights' tourney income.

label: Laboratory
summary: A magus's workshop for magical experimentation; one standard laboratory exists per magus in the baseline covenant.

label: Laboratory Horoscope
summary: Horoscope cast for a season of lab work to gain an Astrological Modifier of +1 to +5 to the Lab Total.

label: Laboratory Magician
summary: Major Supernatural Flaw: the character may cast charms only with the aid of a text.

label: Laboratory Turbulences
summary: Turbulences occurring during laboratory work, covered in the Adolescentia chapter.

label: Laborer
summary: A free Social Status Virtue for a trained worker who provides a valuable service without producing a finished good, using a Profession Ability rather than a Craft.

label: Labyrinth
summary: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab's exterior is a maze or structural puzzle, favored by some Criamon magi (-1 Safety, -1 Health, -2 Aesthetics, +2 Mentem or Vim).

label: Labyrinth Meditation
summary: A non-magical Criamon ritual of walking a maze while contemplating a problem to improve concentration, granting a bonus to a single subsequent roll.

label: Labyrinth of Strife
summary: A tangled structure of tunnels at the Path of Strife's Initiation site that magi can only escape by performing feats violating Criamon tenets of apt action.

label: Lacerta
summary: A Clan Arelie magus of an Iberian sept, parens of Natrix.

label: Lachlan Mac Calum
summary: Younger brother of Donncadh and seanachaidh of Clan Mac Gruagach, a storyteller knowledgeable about Highland supernatural beings who expects to inherit the chieftainship.

label: Lack of Control
summary: Flaw appearing in a Roman Tribunal vocation template.

label: Lack of Penetration
summary: Flaw.

label: Lack of Potency
summary: Flaw possessed by Calum Mac Lachlan.

label: Lacuna
summary: A 'hole' within an urban environment where the Dominion does not dominate, allowing magi to cast spells without realm interaction penalties; may carry other auras.

label: Ladha
summary: Islamic degree of Hell for Christians.

label: Ladislaus
summary: A trusted companion of Roznov covenant who haunts the Prague slave market using his Magic Sensitivity to identify and filter out Gifted children among the slaves for delivery to Coeris.

label: Lady Godgifu
summary: The legendary noblewoman of a story seed whose lord promised to reduce taxes if she rode naked through the marketplace.

label: Lady of the Game
summary: Anonymous powerful magical spirit in the form of a woman who leads nightwalker processions, appoints captains and resurrects eaten animals.

label: Lady of the Lake
summary: Faerie Lady of the Lake who enchanted Merlin and lives at Lake Comper; queen of the korrigan.

label: Lady of Winter
summary: Magic being held captive by the Lord of Summer, disrupting the seasons.

label: Laering
summary: Vitki apprentice.

label: Lagny-sur-Marne
summary: Site of the 1179 tourney to which Henry the Young King brought five hundred knights.

label: Laguz
summary: Elder Futhark rune "Water" used as a vitkir Art. Rune of water, especially the ocean; almost always associated with Aquam.

label: Laigle
summary: Small chartered forest community in Normandy.

label: Lair
summary: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: a creature hides or hibernates in the lab, known or unknown (-1 Safety, +1 Warping).

label: Laity Objects
summary: Items given as gifts to the Church by dying people, such as the deathbed or best robe.

label: Lake Acherusia
summary: Sample terrestrial regio from the Apocalypse of Paul near Tarsus, a multilevel regio leading to a city where Michael baptizes the repentant.

label: Lake Avernus
summary: Circular sulfurous lake on the Bay of Naples in the Roman Tribunal, connected by tunnel to Cumae.

label: Lake Balaton
summary: Lake near Budapest home to Men of the Lake, site of a failed Tremere assault.

label: Lake Brienz
summary: Steep-sided Alpine lake fed by the Aare.

label: Lake Comper
summary: Viviane's home.

label: Lake Constance
summary: Lake on which the trade village of Rorschach stands.

label: Lake District
summary: The region where the covenant Ungulus sits in a carved tower on a ridge, and where Aquila rides the thermals in eagle form.

label: Lake Léman
summary: Lake near Geneva dug by Gargantua.

label: Lake Nemi
summary: A sacred lake in the Roman Tribunal in whose waters Huntress initiates may bathe on the Ides of August during the Eumolpid initiation.

label: Lake Pavin
summary: Lake where a basalt stone summons a storm yielding Auram vis.

label: (Lake) Regio Network
summary: Inherited Virtue of Men of the Lake.

label: Lake Sonderdach
summary: Lake with a dragon.

label: Lake Thun
summary: Lake with the castles of Thun and Oberhofen.

label: Lamashtu
summary: Ancient Babylonian goddess of stillbirth, a Might 45 faerie with lion head, donkey teeth and owl feet.

label: Lamballe
summary: Seat of the Baron of Penthièvre.

label: Lame
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which both of the character's legs are severely damaged, requiring crutches and heavily penalizing movement and combat.

label: Lamed Vav Tzadikim Nistarim
summary: The 36 hidden righteous souls in each generation who sustain the world.

label: Lamellar
summary: Overlapping plates fastened to each other.

label: Lamia
summary: Former queen of Libya, cursed by Hera, now a serpent-bodied faerie who eats children and steals eyes.

label: Lammergeir
summary: Bearded vulture, the heartbeast of Eginhard and Kamilla.

label: Lammergeyer
summary: The bearded vulture deemed by House Jerbiton the correct falconry raptor for magi; its bones make particularly good magical flutes and it has deep orange iron-rubbed plumage.

label: Lammikin
summary: Ugly Scottish faerie who torments children and kills mothers.

label: Lamp without Flame
summary: A Creo Ignem spell that creates a steady daylight-bright light with no apparent source, illuminating about ten paces across a point that may be a mobile item.

label: Lampaul
summary: Fishing community on Ushant.

label: Lampedusa
summary: Island southwest of Sicily once a Roman fish-sauce manufactory, perhaps with a weak Magic aura.

label: Lampione
summary: Island southwest of Sicily said to be a stone dropped by a cyclops; may have a Faerie aura.

label: Lance
summary: Weapon properly wielded only by a mounted character; dismounted it functions as a long spear.

label: Lancea Magica
summary: Magical attack developed by Cerularius that pierces Parma Magica; banned by the Colentes.

label: Lancelot
summary: Cabal of the Crushed Viper member who befriends and betrays Flambeau milites.

label: Land of Nod
summary: Place of Cain's banishment, equated by some with Arcadia.

label: Land of Spirits
summary: Mystical realm explored by the magi of Tarragon Vale alongside Arcadia.

label: (Land) Regio Network
summary: A Minor, Supernatural Virtue giving access to an extensive network of regiones (e.g. in lakes, sky, or caves) between which the character can travel quickly.

label: Landévennec
summary: Abbey.

label: Landed Noble
summary: A Major Social Status Virtue granting a character an agency prior to play; listed with a Resistance of 3 on the Resistance of Agents Table.

label: Landernaeu
summary: Port.

label: Landfriedensbund
summary: Temporary regional peace alliances encouraged by German nobles, designed to keep the peace by developing processes of law instead of military feuds; they pave the way for later eternal alliances.

label: Landgraf
summary: A graf with a larger than usual area of administration, ranked slightly above a count.

label: Landvaettir
summary: Icelandic land spirits who watch the coasts, serve the guardians and bargain with galdramen; they pledge to avenge Biorn Egilsson.

label: Landvaettir attendant
summary: Spirit given to each galdraman during the war, with Might equal to Song Talent x5, reducing casting time and accepting bargains for little vis.

label: Landvaettir bargains
summary: Deals galdramen make with spirits that can give magic resistance.

label: Landvaettir lords
summary: Powerful landvaettir who held the galdramen leader in esteem and give attendant spirits to all galdramen during the conflict.

label: Langon
summary: Village with a chapel on a temple of Venus.

label: Langres
summary: Walled hilltop town of the Lingones.

label: Language
summary: Ability used to find charms in formularies and write lab texts.

label: Langue d'oc
summary: Southern language region of the Cathars, belonging to Provençal.

label: Languedoc
summary: A region of central southern France where Brother Julian wanders and preaches against the spread of the Cathar heresy.

label: Languedoc Tribunal
summary: Tribunal where Mathematikoi robes resemble Cathar perfecti.

label: Languidus
summary: Somnifer's filius, representing Lapis Crudus at Tribunal without formal membership.

label: Lanleff
summary: Round Templar chapel.

label: Lanner
summary: North African falcon easy to train and taught to hunt in pairs.

label: Lannion
summary: Town with Brélévenez Church.

label: Lanterns of the Dead
summary: Cemetery towers with lanterns; an angel pulls down those over unworthy dead.

label: Lanval
summary: Arthurian knight and champion of Oleron defeated by Kherion in 1028.

label: Lanvaux Moors
summary: Moors.

label: Laon
summary: Hilltop city, former Carolingian capital, with a famous cathedral school and where Norlanus lives.

label: Lapidary
summary: An 11th-century text by Bishop Marbode of Rennes on the magical use of gems.

label: Lapis Crudus
summary: Once-great covenant founded 1064 to heal the Flambeau–Tytalus rift, trapped in a faerie regio in Fontainebleau for eighty years by Candidus.

label: Lapis Maior
summary: Level 15 Substantial alchemical reagent, a waxy red stone that transmutes up to 50 cubic inches of lead into gold.

label: Lapis Minor
summary: A Level 20 Alteration Reagent creating a reddish waxy stone whose touch purifies a precious metal from its alloy; called the Lesser Stone, distinct from the sought-after Greater Stone.

label: Lapiths
summary: Ancient people of Thessaly who fought the original centaurs.

label: Laplander Nightwalkers
summary: Nightwalker tradition whose members die if their insensate bodies are simply touched.

label: Laplander Shamans
summary: Shamans who battle in phantastic form, suffering fatigue; the true origin of certamen.

label: Laquerius
summary: The certamen School of the Noose, whose practitioners bind the opponent's ritual working and impose lasting Defense penalties.

label: Lares Lore
summary: An Ability used by Vestals to interact with lares (household spirits, also called penates), domestic faeries of the home and community.

label: Large
summary: Minor General Virtue that changes a magic character's Size without modifying Strength or Quickness; for Beasts of Virtue it gives -1 Quickness and +2 Strength.

label: Large-field Farming
summary: Farming system using about half of Mythic Europe's agricultural land, suited only to heavy soils, found in central England and near large French and German cities.

label: Large Wolf
summary: A wolf up to twice normal weight, usually the leading male of a pack.

label: Largen of Quaesitor
summary: Associate Quaesitor member of Magvillus who avoids its politics.

label: Largs
summary: Site of the battle of 1263.

label: Larinda
summary: A young Ex Miscellanea maga of Dankmar (age 20), daughter and filia of Jiphella, with a sunny disposition and affinities for Animal, Herbam, Aquam, and Auram.

label: Larta
summary: A category of unGifted person afforded protection and tutelage by a Hermetic House; Hildegard of Bingen is cited as a Larta maga of House Jerbiton.

label: Larus Egg-Thief
summary: Clan Chief of Clan Maruhs, a wandering magus with a skua (seabird) heartbeast who haunts the coasts of western Europe.

label: Las Huelgas
summary: Richest nunnery under the Cistercian Rule, near Burgos, founded in 1187; royal burial place.

label: Lasa Vegoia the Matron
summary: Water nymph Daimon who taught the Etruscans theurgy and divination and can teach theurgy.

label: Lash of the Chastened Servant
summary: PeVi 15 removing 5 Might from a demon; incurs suspicion of diabolism.

label: Lasiq
summary: A Major, Social Status Virtue for an experienced Nizari Isma'ili assassin who has completed seven murders and commands a small band of fida'is.

label: Last Flight of the Phoenix
summary: A CrIg 50 spell in which the caster immolates himself in a white-hot blast doing +45 damage; an early version was found in Flambeau's own lab notes, used by magi with Greater Immunity to fire.

label: Last Italian Faerie Forest
summary: The last great Faerie forest of the Roman Tribunal, mainly on Sicily, with shifting borders and many regiones.

label: Lasting Consequences of Serious Damage
summary: Option where Incapacitating Wounds may leave a Minor Flaw.

label: Late Bloomer
summary: Minor Child Flaw: treated as one age category lower on the Aging Chart.

label: Latent Magic Ability
summary: A Minor, General Virtue indicating an unmanifested magical quality, more limited than The Gift, that may appear spontaneously.

label: Latent Magical Ability
summary: A Virtue granting uncontrolled magical talent; Torven's Latent Magical Ability causes wolf packs to come to his aid in the forest.

label: Latent Mystical Ability
summary: Virtue appearing in character statistics or rules in this text.

label: Lateran Basilica
summary: Basilica Innocent III dreamt of as collapsing but propped up by a small ragged man.

label: Lateran Palace
summary: Usual residence of the Pope.

label: Latin
summary: The scholarly language ability; a magus can rewrite up to Latin x 20 levels of Laboratory Texts per season to make them usable by others, and literacy in Latin is required to write or copy Lab Texts.

label: Latin conquerors
summary: Victors of the siege of Constantinople who weakly rule Bear Island.

label: Latin Empire
summary: The crusader-created state ruling Constantinople after the 1204 sack, the weakest of four powers feuding over the Balkans, whose Latin Emperor cares more for his home Flanders than the City.

label: Latin Kingdom of Jerusalem
summary: Crusader kingdom established on Christmas Day 1100.

label: Latin Quarter
summary: The left-bank Paris district of jumbled houses where masters and students live, a lawless place of books, learning, drinking, and gambling.

label: Latins
summary: Latin invaders occupying Constantinople and the Theban Tribunal.

label: Latria
summary: Worship reserved for God alone; offering it to others is a terrible sin.

label: Latrunculus filius Aurelia
summary: Criamon Terram magus and surveyor who believes the Great Ones are buried at Roman road intersections.

label: Lauds
summary: Canonical hour of the Divine Office: Service at 1 am (or dawn in summer) after which monks return to bed.

label: Laughter of Mentem Vis
summary: Vis whose laughter fills listeners with joy.

label: Laurens
summary: Dwarf king who rules the Rosegarten regio and cursed his roses to appear as stone.

label: Lausanne
summary: City listed in the Tribunal index.

label: Laval
summary: Town whose mayor Pugnatis controlled.

label: Lavinia
summary: Archmaga and Quaesitor of House Guernicus, an Intellego specialist skilled in wards and necromancy, who calls the War Tribunal at Durenmar and co-leads the crusade.

label: Law
summary: Ability appearing in character or covenant library statistics in this text.

label: Law of Contagion
summary: Magical principle transferring the Stag of Virtue's fever immunity to those who eat its flesh.

label: Law of Names
summary: A magical principle by which knowing a ghost's full name allows it to be summoned, as used in the Incantation of Summoning the Dead.

label: Law of Sympathy
summary: Magical principle by which the Cockerel of Virtue's cry terrifies spirits of darkness.

label: Lawidh
summary: Cherub who tests the faithful.

label: Laws of Edward the Confessor
summary: 12th-century English laws under which the King owns all Jews and their property, relevant to a Minority Boon covenant in England.

label: Laws of Hospitality
summary: The Rhine Peripheral Code rules, derived from German guest-laws, governing the duties of guests and hosts and entitling a magus to request hospitality at any legal covenant for a vis fee.

label: Lay to Rest the Haunting Spirit
aliases: Lay to Rest the Haunting Spirit
summary: A Perdo Mentem (General) spell that reduces a ghost or spirit's Might by the spell's level if it penetrates, causing the spirit to vanish if its Might reaches zero.

label: Laylat al-Bara'a
summary: Night when God approaches Earth to forgive sins.

label: Laylat al-Qadr
summary: 27th of Ramadan, when all Infernal auras drop to zero until dawn.

label: Le Cité
summary: Capital of Périgord, with the sacred spring Vésone and St. Stephen's Cathedral.

label: Le Conquet
summary: Town where Fudarus formed an artificer guild.

label: Île de la Cité
summary: The mile-long central island of Paris, its ecclesiastical and administrative core.

label: Le Havre
summary: Port from which the Ship of the Dead departs.

label: Le Mans
summary: Capital of Maine with the Cathedral of St. Julien and a pagan fertility menhir.

label: Le Mans Menhir
summary: Pinkish menhir by Le Mans cathedral, former fertility cult center whose sacrificial blood yields Creo vis.

label: Le Puy
summary: Town from which the Capuchonnes spread.

label: Le Puy-Notre-Dame
summary: Pilgrim church housing the Girdle of the Virgin.

label: Le Puy-St-Front
summary: Town rival to Le Cité.

label: Lead curse tablets
summary: Tablets thrown into the waters.

label: Lead Mania
summary: Silver Lady power similar to Blessing of Childlike Bliss.

label: Leader of the Pack
summary: Black Dog power making canines fight as a trained group at +2.

label: Leadership
summary: An Ability for commanding others; women raised to manage holdings always have Leadership scores, and the angel Seferiel has Leadership 7 with a specialty in magi.

label: Leadership (Virtue)
summary: Virtue +3 held by Mercatora.

label: Leadworker
summary: Minor Hermetic Virtue descended from Aita cult necromancy, enabling crafting of katadesmoi and kolossoi containing fixed arcane connections; Leadworkers also supply Tremere magi with ghosts.

label: League of Iconophiles
summary: The most powerful of the eastern Empire's transient magical leagues, formed to oppose Emperor Leo III's destruction of religious icons; its members are the ancestors of House Jerbiton.

label: Leap of the Fire
summary: A Rego Ignem spell (Level 10) that causes a bonfire to leap up to 10 paces in any direction, catching if there is fuel; a Targeting roll lets it deal +10 damage to a target.

label: Leap of the Shadows
summary: Evocation/Portage 20 rite moving a seen target instantly into shadows.

label: Learn (Ability) From Mistakes
summary: A Minor, General Virtue granting experience points in a chosen Ability the first time per session the character botches or narrowly fails a roll.

label: Learn Chirurgy from Mistakes
summary: A Virtue commonly taken by empirici allowing them to learn the Chirurgy Ability from their failures.

label: Learn From Mistakes
summary: Mastery ability granting experience when botching or narrowly failing the spell.

label: Learned Magicians
summary: Magicians who influence luck, health, and magic with protective devices and trade in protecting buildings against magical siege engines.

label: Leather Ripper
summary: A Minor, Supernatural Virtue granting the power to destroy a group of leather objects, as a PeAn(He) 30 effect.

label: Leaving the Crypt
summary: Necropolis ghost power to physically affect the living for a Diameter.

label: Lecanomancy
summary: Divinatory method using bowls of fluid, listed among Ceremonial Augury Phenomena.

label: Leccacorvo
summary: The Genoese bank cited as a legendary money/banking income example.

label: Lech
summary: One of the three legendary founding brothers of the Slavic peoples, who continued on to settle in Poland.

label: Lecherous
summary: A Major or Minor Personality Flaw in which the character seeks sexual contact with as many people as possible.

label: Lechfeld
summary: Battle site in 955.

label: Lectio
summary: Ability appearing in character statistics in this text.

label: Lector
summary: Minor order whose members receive a codex of lessons and now have ceremonial duties.

label: Leczyca
summary: A covenant established in Poland in 1052 by refugees from Grand Silesia to reinforce the New Slavonic Tribunal's authority over the Slavic lands.

label: Leda
summary: Julia's twin sister, abducted by faeries at age five.

label: Ledea
summary: Merinita maga who started a healing cult around an Airy Spirit's spring, hoping to convert it to Faerie.

label: Left Bank of Paris
summary: The intellectual and scholarly district of Paris, center of Roman Lutetia.

label: Legacy
summary: Minor Story Flaw: the character descends from a legendary magus or Redcap and is accorded respect but given harder tasks.

label: Legates
summary: Personal representatives of the pope sent throughout Europe.

label: Legati a latere
summary: Highest grade of papal legate, usually cardinals, with the widest powers including decisions binding even the pope.

label: Legati nati
summary: Historic title held by some archbishops (vicarii apostolici) that by 1220 carries no real power.

label: Legatus
summary: Field leader of House Tremere in war and the Primus's heir.

label: Legatus a latere
summary: Closest advisors of the pope, appointed by him, who aid him in Rome and act as legates; up to 53 at a time in three ranks.

label: Legatus missus
summary: Grade of papal legate (nuncio) given a particular mission, often priests or deacons from the capellani.

label: Legend Lore
summary: Ability appearing in character or covenant library statistics in the Roman Tribunal.

label: Legendary Artist
summary: An artist whose Reputation reaches 11 and is taken by his muse into a supernatural realm, becoming an immortal being with a Might score and supernatural powers based on his Craft or Profession.

label: Legends of Brittany
summary: Summa on Faerie Lore by Celeres of Breton Arthurian tales.

label: Legerdemain
summary: An Ability used by a thieving performer to pick a victim's pocket via a Dexterity + Legerdemain roll while the crowd is captivated.

label: Legio IX Hispana
summary: Roman legion that marched north in 118 and vanished; ghost sightings are reported.

label: Legion Lore
summary: Ability referenced as used or valued by Tremere magi or creatures.

label: Legion of Mithras
summary: A 13th-century mystery cult reconstruction of the ancient Cult of Mithras that teaches additional powers via Initiation; Castra Solis's shield grogs may serve it as Auxiliaries.

label: Legion of Mithras Lore
summary: Organization Lore of the Legion used by Mystagogues.

label: Legionaries
summary: Roman soldiers garrisoned at the temple town.

label: Legionary ghost
summary: Ghost of a fallen Roman legionary, Magic Might 10 (Mentem).

label: Leiden papyri
summary: Ancient papyri containing a list of 37 substances and plants with their mystical names.

label: Leinster
summary: Irish region where the gallowglaigh fought.

label: Leir
summary: Son of Bladud.

label: Lemnos
summary: The island where Hephaestus settled and took twelve forge-companions; site of a Forge of Hephaestus, a Verditius covenant (Ingasia), and an all-Verditius community.

label: Lend Senses
summary: Famulus Power lending its hearing or sight to one it touches; broken by displays of religious sentiment.

label: Lens of Glimpsing Spirits
summary: InIm(Me) 34 constant-effect crystal lens in a brass ring that reveals invisible spirits.

label: Lent
summary: Penitential season; a feast at its start uses up forbidden foods, and war is forbidden during it by the Truce of God.

label: Leo
summary: Priest among the early Franciscans, known as Brother Lamb of God; Francis' confessor and scribe.

label: Leo III
summary: The Byzantine Emperor who in 729 ordered the destruction of images of Christ and the saints and forbade crosses in worship, prompting the formation of the League of Iconophiles.

label: Leodontina
summary: Filia of Tremere who became unhinged before Tribunal and was ostracized; most of her filii were killed in the ensuing Hunt.

label: Leon of Armenia
summary: Armenian ruler who declared war on the Templars in 1211.

label: Leonardo Fibonacci of Pisa
summary: A reclusive Pisan mathematical genius (Int +4, Com +5) who discovered the golden section / Fibonacci sequence and wrote the tractatus Liber abbaci; his work can aid Aristotelian Magic Theory and Herbam research.

label: Leopold of Austria
summary: Leader of the Fifth Crusade.

label: Leper Magi
summary: A small lineage within House Tytalus descended from Hariste and Epimetheus who draw magical strength from leprosy; powerful healers and longevity experts who are inevitably specialized in Corpus magics.

label: Leper Magus
summary: A Major Hermetic Virtue exclusive to House Tytalus describing the mystic legacy of leprosy passed from Tytalus through Hariste's line; grants Life Boost and lets the magus mortify his flesh to produce vis.

label: Leprosy
summary: A Major General Flaw representing the divine disease; it gives a permanent -2 Living Condition modifier and an extra Heavy Wound during Aging Crises, and prevents gaining a positive reputation.

label: Leprosy (Flaw)
summary: A Major Flaw gained by the victim of the leprosy disease, imposing a Living Condition penalty and reputation effects.

label: Leprosy, Hermetic
summary: A Critical Melancholic Disease caused by Hermetic spells, a rapid hideous wasting disease with a pungent rotting smell.

label: Les Halles
summary: The great central market of Paris, covered by Philip II in 1183.

label: Les Trois Pignons
summary: Barren sandstone massif in western Fontainebleau housing Lapis Crudus.

label: Lesser Benediction
summary: A Minor, Supernatural Virtue granting a minor blessing from a supernatural power, with examples like Gift of the Gab, Green Fingers, and Pricking Thumbs.

label: Lesser Charm
summary: Minor Supernatural Flaw: a Virtue activated by a secret ritual charm.

label: Lesser Elixir
summary: Minor Mystery Virtue enhancing a Longevity Ritual with extra ingredients whose Elixir Points raise the Aging Bonus; requires Hermetic Alchemy.

label: Lesser Enchanted Item
summary: A category of enchanted device requiring the Lab Total to be at least double the effect's modified level and to which Effect Expiry cannot be applied.

label: Lesser Enchantment Imaginem Vis
summary: Truffle-shaped Imaginem vis whose shavings flavor food, giving a host +3 to influence guests.

label: Lesser Enchantment Rego Animal Vis
summary: Truffle-shaped Rego vis whose scent compels wild boars and pigs to try to devour it, driving them berserk.

label: Lesser Enchantment Vis
summary: Extraordinary vis emulating a lesser enchantment, usually level 30 or lower, not consumed by use.

label: Lesser Expansion
summary: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab is enlarged with some specialized equipment (+1 General Quality, +2 Upkeep, 1 Specialization point).

label: Lesser Faerie Powers
summary: Virtue appearing in faerie statistics in this text (Lesser Faerie Powers).

label: Lesser Feature
summary: A Minor laboratory Structure Virtue: the lab features a unique structure aiding certain lab work, granting +1 Aesthetics and 1 Specialization point.

label: Lesser Focus
summary: A Minor laboratory Structure Flaw: an existing Lesser Feature is the central focus of the lab, enhancing it but hindering unrelated activities.

label: Lesser Guardian
summary: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Virtue: a supernatural creature (less than Might 20) not the owner's familiar resides in and protects the lab (+1 Safety).

label: Lesser Horde
summary: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Virtue: a small group of semi-intelligent creatures helps in the lab (+1 General Quality, +1 Upkeep, +1 Safety, +1 Aesthetics).

label: Lesser Illusion
summary: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: one apparent merit of the lab is merely an illusion; a balancing Minor Virtue is taken but its effects are negated.

label: Lesser Infernal Power
summary: A Minor Supernatural Virtue for corrupted beasts adding 2 to Infernal Might and granting an Infernal Power that cannot have a Penetration total.

label: Lesser Limits of Hermetic Magic
summary: The boundaries of what Hermetic magic can achieve, resulting from Bonisagus' unfinished theory; the forest paths each lead to overcoming one of these limits.

label: Lesser Magic Power
summary: Virtue granted by the Rowan of Virtue amulet, equivalent to a Rego Vim ward.

label: Lesser Magical Power
summary: A Virtue or Magic Quality named among the traits of magical animals or dragons in this text.

label: Lesser Malediction
summary: A Minor Supernatural Flaw in which the character has been cursed by a supernatural power, with effects about as bad as other Minor General Flaws.

label: Lesser Nymph
summary: Weak dancing nymph with Might 10.

label: Lesser Power
summary: Minor Supernatural Virtue granting a limited power designed as a Lesser power; activation costs Fatigue levels based on Might cost. Also a Magic Quality.

label: Lesser Purifying Touch
summary: A Minor, Supernatural Virtue letting a character heal a specific minor or self-recovering illness with a touch and a Fatigue level.

label: Lesser Secundus
summary: House Jerbiton officer who must remain at Valnastium.

label: Lessini Mountains
summary: The mountains where the Alps cross into Italy, site of Dietrich Von Bern's ornate tomb filled with dragon-blood-enchanted arms.

label: Let death seize upon them, and let them go down quick into hell
aliases: Let death seize upon them, and let them go down quick into hell
summary: Purity Cursing effect (Level 85) laying utter waste to everything within a boundary.

label: Let the Bonfire Burn
summary: Flame Dancer power setting fire to a slightly inflammable target.

label: Leti
summary: Spirits of death, one of which Francis might call his sister Bodily Death.

label: Letter of Authority
summary: Document granted by a Quaesitor to non-Quaesitors giving them investigation immunity and the right to demand cooperation.

label: Letter of Credit
summary: Templar banking instrument allowing pilgrims to deposit wealth and retrieve it elsewhere.

label: Leucrota
summary: A mythical beast whose tongue provides a Shape and Material bonus of +6 to mimicking human voices.

label: Levant Lore
summary: Ability appearing in character or covenant library statistics in this text.

label: Levant Tribunal
summary: Tribunal existing since shortly after the Order's founding that gained attention during the crusades; home of the Covenant of Al Arama.

label: Leviathan
summary: Vast ancient being of the Aquam province of the Twilight Void tethered to Big Harcar, which desires the destruction of certain ships; Osgood's master.

label: Levy
summary: Lowest, quickly drafted and poorly equipped soldiers who also provide siege labor.

label: Lewis
summary: Hebridean island with large stone circles.

label: Leywrite
summary: Theoretical adultery tax charged on a woman who made herself unmarriageable by losing her virginity.

label: Liar's Chime
summary: InMe(Im) 25 modification of Frosty Breath of the Spoken Lie that sounds a bell when the target lies.

label: Liban
summary: Irish woman changed into a mermaid by Danu who lived 300 years, was baptised, and entered Heaven as a Holy Virgin.

label: Libellus
summary: The newest and one of the largest covenants in the tribunal, founded and led by Stephen Eruditus of Jerbiton; an unknown quantity in tribunal politics.

label: Liber abbaci
summary: Leonardo of Pisa's book (1202), a Quality 14 tractatus on Artes Liberales (arithmetic) covering interest, square roots, alloy percentages, and the golden section; reading it aids Herbam research and Aristotelian Magic Theory.

label: Liber de Compositione Alchemiae
summary: Morienus Romanus' alchemical work, translated into Latin by Robert of Chester in 1144.

label: Liber de Lumine
summary: A Tractatus on Ignem (Quality 11) by Elaine concentrating on light as an aspect of the Form of Ignem.

label: Liber Regularum
summary: Civil and Canon Law summa (Quality 10, Level 3) by St. Victricius.

label: Liberalia
summary: March Ceremony of Welcome for apprentices and its feasting, traditionally hosted by Tarragon Vale.

label: Liberate the Sinful
summary: Domination power permanently removing a sinful Personality Trait.

label: Libra
summary: Sign of the Zodiac with its own element, temperament and decans in astrological correspondences.

label: Library of Alexandria
summary: Destroyed by Caesar in parable.

label: Library of Apollodorus
summary: A work summarizing the Golden Fleece legend.

label: Library of Durenmar
summary: Enchanted to prevent Memory Palace of the Sage being performed within.

label: Library of the Normandy Tribunal
summary: Tribunal-owned book collection kept at Confluensis and leased as Tourney prizes.

label: Library of Valnastium
summary: Temple of the Muses moved from Greece; one of the Order's finest mundane libraries that invented the shelf.

label: Library Tower
summary: Oldest structure of Confluensis with council chamber, library and Mercere Portal.

label: Libuse
summary: The Gifted granddaughter of Czech who had a great vision at Vysehrad Rock foretelling her husband Premysl, founder of Bohemia's ruling dynasty.

label: Libya
summary: Land whose queen became Lamia.

label: License of Absence
summary: A Major, General Virtue for a priest relieved of some duties, giving an extra free season each year; only available to Priest Social Status.

label: Licho
summary: One-eyed old woman faerie personifying ill-fortune, who clings to victims and tricks them into self-harm.

label: Lickspitten
summary: A famulus in the form of a black cat with a star of white hairs on its belly, serving a witch by hiding the taint of her Powers.

label: Lickstone
summary: Small metal plate attached to the palate carrying redcap spells; Cymena's contains Seven-League Stride.

label: Lictor
summary: Experienced hoplite chosen by the Greater Alpine Tribunal to coordinate Wizards' Marches; wears a leopard-edged sash.

label: Liddesdale
summary: Valley in the Scottish Borders with a Malevolent Infernal aura 3 tarnished with Fear.

label: Liddeswater
summary: Small river running through Liddesdale.

label: Liege
summary: A prince-bishopric and market city where the River Legia joins the Meuse, grown from the martyrdom site of St. Lambert; its most famous bishop was Notger.

label: Lien
summary: Loan in which the lender receives the use of a borrower's vis source until repaid.

label: Life Boost
summary: A Minor, Hermetic Virtue letting a magus boost Formulaic or Ritual spell casting totals by +5 per additional Fatigue level spent, risking damage.

label: Life-Boost
summary: Virtue requiring expenditure of Fatigue; a Daimon expends Might instead.

label: Life-Linked Art
summary: A Major Supernatural Virtue letting an artist wound himself while working to increase artwork's Aesthetic Quality, making the piece a permanent Arcane Connection.

label: Life Linked Folk Witch Magic
summary: Virtue possessed by Mistress Greta.

label: Life-Linked Folk Witch Magic
summary: Major Supernatural Virtue letting a folk witch spend Fatigue levels to boost her Casting Total by 5 each.

label: Life-Linked Spontaneous Magic
summary: A Major, Hermetic Virtue letting a magus produce stronger spontaneous magic at the cost of declaring an effect level and spending Fatigue or taking wounds.

label: Life of Saint Guthlac
summary: Text quoted about demons attacking Saint Guthlac.

label: Life Stages
summary: Human transitions (birth, reason, adulthood, mastery, mortality) that attract faeries.

label: Lift the Unfair Curse
summary: General-level TaCu spell that removes a curse if the total meets double the curse's level (or its level if the caster cast it).

label: Lifting the Dangling Puppet
summary: A Rego Corpus spell (Level 15) that lifts a person of Size +1 or less vertically into the air.

label: Ligature
summary: A small charm of parchment, stones, or herbs worn around the neck containing an Arcane or Sympathetic Connection, employing natural principles to grant a bonus to a single die roll.

label: Light Shaft of the Night
summary: A Rego Ignem spell (Level 20) that collects moonbeams and starlight into a controllable vertical shaft of soft silvery light, castable only under the night sky.

label: Light Sleeper
summary: Virtue appearing in a Roman Tribunal vocation template.

label: Light Touch
summary: A Virtue improving fine manual work; held by the Craftsman template and offered as an alternative for the Spying Maid.

label: Lightless
summary: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: the lab is totally dark and its contents cannot be seen, requiring other means of spatial perception (-1 Upkeep, +1 Warping).

label: Lightning Reflexes
summary: A Virtue granting superior reflexes, cited in connection with the adder's reflexive attacks and listed as suitable for beasts.

label: Ligurio
summary: Vassal of Fudarus (913-1011) in the Vendée, destroyed by giants presumed sent by Kerguntuil.

label: Lila
summary: Henri's only child, a daughter whose marriage to a manipulable husband is vital to Nidi's welfare.

label: Lilac Grove of Nidi
summary: A possibly druidic oak grove in Henri's chase overgrown with perpetually flowering lilacs that yield Herbam vis; Nidi's key vis source.

label: Lilin
summary: Female Tempter night spirits giving nightmares and smothering children; their offspring with men are shedim and lilin.

label: Lilith
summary: Demoness of prostitution, wife of Iblis and concubine of Adam; Queen of Tempters sharing leadership of the ninth order, depicted as a naked woman with a serpent's tail, enemy of infants.

label: Lille
summary: Seat of the Counts of Flanders and a cloth fair town.

label: Limbo
summary: Destination of unbaptized pagans.

label: Limbo of Infants
summary: Part of Hell holding those who die in original sin alone, without personal mortal sin.

label: Limbo of the Fathers
summary: Part of Hell where the souls of the just who died before Christ awaited Heaven; emptied by the Harrowing of Hell.

label: Limes
summary: A line of defensive forts reinforced by magic built by the Roman legions under Mercurian guidance, delineating the empire's northern extent and first fracturing the Hercynian Forest.

label: Limit (Condition) Duration
summary: A gruagach Duration required for all Blessing and Curse spells, lasting until a condition that lifts the spell is fulfilled; easier-to-lift limits are cheaper.

label: Limit of Arcane Connections
summary: A Hermetic limit concerning the use of Arcane Connections; a Touch-range spell on a room does not violate it even when affecting unseen people within.

label: Limit of the Divine
summary: One of the two fundamental limits of Hermetic magic: magic cannot affect the Divine, with most lesser limits believed to derive from it.

label: Limit of the Lunar Sphere
summary: A boundary of Hermetic magic at the orbit of the moon; magic cannot affect the moon or the ethereal region beyond it, and it stunts spells reaching toward the heavens.

label: Limited Gestures
summary: Minor Inferiority limiting manipulation to vague gestures.

label: Limited Movement
summary: Minor Inferiority restricting travel to short distances.

label: Limited Speech
summary: Minor Inferiority preventing intelligible speech.

label: Limits of Magic
summary: The fundamental boundaries constraining Hermetic magic; Major Breakthroughs push them, Hermetic Breakthroughs break Lesser Limits such as the Limit of Magic Resistance.

label: Limoges
summary: City divided between the Cité and the commercial center around the Abbey of St. Martial.

label: Lincoln
summary: An important town and seat of a powerful bishop, left in poor material state by the battle of Lincoln in 1217; its castle is held by Nicola de Hay.

label: Linden Gild
summary: A peace-striving go-between gild founded by former magi of Fengheld after the Schism War, seeking cooperation between magi and covenants; led by Occultes of Durenmar.

label: Lindisfarne Priory
summary: Priory on Holy Island famed for illuminated scriptures; its library holds the Vitae of Saint Cuthbert and Bede's works.

label: Lindorm
summary: A huge legless bat-winged worm of German and Scandinavian tales that hoards treasure and takes hostages for ransom.

label: Lindworm
summary: Dragon near Klagenfurt with a taste for virgins, slain by Herakles.

label: Line of Muj
summary: A mythic lineage from the Balkans whose ancestor made a pact with a magical guardian spirit, blessing his descendants with great strength and power over storms; surviving members live in the Transylvanian Tribunal and belong to House Tremere.

label: Line Range
summary: New Hermetic Geometry Range equivalent to Sight not requiring the target be seen, needing a geometry calculation.

label: Lineage of Abydaros
summary: Mystery lineage to which Carmine belongs.

label: Lineage of Carolinus
summary: Mystery lineage of which Vortimer is a senior member.

label: Lineage of Hercynius
summary: A Bonisagus lineage descended from Hercynius, the penultimate apprentice of Bonisagus, which founded Waldherz to pursue primal forest magic and was largely destroyed in the Schism War.

label: Lineage of Irmele
summary: A line of wandering, weather-working magi within House Bonisagus founded by Irmele filia Trianoma, prominent among the peregrinatores and the Linden Gild.

label: Lineus
summary: Example magus who casts a Line Range spell at Centrus beyond a wall.

label: Lingering Injury
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which an old injury won't heal, penalizing physical rolls and worsening with age.

label: Linguist
summary: A Minor, General Virtue increasing all Language Advancement Totals and character-generation language experience by a quarter.

label: Linosa
summary: Small island southwest of Sicily.

label: Lion
summary: Legendary fierce beast said by Pliny to have lived in Greece; will not attack a prostrate man.

label: Lion Mane Collar
summary: Collar woven from a Lion of Virtue's mane that duplicates Mastering the Unruly Beast.

label: Lion of Mithras
summary: Fourth rank (Captain), learns Inscription on the Soul and spends seven years at the temple.

label: Lion of the North
summary: An Ars Magica sourcebook describing Pralix's war against Dav'nalleous, referenced in-text.

label: Lise
summary: A Spirit Votary and Warped priestess of the Dark Mother, aged 129, who seeks revenge against the Church after mistreatment by a priest.

label: Lisieux
summary: County granted to Rollo.

label: Lismore
summary: See created in 1190, and Isle of Lismore.

label: Lists
summary: Hoardings marking starting points and site of jousting.

label: Literatus

label: Literatus Manor House
