label: Midsummer Fair
summary: Annual gathering held at the Motherhouse of the Covenant of the Icy North where Alpine magi trade and socialize, coinciding with informal and Quaesitorial tribunals.

label: Midusulf
summary: One of Birna's six apprentices, told to 'Lead,' founder of Clan Midusulf, whose name means 'mead-wolf' (bear) in Old Gothic.

label: Midwife
summary: An almost exclusively female practitioner whose Chirurgy skills are employed throughout pregnancy and childbirth, sometimes having her thumbs surgically removed to assist births.

label: Might Recovery Requires Vitality
summary: Major Supernatural Flaw requiring rest and a meal in a human community to regain Might.

label: Mighty Torrent of Water
summary: A Creo Aquam spell (Level 20) that sprays a jet of water at a target, dealing damage and potentially sending them flying back.

label: Mihalpi
summary: Primus of House Mercere, addressee of Thomas Verus's letter.

label: Mihalyi
summary: Insatella's father, the last Primus of Mercere, who replaced Aldico after the Schism War.

label: Miklos filius Kosma
summary: Faerie-blooded young Jerbiton magus at Journeys End, a musician and enchanted tailor married to Lyndsay.

label: Miklos's mandolin
summary: Magical mandolin won in Arcadia that commands living things through song lyrics.

label: Milan
summary: A north Italian city near the iron mines of the southern Alps, famous for armaments and its capacity to produce enormous numbers of weapons to order.

label: Milanese
summary: Milanese force and rivals that besieged Castro Selvaggio and were suspected in its fall.

label: Mild Aging
summary: A Minor General Virtue granting a +1 bonus to the Living Conditions Modifier on aging rolls and a +3 bonus to survive an aging crisis.

label: Miles de Levis
summary: Bailli of Cotentin, appointed 1215.

label: Militant Orders
summary: Orders of warrior monks established to aid the crusades; four major ones in 1220.

label: Military Order (Church Boon)
summary: Major Church Boon: the church is an outpost of a military order.

label: Military Orders
summary: Orders of knights whose heads attended Lateran IV; a church may be an outpost of one.

label: Milites Dei
summary: Bull of Eugenius III in 1145 clarifying Templar clergy rights.

label: Milites Templi
summary: Bull proclaimed by Celestine II in 1144 describing Templars as defenders of pilgrims.

label: Milk Brother
summary: A human who shared milk with a gwiber, gaining Animal Ken and a Faerie Friend bond with it.

label: Millards
summary: A court of Parisian argotiers who racketeer among peasants in the countryside.

label: Milo
summary: Second apprentice of Verditius who combined Boethius's philosophy with Germanic runes to invent Verditius Runes and discovered Hephaestus's torture chair at Ravenna.

label: Milo of Bonisagus
summary: An Archmage of House Bonisagus who prepared for his archmage contest while a member of Schola Pythagoranis, then joined Durenmar.

label: Milvi Antiquiti
summary: 'Kites of old', a Societas Merceris of Mutantes and companions who copy and lend ancient books, flying in hawk form.

label: Mimer the Old
summary: A minor deity in the Scandinavian pantheon from whom Wayland learned smith-craft techniques.

label: Mimic Dogs
summary: Creatures described by Roman writers that could be taught to repeat human actions; probably servant faeries destroyed by the Dominion.

label: Mimic the Christ's Miracle
summary: A cantation (low-level formulaic spell for apprentices) listed in the book's contents.

label: Mimicry
summary: Virtue named in the text, associated with Larta chefs, smiths, minstrels or muses.

label: Mimir
summary: Wise counselor of the gods, of Ymir's second, friendlier brood.

label: Mimizan
summary: A covenant in the Provençal Tribunal with only two members, one of whom is the Praeco Dama.

label: Mina
summary: Site of the hajj where pilgrims stone a column representing Satan.

label: Mind of the Beast
summary: A Muto Mentem spell (Level 30) with an Animal requisite that turns the target's mind into that of an animal of the caster's choice, with the victim acting like that animal.

label: Mind Suggestion
summary: Sluagh power (ReMe 30) implanting suggestions to kill or destroy what the target holds dear.

label: Mineral Rights
summary: Rights to resources beneath the ground, held by the lord or king.

label: Minerva
summary: A pagan goddess whose image in high relief is carved into rock just south of Chester and is said to continue to watch over the city.

label: Minerva Sulis
summary: Sleeping Romano-Celtic goddess of Bath; Faerie Might 25; grants requested vengeance via curse tablets.

label: Miniature
summary: A Flaw or Inferiority named among the traits of magical animals or dragons in this text.

label: Minister General
summary: Title of the leader of the Franciscans after Francis.

label: Ministeriales
summary: Unfree German knights who served in exchange for upkeep and are being absorbed into the hereditary knightly class.

label: Minnesingers
summary: A type of German minstrel copying the northern French style with emphasis on knightly combat and sensual love, exemplified by Walther and Wolfram.

label: Minor Allergy
summary: Cat power, a Sight-range version of Touch of the Goose Feather.

label: Minor Deficiency
summary: Flaw listed in character statistics in this text.

label: Minor Demon of Pride
summary: Demon attracted to a boy manipulated by a faerie queen in a story seed.

label: Minor Discomfort from Iron
summary: Flaw listed in character statistics in this text.

label: Minor Enchantments
summary: A Minor Supernatural Virtue giving the character items with magical powers designed as Hermetic enchantments totaling 25 levels or less.

label: Minor Flaw (Inferiority)
summary: Minor Inferiority granting a Minor General or Supernatural (Magic) Flaw.

label: Minor Knight
summary: Faerie with typical Might 10.

label: Minor Magic Deficiency
summary: Flaw appearing in a Roman Tribunal vocation template.

label: Minor Magical Deficiency
summary: Flaw appearing in character statistics or rules in this text.

label: Minor Magical Focus
summary: A Hermetic Virtue narrowing and strengthening a magus's magic; the range of a Supernatural Ability is meant to approximate one, and it is required for the Beast Masters tradition.

label: Minor Magical Focus in Certamen
summary: All Tremere magi have a Minor Magical Focus in Certamen, making them excellent duelists but limiting their power.

label: Minor Orders
summary: Clerks such as porters, lectors, exorcists and acolytes who need not be ordained.

label: Minor Potency
summary: A Virtue granted at the first Station of the Criamon Path of the Body, conferring potency in an aspect of the Art of Corpus.

label: Minor Rune Focus
summary: Minor Virtue: single-rune focus.

label: Minor Supernatural Ability
summary: A Virtue granting a minor supernatural power, gained by long-lived Durenmar covenfolk in their seventh decade.

label: Minority (Church Boon)
summary: Church Boon representing a minority community, such as Jews, attached to the parish.

label: Minotaur
summary: Immortal minotaur arena gladiator (Magic Might 10) lairing beneath the ruined amphitheater of the temple town.

label: Minster
summary: Older superior church with aristocratic patronage ruling subordinate churches; some persist in 1220.

label: Minstrel
summary: Musician using almost-magical music to affect emotions.

label: Miqveh
summary: Communal ritual bathhouse maintaining halakhic purity.

label: Mirabilia
summary: Monastic books recording faeries and magical or unusual natural phenomena, signs and wonders; a research resource for magi.

label: Miracle Need
summary: Modifier to a miracle's level based on how desperate or deserving the supplicant is, from Calamitous (-15) to Impious (+20).

label: Miracle of Our Lady of Boulogne
aliases: Miracle of Our Lady of Boulogne
summary: Apparition of the Virgin in 636 leading to a crewless boat bearing her statue, now a pilgrim relic.

label: Miracle Timeliness
summary: Modifier to a miracle's level based on how quickly it manifests, from Immediate (+10) to Generation (-20).

label: Miracles
summary: The direct intervention of God in the world, which can do anything, cannot fail, and cannot be resisted by any other power including creature Magic Resistance.

label: Miracula
summary: Monastic chronicles containing ghost stories of souls returned from purgatory and miracles of saints, read to foster Devotion and useful for research.

label: Miraculous Beer Mug
summary: Magical toy sold at the faerie toy market.

label: Miraculous Effects
summary: Limited but reliable supernatural effects produced by holy characters by combining a Method and a Power, rolled against a target level.

label: Miramolin
summary: King of Morocco who imprisoned and later killed Franciscan friars, whose remains the flames would not touch.

label: Miravet
summary: Significant Western Templar commandery in Aragon.

label: Mircalla
summary: Ghost of the Motherhouse, a mother murdered by a magus's grogs, immune to Hermetic magic and protective of mistreated apprentices.

label: Mirebeau
summary: Castle where Eleanor was besieged.

label: Miriam
summary: Flavius of Jerbiton's wife, of unclear cultural group and magical tradition; she attended the First Tribunal in an undescribed capacity and is buried beside Jerbiton.

label: Mirror of Lapis Crudus
summary: A magical mirror in a hut straddling the regio boundary, created by Mnemon; now the gate through which persons of like status swap places.

label: Mirror of Opposition
summary: A Muto Vim spell cast on another spell being cast, causing it to have the exact opposite of its normal effects; ten Form-specific versions exist.

label: Mirror of Souls
summary: Mirror in the Abyssal Pit that reveals and scries anyone named or sympathetically connected, with Penetration 50; a source of insight for Original Research.

label: Mirrors of the Soul
summary: Summa on Imaginem by Perpauca Bonisagi.

label: Mischievous Childhood
summary: A childhood template used as the starting point for the sample Verditius apprentice.

label: Miser's Midas
summary: Focus power turning any living thing the character touches, except himself, to stone.

label: Miser's Pot
aliases: Miser's Pot, Bane of the Hoarder
summary: An Accuser in the form of a small three-legged brass cauldron that punishes the greedy rich by stealing their wealth and dragging them to Hell.

label: Misfortune
summary: Ruchin Power making the target suffer bad luck and a -2 penalty on luck-based rolls.

label: Misguided Faeries
summary: Faeries representing fear of decrepitude and powerlessness who are attracted to people working in old age, including magi, but attack them ineffectively.

label: Misguided Traditions
summary: Infernal traditions deluded into believing they do good.

label: Mishneh Torah
summary: Maimonides' Summa on Rabbinic Law, the foremost authority.

label: Missal
summary: Tractatus in Church Lore and Music with the text for Mass; every church has one.

label: Missing Ear
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character cannot accurately locate the direction of sounds, suffering a penalty to hearing rolls.

label: Missing Equipment
summary: A Minor laboratory Outfittings Flaw: a lack of equipment makes one or two activity types totally impossible (-1 Upkeep).

label: Missing Eye
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character cannot judge close distances easily, penalizing missile, targeting, and melee attack rolls.

label: Missing Hand
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character has lost a hand, penalizing climbing, combat, and activities requiring both hands.

label: Missing Ingredients
summary: A Free laboratory Outfittings Flaw: a lack of certain ingredients severely hampers one Technique or two Forms, halving relevant Lab Totals (-1 Upkeep).

label: Missing Sanctum Marker
summary: A Free laboratory Outfittings Flaw: the sanctum marker is not prominently displayed or is missing, inviting Hermetic intrusion (-1 Aesthetics).

label: Mist Raising
summary: Hagbui power (CrAu 10) raising a corpse-smelling mist.

label: Mistaken Identity
summary: A Major Story Flaw in which someone who looks exactly like the character commits violent or embarrassing acts, forcing him to deal with the consequences.

label: Mistletoe of Virtue
summary: Parasitic herb of virtue that, when Enriched by taking root in the wearer's flesh, grants the Supernatural Ability Divination & Augury but also Fragile Constitution; unenriched worth 2 pawns of Intellego vis.

label: Mistletoe Sprig of Herbam Vis
summary: Mistletoe vis granting understanding of its forest.

label: Mistress Greta
summary: Elderly Gifted folk witch of Reims who escaped the stake by flying and now lives alone in a forest cave regio.

label: Mistridge
summary: Provençal covenant, Windgraven's traditional enemy, whose Magi aided the Sicilian Vespers.

label: Mists of Change
summary: A Muto Corpus ritual (Level 60) with an Animal requisite in which patches of mist transform anyone remaining in the target area into a random creature for a Year.

label: Mithras
summary: A luminous Persian-origin sun god worshiped by the Cult of Mithras as savior of Creation and divine Bull-Slayer; Castra Solis is named for his sun-god aspect.

label: Mithridates VI
summary: King of Pontus and enemy of Rome who employed Crateuas as court physician; his potions let him survive poison and torture.

label: Mitigating Deadly Wounds
summary: Optional rule letting a player reduce a wound's severity by accepting a new Flaw.

label: Mitigation of Realm Interaction Effects
summary: Learned-magician rules for reducing penalties from Divine or Infernal auras via Entreat the Powers.

label: Mittenwald
summary: Town listed in the Tribunal index.

label: Mitzvot
summary: Religious commandment; commanding a golem to transgress one risks madness.

label: Mjollnir
summary: Thor's hammer, a thunderbolt imprisoned in iron that inflicts +30 lightning damage.

label: Mnemon of Tytalus
summary: Rego master of Lapis Crudus who created the mirror gate and renegotiated with Candidus.

label: Moat Monster
summary: A creature serving as a Local Ally for the Military Camp covenant situation, also referenced as a covenant Boon.

label: Mob Football
summary: Peasant football played on festive days with unlimited players and few rules, winners getting the ball to a designated spot.

label: Mobile
summary: A Free laboratory Structure Virtue: the entire lab can be readily moved, e.g. on a ship or cart, usually taken with the Unstable Flaw (+1 Experimentation).

label: Mogidell
summary: Great Spirit of Ushant of mists and sea-fog, appearing as a huge gray bird.

label: Mohammad
summary: Prophet to whom the Qur'an was communicated, commemorated on the Night of Destiny.

label: Molech
summary: Prince of the False Gods (Might 50, Ignem), King of Fire who first lit Hell's fires; worshiped in Tyre and Carthage as Moloch with child sacrifice.

label: Moles Magna
summary: Vassal of Oleron (1136-1182) built within a dam on the edge of the Morvan, destroyed when the dam burst.

label: Molosser
summary: Large Roman dogs forming the basis of the St. Bernard breed.

label: Moly
summary: Magical plant shown to Odysseus by Hermes.

label: Monarchs of the Veiled Court
summary: Second degree of the Volshebnii Mechtateli who maintain the dream of the Vermilion Temple and may enter its innermost chambers.

label: Monasteries
summary: Self-sufficient religious houses governed by a Rule, dominated by an abbey church.

label: Monastery
summary: Religious house; the Inheritance seed's monastery has Divine aura 4.

label: Monastery of St. John of the Vines
aliases: Monastery of St. John of the Vines
summary: Rich abbey in Soissons founded in the 11th century under royal patronage.

label: Monastery of St. Remigius
summary: Eighth-century monastery and basilica over the grave of St. Remigius in Reims.

label: Monastic Enclosure
summary: Rule of enclosure and stability of abode that Francis' preachers ignore.

label: Monastic Gardens
summary: Monastic horticulture including cloister garth, orchards, physic garden, infirmary garden and herbers.

label: Monastic Vows
summary: A Major Story Flaw in which the character has taken vows of poverty, chastity, and obedience to a religious superior, as a friar, monk, or nun.

label: Monastic Vows (Flaw)
summary: Story Flaw for religious characters living outside their community where keeping vows is a struggle.

label: Monastic Vows (Hermetic)
summary: Major Hermetic Flaw: vows of poverty, chastity and obedience; the magus cannot own vis, possesses only functional magic devices, and may be barred from binding a familiar. All Neriusians take it.

label: Moncontour
summary: Market town.

label: Monferrato of Quaesitor
summary: Associate Quaesitor member of Magvillus who avoids its politics.

label: Mongol Horde
summary: Force gathering far to the East that will bear down upon Mythic Europe.

label: Mongol Saber
summary: Mongol variation on the long sword.

label: Mongols
summary: Invaders against whom the 1245 council calls a crusade; can cause a diocese to be in partibus infidelium.

label: Monica Ierne
summary: The second-in-command of House Tremere, an Archmaga and master of combat magic originally from the Stonehenge Tribunal who serves as an excellent field commander.

label: Monistic Mysticism
summary: Mystical path of losing the self in the oneness of God, requiring Visions or True Faith; its Divine Ascent takes the form of Divine Gloom.

label: Monition
summary: Official warning, usually for first-time offenders.

label: Monk
summary: Male religious living under a rule in a monastery.

label: Monk of the Scottish Church
summary: Companion template: a monk of the Scottish Church who left his monastery after it was annexed to the Cistercians.

label: Monkey
summary: Pet with game statistics.

label: Monksend Castle
summary: Castle built by David Goulis from 1187 on Benedictine monastery lands, reputed haunted.

label: Mons Graupius
summary: Battle of A.D. 84 where Romans defeated the Caledonians.

label: Monster's Hole
summary: Dragon pit.

label: Monstrosity
summary: (Form) Monstrosity Flaw developed by warped spice trees.

label: Monstrous Appearance
summary: Major Social Interaction Flaw giving -6 in social situations where appearance matters.

label: Monstrous Blood
summary: A Minor Supernatural Flaw in which the character's essential nature has been changed through exposure to the Magic realm, giving her true form unfortunate supernatural properties and a visible deformity, while granting a -1 bonus to Aging rolls.

label: Monstrous Form
summary: Death shark flaw.

label: Mont Auxois
summary: Site of Alesia with a Magic aura and haunted temple to Matres.

label: Mont Joux
summary: The tallest summit in Europe, called Mons Iovis by the Romans after Jupiter Pennius; site of the Covenant Where Journeys End (later known as Mont Blanc).

label: Mont Maudit
summary: The 'Accursed Mountain', second-highest peak of the Mont Joux ridge, where Bernard of Menthon chained or destroyed the demon worshipped as Jupiter.

label: Mont Saint Michel
summary: Abbey whose quarry stone resembles Confluensis' buildings.

label: Mont St. Michael
summary: Benedictine monastery founded by the archangel Michael; enters a Divine regio (aura 8) at high tide.

label: Mont St. Michel
summary: Isle at the Normandy border.

label: Montagne de Reims
summary: Hilly forested limestone plateau south of Reims with chasms, wild beasts and vis sources.

label: Monte Cassino
summary: Italian monastery from which St. Benedict's remains were moved.

label: Montferrand
summary: Town around the Count of Auvergne's castle, rival of Clermont.

label: Montferrat
summary: City refusing to join the Lombard League.

label: Monticelli
summary: Community near Florence founded by Agnes in 1219 and addressed by Ugolino's rule.

label: Montjoy
summary: Templar castle in Aragon.

label: Montmartre
summary: Hill north of Paris named for the martyrdom of St. Denis, formerly Mons Mercurius.

label: Montpellier
summary: A famed southern medical school where Gilles de Corbeil taught before leaving amid feuding with the faculty; one of the schools granting the Magister in Medicina.

label: Montserrat
summary: Mountain above Barcelona, possible Grail resting place.

label: Montverte
summary: A covenant in the Normandy Tribunal occupying a castle with curtain walls and mural towers, which it shares with its mundane lord and uses as a base for raiding permitted by that tribunal's Peripheral Code.

label: Monzón
summary: Templar castle in Aragon.

label: Moonbeam
summary: A Creo Ignem spell (Level 3) that causes a gentle reading-bright light to shine down and illuminate the area encircled by the caster's arms.

label: Moorish magicians
summary: Shadowy tradition of North African magicians with tentative links to Jerbiton magi of Iberia.

label: Moors
summary: Moorish lands where Giacomo met charm casters; they hold alchemical texts.

label: Morag
summary: A giant driven from his mountain home by diabolists who has taken to robbery near a covenant, holding a captured knight hostage in a cave; he craves revenge against the diabolists.

label: Moral Evil
summary: An act of free will against the moral order prescribed by God; the only kind of evil that constitutes sin.

label: Moral Virtues
summary: Also Capital or Cardinal virtues (Justice, Fortitude, Temperance, Wisdom) that moderate fleshly desire.

label: Morale
summary: Roll from Chapter Nine: Optional Combat Rules made by a losing commander; failure may leave groups Disordered or Routed.

label: Morale and Discipline
summary: Optional rules that weaken groups while making the leader more important, requiring Discipline and Morale rolls in battle.

label: Morale Roll
summary: A reaction roll (leader's Presence + Leadership + stress die) made when bad things happen on the battlefield; failure disorders or routs the group.

label: Moratamis of House Guernicus
summary: A maga of House Guernicus who, suspicious of Carolus of Tytalus, challenges him to certamen but ultimately concedes; an Intellego and Mentem specialist in the certamen example.

label: Moravia
summary: The eastern March of Bohemia bordered by the Carpathian Mountains and Hungary, through which flows the River Morava; home of the covenant of Roznov.

label: Moray
summary: Northern region ruled by MacBeth and Lulach's descendants.

label: Morgan
summary: Welsh freshwater merman nursery terror.

label: Morgan Le Fay
summary: Half-sister of King Arthur who imprisoned Guyomart in the Valley of No Return.

label: Morgana
summary: The faerie who kept Ogier as a lover in Avalon, rejuvenated him with a ring, and later recaptured him.

label: Morgana Le Fay
summary: Enchantress said to be Oberon's mother and Ogier's captor.

label: Morgat
summary: Caves.

label: Moricus the Short
summary: One of the early followers of Francis.

label: Morienus Romanus
summary: Author of Liber de Compositione Alchemiae.

label: Morlen of Merinita
summary: A young Merinita magus among the members recruited to Nigrasaxa.

label: Mormaer
summary: Great steward; the seven mormaers became earls.

label: Mormo
summary: Possessing faerie that bites naughty children, once a mother turned werewolf.

label: Morning Star
summary: Ability appearing in character or covenant library statistics in the Roman Tribunal.

label: Morning Star Attack
summary: Ability listed in a Roman Tribunal vocation template.

label: Morningstar of the Virulent Flame
summary: CrIg 30 spell known by Verox.

label: Moro
summary: Vampires created from exposed children, shape of death's head moth.

label: Morocco
summary: Destination of early Franciscan missions where friars were martyred in 1220.

label: Moroi
summary: Leti leading the doomed to fated demise, led by Moros.

label: Moros
summary: Leader of the Moroi.

label: Morphea
summary: A dream maga used in examples who explores dreams, fights a demon and a diabolist dream traveler, and physically enters a dream.

label: Morrigan
summary: Old goddess, a powerful faerie whose descendants may bear Faerie God Blood.

label: Morrighu the Screech-Hag
summary: The Screech-Hag, an Aerial Power demon of warfare with a crow's body and an old woman's upper parts, who claims to have been a Faerie goddess of victory.

label: Mortal Sin
summary: An act that assists the Infernal or does not serve God, staining the soul; divided into mortal (major) and venial (minor) sins.

label: Mortuary
summary: A charge always levied on the dying to make things right between the Church and a dying thief (described in Chapter Six: Manorial Fiefs).

label: Mortuary Mass
summary: Funeral Mass for the living believed to kill them; an Infernal rite.

label: Mortuary Society of Kassala
summary: A society in Kassala, Alodia that makes Kassalan Dust and practices Kassalan Exorcism rites against ghosts and the physical dead.

label: Morum of Tytalus
summary: Arabic Tytalus serving Magvillus as an enforcing associate member; bitter enemy of Verox.

label: Morwena of Ex Miscellanea
summary: Magus who in 1030 A.A. charged Darius of Guernicus with a thirty-year vendetta against her.

label: Moses
summary: Led the Hebrews from Egypt and commanded Rahab to part the Red Sea; God parted it Himself when Moses' power was insufficient.

label: Moshe ben Isaac
summary: Example kabbalist who creates the golem Isaac to protect his community from a corrupt tax collector.

label: Mosque
summary: Muslim building for communal prayer with a Dominion aura of 4 or 5.

label: Mosque of the Prophet
summary: First mosque, in Medina, housing the tombs of Muhammad, Fatima, Abu Bakr and 'Umar; Dominion aura 9.

label: Mosul
summary: Persian city north of which the Mulhidun live.

label: Mother (foreman elf)
summary: A protective foreman elf.

label: Mother of Winds
summary: Bearded old woman with four giant sons she keeps in order with her sack.

label: Mother Road
summary: The source of all roads, identified with the Faerie Realm itself, used to traverse vast distances swiftly via trods.

label: Motherhouse of the Covenant of the Icy North
aliases: Motherhouse of the Covenant of the Icy North
summary: The Bavarian seat of the Covenant of the Icy North, effectively a Guernicus house covenant of Quaesitores who manage the Bavarian Common and host the Tribunal and the Midsummer Fair.

label: Motion Sickness
summary: A Minor General Flaw causing the character to become violently ill when riding a horse, in a cart, or sailing, doubling fatigue loss on long journeys.

label: Motovun Forest
summary: Forest on Istria where white truffles grow.

label: Motte-and-Bailey
summary: Castle of an artificial mound with a wooden tower overlooking a palisaded courtyard (bailey).

label: Mougau-Bihan
summary: Giant's tomb.

label: Mount Ararat
summary: Mountain on whose top the dragon Vishap resides.

label: Mount Beauvray
summary: Mount.

label: Mount Blanik
summary: A mountain covered by a Divine regio, with an underground cavern holding the sleeping army of St. Wenceslaus, the Knights of Blanik, awaiting Bohemia's direst need.

label: Mount Carmel
summary: Mountain in the Holy Land where Carmelite hermits live in caves around Elijah's well.

label: Mount Dindymon
summary: The mountain on Bear Island atop which the Temenos of Dindyméné lies and beneath which the titaness Dindyméné is bound.

label: Mount Dol
summary: Granite outcrop sacred to druids, site of Branugurix.

label: Mount Etna
summary: A volcano on the island of Sicily beneath which the fire spirit Adranus slumbers; believed by the ancients to hold a gateway to the Underworld, it last erupted in 1194.

label: Mount Harder
summary: Mountain bearing the face of the Harder Man.

label: Mount Klapsi
summary: Western mountain of Bear Island, wooded wilderness with boars, bears and lions.

label: Mount Lycaeon
summary: Associated with a ritual rumored to turn men into wolves for nine years.

label: Mount Lykaion
summary: Mountain in Arcadia where the lykaia rite took place.

label: Mount Mercury
summary: Highest point in the Vendée with a church on a Mercury shrine, a Redcap pilgrimage site.

label: Mount of Olives
summary: Site outside Jerusalem where Rabi'a is buried.

label: Mount Olympus
summary: The mountain home of the Greek gods from which Hephaestus was twice cast out; also the location of an all-Verditius covenant and a Forge of Hephaestus.

label: Mount Pilatus
summary: A mountain in the Alps where climbing can generate terrible storms, cited as an example of a Site of Weakness Hook.

label: Mount Purgatory
summary: A mountain commonly believed to sit at the center of the antipodal region directly opposite Jerusalem, atop Hell, a place of contrition and repentance.

label: Mount Radhost
summary: A 3700-foot summit in Moravia, site of a crude stone temple to Radegast with a Magic aura of 6 (secretly Infernal), where a great festival fuelled by human sacrifice yields vis for Roznov's magi.

label: Mount Saint Michael
summary: Place where Saint Keyne's brother lived and she left a magical chair.

label: Mount Saint Odile
summary: A mountain in the northern Vosges housing the convent of St. Odile and a holy spring with a Divine aura of 4, a place of pilgrimage especially for those with eye diseases.

label: Mount Sinai
summary: Holy site with high Dominion (5-10) and terrestrial regiones.

label: Mount Tabor
summary: Site of the transfiguration where Joachim meditated for forty days.

label: Mount Triglav
summary: Mountain in Slovenia home of the Zlatorog.

label: Mountain Giants
summary: Norse giants associated with Terram who have Terram Resistance.

label: Mountain of Blood
summary: Field of Purgatory where the violent are blasted by icy wind and hurled into a river of filth.

label: Mountains of Qaf
summary: Homeland of the jinn thought to surround the world, likely within Arcadia.

label: Mountaintop
summary: A Free laboratory Structure Virtue: the lab sits at a mountain peak, a dramatic remote setting prone to winds and snows (-1 Safety, +1 Upkeep, +2 Aesthetics, +2 Auram).

label: Mounted Archery
summary: Rules for shooting from horseback, relevant to the horse bow.

label: Mounted Combat
summary: Rules giving riders bonuses to Attack and Defense and a separate action for the steed.

label: Mournful Mound
summary: A hill containing the barrow of the Black Serpent, reached beyond the court of the sons of the King of Suffering, where Peredur slew the serpent.

label: Mouse of Virtue
summary: A mouse born spontaneously from the soil, able to gnaw iron.

label: Mouth of Hell
summary: Entrance to Hell in Purgatory, a mountain-sized beast's mouth guarded by two seraphim.

label: Moving Objects with the Mind
summary: Cat power, a Sight-range version of Unseen Arm.

label: Mu'adhdhin
summary: Mosque attendant who summons the faithful to prayer; basis of the Devout Mu'adhdhin grog template.

label: Mu'tazilis
summary: Muslim theological school stressing free will and a created Qur'an; briefly favored then banned in 1017 and 1041.

label: Muhammad
summary: Prophet of Islam born at Mecca c. 570, recipient of the Qur'an; the most revered holy forbear with Divine Might 100.

label: Muhammad al-Basri
summary: Shaykh who miraculously found a woman's dowry certificate.

label: Muhammad al-Mahdi
summary: Twelfth imam of the Twelvers, in occultation until he returns as the mahdi.

label: Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i
summary: Founder of the Shafi'i school of law (d. 820), buried in Cairo; holy forbear with Divine Might 25.

label: Muhammad ibn Jarir al-Tabari
summary: Author of Jami' al-Bayan (d. 923).

label: Muilearteach
summary: A sea giantess who comes ashore in storms as a begging hag and devours those who shelter her; she has a pot of healing ointment.

label: Muireartach
summary: The Pictish goddess of sea storms.

label: Muirgheal
summary: A Quaesitor who led the Order's investigation into the Normandy restless-dead crisis and invited the Gifted Donatores to join the Order en masse.

label: Mulhidun
summary: Infernal tradition of devil-worshipers near Mosul and Seljuk lands who revere Enais, the Peacock Angel, and summon and command demons as servants.

label: Mull
summary: Southern island group granted to Somerled in 1156.

label: Mulsum
summary: Honeyed wine served with the first remove.

label: Multiheaded Giants
summary: Giants found across Mythic Europe whose heads each have their own personality, making them either easily confused or incredibly cunning.

label: Multure
summary: Fee of a proportion of the grain milled, paid by millers renting mills.

label: Mummel Lake
summary: An enchanted isolated lake near Seebach in the Black Forest, home to a Nixe (water-nymph) whose jealous elemental spirits may slay the mortals she bewitches.

label: Mummers
summary: Masked bands who parade, beg or perform traditional plays during Christmas; faeries use the role to enter human lands.

label: Mundane Beasts
summary: Beasts of Mythic Europe with no Might and no vis, using Cunning instead of Intelligence.

label: Mundane Politics
summary: Covenant Hook: the covenant is deeply embroiled in mundane politics.

label: Mundane raiding
summary: Normandy tradition that raiding mundane resources is not a Hermetic crime.

label: Mungan Mor
summary: Magus Ex Miscellanea of Mac Gruagach trained as an animal mage, master of the clan's herds who drives them to the Lowlands each autumn.

label: Munich
summary: City listed in the Tribunal index.

label: Munkar
summary: One of the two Questioners, Throne angels who examine the Muslim dead in their graves about Muhammad and punish unbelievers.

label: Munkar and Nakir
summary: The Questioners, example angels.

label: Munsalvaesche
summary: Castle where Parsifal places the Grail, guarded by templeisen.

label: Munster
summary: A prosperous market and episcopal city on the Munsterland plain, founded as a monastery in 805 to convert the Saxons.

label: Muqta
summary: A Major Social Status Virtue for an important emir entrusted with an iqta', a feudal-like fief, following the Landed Noble rules.

label: Muqta' of Baghdad
summary: Powerful patron protecting the Radhanite merchant.

label: Murderous Woodland
summary: ReHe 55 Boundary ritual that wakens every tree on the island to walk and fight on command.

label: Murdrum
summary: A fine on a community where a secretly killed person cannot be proven English rather than Norman.

label: Murion
summary: Prima of House Bonisagus and Praeco of the Rhine Tribunal, a powerful and overbearing archmagus who presents her plan to recolonize the Rhine Gorge to the new magi at the Forum of Durenmar.

label: Murmur of the Deep
summary: Atlantean power to hear from any point in the same water-way.

label: Muscaria
summary: Practical Criamon maga who developed the Cave's mushroom farms; her predecessors expect her to become the next Prima.

label: Muse
summary: A title for any supernatural entity from the four realms that attaches itself to a prominent artist, granting Virtues, powers, and Warping in exchange for promoting its interests, eventually carrying the artist to its home realm.

label: Muslim Calendar
summary: Lunar calendar dating from the hijra of 622.

label: Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj
summary: Compiler of Sahih Muslim (d. 875).

label: Muspelheim
summary: The fiery prison where the fire giants dwell.

label: Muspelli
summary: Non-Hermetic tradition whose childhoods the book does not specifically address.

label: Mustard Plaster
summary: A Theriac of Level 5, Potency Moderate, a linen cloth with ground mustard seeds that grants +3 to Wound Recovery rolls for Medium and Light Wounds by drawing out choler.

label: Mutable Devices
summary: A discovery from Heron of Alexandria's Mechanica allowing characters to scavenge spun vis and use its capacity in new enchantments.

label: Mutable Gender
summary: A demonic power allowing a demon to switch gender at will.

label: Mutable Virtue
summary: Astrological variant of a Virtue or Flaw applying only in the mutable signs; Major becomes Minor, Minor effects doubled.

label: Mutable Virtue or Flaw
summary: Rule option listed among the Curious Common Magics.

label: Mutantes
summary: Mercere lineage descended from Mutantus practicing Mutantum Magic ('magic-taming').

label: Mutantum Magic
summary: Minor Hermetic Virtue for descendants of the Mutantes allowing Boosted, Harnessed and Tethered spells and items.

label: Mutantus
summary: Great-grandson of Triceres who studied transformation magic and trained the first Mutantes.

label: Mute
summary: A Major General Flaw in which the character cannot speak; magi with this Flaw take a -10 penalty to all spellcasting unless offset by the Quiet Magic Virtue.

label: Muto
summary: Technique meaning 'I transform'. Changes a target into something unnatural to itself.

label: Muzdalifa
summary: Stopping place between 'Arafat and Mina during the hajj.

label: My covenant will I not break, nor alter the thing that is gone out of my lips
aliases: My covenant will I not break, nor alter the thing that is gone out of my lips
summary: Invocation Adjuration effect (Level 20) binding both parties to the terms of a bargain with a supernatural being.

label: My heart is inditing a good matter
aliases: My heart is inditing a good matter
summary: Invocation Blessing effect (Level 20) granting the Free Expression Virtue for a day.

label: My New Best Friend
summary: A Creo Mentem 25 spell of Henri de Tours that makes a target believe the caster is an old friend by substituting the caster for one of the target's real friends.

label: Myanar
summary: A figure who challenged Quendalon for leadership of the cult of Diana and was slain by him; his followers fled to House Bjornaer and founded the rival secret cult that became the Huntress.

label: Mynyddawg Mwynfawr
summary: Lord of Caereidyn whose 300-strong war band Aneirin praised.

label: Myomancy
summary: Divinatory method using behavior of mice and rats, listed among Ceremonial Augury Phenomena.

label: Myrina
summary: Current Evangelium, living at Dragon's Rest.

label: Myrmecoleon
summary: A mythical creature whose exoskeleton provides a Shape and Material bonus of +6 to deprivation and starvation effects.

label: Mystagogue
summary: A charismatic Mystery Cult figure who commands a probationer and grants Initiation; Criamon usually use guides instead, though the Paths of Mirror and Strife use formal Mystagogues.

label: Mysterious Path
summary: Potentate power creating an instantly traversable path between two locations.

label: Mystery Cult
summary: Organizations that teach a mystery; four Houses of the Order of Hermes (Bjornaer, Criamon, Merinita, Verditius) are Mystery Cults whose members are Initiated into Outer and deeper Inner Mysteries.

label: (Mystery Cult) Lore
summary: An (Organization) Lore Ability for a particular Mystery Cult, covering its legends, history, structure, rites, secret passwords, and Initiation ceremonies.

label: Mystery Effect
summary: Enchantment outside Hermetic theory usable only as part of a Mystery ritual.

label: Mystery Houses
summary: The four Houses of Criamon, Bjornaer, Merinita, and Verditius, the smallest of the 12 Houses, which tend to look inward.

label: Mystery of Ascendancy to the Hall of Heroes
aliases: Ascendancy to the Hall of Heroes
Mystery Ascendancy to the Hall of Heroes
Mystery of Ascendancy to the Hall of Heroes
summary: Major Hermetic Mystery Virtue requiring Hermetic Theurgy, teaching a path of apotheosis by which a hierarch ascends as a Daimon to the Hall of Heroes with the aid of celebrants.

label: Mystery of Becoming
summary: Mystery preferred by faerie magi to becoming minor faeries in Stone Couches.

label: Mystery of Divination
summary: A Major Virtue acquired through Clan Ilfetu's Trial and Oath of the Prophet, alongside the Visions Flaw.

label: Mystery of Divination and Augury
aliases: Esoteric Mystery of Divination and Augury
summary: An Esoteric Mystery into which Clan Ilfetu members may be Initiated, teaching the haemagmomancy divination method.

label: Mystery of Hermetic Synthemata
summary: The Mystery into which a new hierophant of the Huntress is Initiated, vital to controlling the pagan messiah they hope to create.

label: Mystery of the Anima
summary: A Major House Mystery of House Bjornaer that transforms the heartbeast into a spiritual or elemental form composed of an element such as earth, fire, air, water, smoke, or shadow.

label: Mystery of the Epitome
summary: A Major House Mystery of House Bjornaer that perfects the heartbeast into a Beast of Virtue, granting Characteristic bonuses, Mythic Feats, and immunity to physical Flaws in inner form.

label: Mystery Virtues
summary: Virtues gained through Initiation into Mysteries; they can be taught to non-Initiates only under special circumstances such as a Minor Breakthrough.

label: Mystic
summary: Those dedicating their lives to pursuit of the love of God through contemplative or monistic mysticism.

label: Mystic Fraternity of Samos
summary: A Pythagorean Mystery Cult organized into degrees that teach planetary, geometric and theurgic Virtues; its Inner Order members run publicly known Schools.

label: Mystic Nun
summary: Companion template of a noble-born nun whose mystical visions inspire verses studied by theologians.

label: Mystic Tower
summary: Crusader base conjured in Iceland's southeastern highlands and protected by the Aegis of the Hearth, later assaulted by the giants.

label: Mystical Choreography
summary: A Minor Hermetic Virtue letting a magus perform Ceremonial Magic faster (five minutes per magnitude, or one minute in a prepared space) through skilled body movement.

label: Mythic Alchemists
summary: Alternate learned tradition that creates potions, powders and pastilles rather than charms.

label: Mythic Alchemy
summary: Major Supernatural Virtue and Ability allowing magical transmutation of substances, preparing superior craft materials and extracting vis.

label: Mythic Blood
summary: A Virtue marking descent from a supernatural ancestor such as Birna or a Great Beast, granting a magical feat spell, a Minor Magical Focus, and a hereditary Personality Flaw.

label: Mythic Blood (Zmey)
summary: Major Hermetic Virtue from descent from a zmey, granting a Minor Magical Focus with Storms and an innate power of invisibility, flight, or shapechange.

label: Mythic Cathay
summary: Distant land to which emissaries went.

label: Mythic (Characteristic)
summary: Minor Heroic Virtue granting a specialty for a positive Characteristic.

label: Mythic Companion
summary: A powerful tier of player character that may take up to 10 points of Flaws and twice the normal Virtues, defined by a Free Virtue specifying which type of Mythic Companion they are.

label: Mythic Companion Virtue
summary: Free Virtue specifying a Mythic Companion's status; incompatible with The Gift.

label: Mythic Europe
summary: The setting of Ars Magica: an early-13th-century Europe in which the myths and superstitions of the age are literally true. Magi of the Order of Hermes wield potent magic from covenants hidden across the continent, while faeries, demons, angels and magical beasts inhabit the wider world.

label: Mythic Europe Lore
summary: Ability appearing in character or covenant library statistics in this text.

label: Mythic Feat
summary: An automatically successful incredible action a Beast of Virtue may perform at the cost of a confidence Point, covering feats of Perception, Presence, Strength, and other Characteristics.

label: Mythic Germany
summary: The magic-soaked lands of medieval Germany within the Holy Roman Empire, birthplace of the Order of Hermes and setting of the Rhine Tribunal.

label: Mythic Herbalism
summary: A Major Supernatural Virtue and Ability that lets a character create healing unguents, poultices, virulent poisons, and physical-bonus potions.

label: Mythic Mimicry
summary: Major Heroic Virtue to memorize accounts of any length and mimic voices or handwriting.

label: Mythic Pennies
summary: Currency hoarded by Nicholas.

label: Mythic Places
summary: Rare remaining magical and mysterious sites in Italy.

label: Mythic Pound
summary: The standardized currency unit used for prices in Ars Magica, equivalent to a pound of silver, a typical peasant's annual income, or a year's upkeep of an average Hermetic laboratory.

label: Mythic Presence
summary: Virtue often held by those of Carolingian blood.

label: Nátt-thel
summary: 'Darkest part of night'; vitki equivalent of Twilight losing The Gift.

label: Nátt-thel Prone
summary: Major Flaw: Nátt-thel on single botch.

label: Naameh
summary: One of the four demon wives of Iblis, a demon of prostitution.

label: Nagging Curse
summary: PeCo 20 spell cracking a tooth's enamel to cause distracting pain.

label: Nails of the Cuckold's Vengeance
summary: Andrew's Power causing stabbing nail-like pains.

label: Nain
summary: Infernal imp-like guardians of the Carnac stones, once korrigan, who lure victims with false treasure and deadly dances.

label: Nakir
summary: One of the two Questioners, Throne angels who examine the Muslim dead in their graves about Muhammad and punish unbelievers.

label: Name hiding
summary: Means by which powerful beings hide their synthemata, reducing research points; typically Might/2.

label: Nameless Covenant
summary: A Díedne covenant established on an ancient druidic shrine on Anglesey in 817, destroyed in 1011 and stricken from the records by the quaesitores after the Schism War.

label: Nameless Rock
summary: Magic Thing island east of South Wamses, conspiring to join with it.

label: Nameless Runes
summary: Minor Virtue: cast without name.

label: Names of Power
summary: Minor Hermetic Mystery Virtue of name magic; Names of Power add bonuses to Casting Score for spells matching their scope, limited by Magic Theory.

label: Nantes
summary: City on the River Loire, political and ecclesiastical center and capital of the duchy of Brittany; its cathedral is a site of martyrdom from 843.

label: Nanteuil
summary: Knights Templar priory in the Montagne de Reims, possibly a Divine regio.

label: Naonhaithya
summary: Lord of the Vessels of Iniquity, the Zoroastrian daeva of rebellion and irreverence who spreads anarchy and the corruption of good rulership.

label: Naples
summary: A city whose catacombs harbored the necromancer Guorna the Fetid and her tradition, which Tytalus and Tremere destroyed.

label: Naples Covenant
summary: Covenant founded in Naples by apprentices of Literatus that continues Literatus' work after its disbanding.

label: Narisian
summary: Head of Sansaron, abrupt and unwelcoming to Tamgor.

label: Narquois
summary: A court of Parisian argotiers who are pensioned soldiers extorting with threats.

label: Narrative Map
summary: Tarragon Vale's device displaying the underlying structures of mystical realms.

label: Narrowly Cognizant
summary: A Free Virtue indicating a faerie is aware of its faerie nature in a limited way; it tries to play its role accurately and cannot break role even unto death.

label: Nasir
summary: A minor angel of the Divine realm (Divine Might 25, Corpus) charged with the safety of pious travellers, who aids those in need before vanishing. He has powers such as Calming Touch, Spirit Form, Steadying Hand, and Subtle Form.

label: Natalis Invicti
summary: Day honoring the sun god's birth (December 25), adopted for the celebration of Christ's birth.

label: Nathanael
summary: Archangel whose servants guard the Treasury of the Four Winds.

label: Native Language
summary: Ability used by young characters, e.g. in example childhoods and sample characters.

label: Natrix
summary: The filius of Lacerta in a Clan Arelie sept in Iberia.

label: Natt
summary: Daughter of Mimir and Urd, the all-enshrouding night.

label: Natt-thel Prone
summary: Flaw of Eirik Svennson, a vitkir susceptibility.

label: Natura Antiqua
summary: A covenant of nature magi founded in the East Anglian fens in 1133, destroyed by Geoffrey de Mandeville during the Civil War in 1143.

label: Natura Antiqua Cult Lore
summary: Example new Mystery Cult Lore.

label: Natural Appearance
summary: Major Quality letting a magic character look like a normal human or living creature.

label: Natural Environment
summary: A Major laboratory Structure Virtue: natural scenery such as forest, desert, or river is in or around the lab, granting Aesthetics and terrain-appropriate Specializations.

label: Natural Leader
summary: A Minor General Virtue giving a +3 bonus to social situations where the dominant character takes the lead, partly overcoming the social penalty of The Gift.

label: Natural Magician
summary: A practitioner of non-Hermetic natural magic; Amabel the Learned is one, as powerful as many Hermetic magi, and some churchmen have begun employing such magicians.

label: Natural Measures
summary: Measures based on the body or nature, such as salmon 'as thick as a man's wrist', which generally favor the lord.

label: Natural Philosophy
summary: Arts open to Jewish scholars distrustful of magic.

label: Natural Sciences
summary: Book Two of the Epistles; Philosophiae tractatus and Elementalist Water summa.

label: Natural Tether
summary: A tether consisting of perfect natural features or astrological alignments, scoring 1 or 2, such as caves, forests, ice, volcanoes, water or wind.

label: Nature Lore
summary: A Mystery (Virtue) Initiated by the Vestals with the unique focus of lares (household spirits), letting them interact with the faeries of a settlement as nature magi do with the wilderness.

label: Nature Wizard
summary: A variant of Elemental Magic affecting Herbam rather than Ignem.

label: Nauarchos
summary: Tremere naval officers of the House fleet.

label: Nauche-Fleur
summary: Covenant accused in 1095 of feudal obligation to a baron via an unGifted companion; found innocent.

label: Naudiz
summary: Elder Futhark rune "Need" used as a vitkir Art. Very negative rune of hardship and need; can delay or bind other rune effects.

label: Naumburg
summary: A well-fortified town high above the River Saale with its own bishop, beginning construction of a cathedral dedicated to St. Peter and St. Paul.

label: Naval Koerakoonlased
summary: Peaceful farming koerakoonlased on an island found by Kalevipoeg, who became fishers.

label: Nazareth
summary: Mary's hometown.

label: Nebelkönigin
summary: A magically enhanced ship, pride of Waddenzee's pirate fleet, stolen from Oculus Septentrionalis (built by the Verditius shipwright Marcus) while it carried vis and magical books.

label: Nebuchadnezzar
summary: Conqueror of Jerusalem in 587 BC who destroyed the First Temple.

label: Necessary Condition
summary: A Flaw imposed as a Great Beast's Ordeal requiring a condition for magic (e.g., a bull chimera touching the ground); also a common Bjornaer flaw when in human or heartbeast form.

label: Necessary (Realm) Aura for (Ability)
summary: A Minor Supernatural Flaw giving a -3 penalty to a particular Ability when the character is not in the appropriate supernatural aura.

label: Necessity
summary: The underlying laws of the universe in Criamon cosmology that forced the immortals into the cycle of time for three eternities.

label: Nechtan
summary: King of the Picts who accepted the Roman Church in 710.

label: Nechtan Dubh
summary: Gruagach of Mac Gruagach trained by Brude Deathless, a descendant and favorite student of Brude, free with his Curses and Gifts.

label: Nechtan Mac Brude
summary: Pictish gruagach, son of Brude Deathless, who led Clan Mac Gruagach in 814 and kept it neutral; died in 987.

label: Necromancer
summary: Magus vocation (Ex Miscellanea) trained in the catacombs of Vardian's Tomb in necromancy.

label: Necromancers of Vardian's Tomb
summary: Ex Miscellanea magi invited into Vardian's Tomb who proved to be necromancers, in conflict with the Jerbiton founders.

label: Necromancy
summary: Originally conversing with the dead; by the 13th century covering evocation of spirits and demons.

label: Necromantic cult
summary: Tremere's ancestral necromantic tradition, which made lairs under cities like Naples.

label: Necropolis Regio
summary: A possible second regio (Magic aura 7) mirroring the temple town, always night, where those who die in the temple regio reappear as ghosts.

label: Ned Ludd
summary: Name attached to Luddite manifestos.

label: Need Not Sleep
summary: Virtue.

label: Nef
summary: The main carvel-built trade ship of the Mediterranean, following a Roman design with lateen rigging borrowed from the Arabs and up to three masts.

label: Negative Reaction
summary: Minor Social Interaction Flaw giving -3 on all social rolls.

label: Nehardea
summary: Babylonian yeshivah city.

label: Nehushtan
summary: The brazen serpent of Moses that healed all who looked upon it, broken by Hezekiah; if reassembled it would have Mass Healing.

label: Neil
summary: Example player who designs a doppelganger faerie.

label: Nellie Long Arms
summary: Variant of Jenny Greenteeth with long arms.

label: Nemesis
summary: Entity thought to be of the magic realm, hater of immoderation, called upon by the Call for Justice ritual.

label: Nennius
summary: Eighth-century British monk author of History of the Britons.

label: Neo-Mercurian Magic
summary: Organization Lore ability of the Neo-Mercurians used with Performance Magic.

label: Neo-Mercurians
summary: Mystery cult seeking to reconstruct authentic Mercurian magic within Hermetic theory, restoring ancient temples.

label: Nephelococcygia
summary: A mobile magic regio (aura 10) in the clouds inhabited by intelligent birds, containing a city of nine concentric walls; its entrance usually lies in the Thebes Tribunal.

label: Nephilim
summary: A Mythic Companion type: divine giants and heroes of ancient myth, descended from angels, who age very slowly and dwell mostly in divine regiones. They require the Blood of the Nephilim and related Divine-aligned Virtues.

label: Nephilim (Virtue)
summary: The Free Mythic Companion Virtue defining a character as a Nephilim.

label: Neptune
summary: Sea god whom Rumael falsely claims to be.

label: Neptune's Brooch
summary: A wondrous carved precious stone made by a jeweler that prevents the wearer from drowning by letting him float on water (Craft Level 14).

label: Neptune's Imprisoning Arms
summary: A Muto Aquam spell (MuAq 25) created by Falke that forms semi-solid 'vines' of water that can hold a small boat or up to six people, operating like Trap of the Entwining Vines.

label: Neptune's Wrath
summary: A Rego Aquam Ritual spell (Level 40) that creates a gigantic wave up to a mile wide capable of capsizing ships and devastating coastlines.

label: Neqael
aliases: The Lady of the Purple Bower
summary: The Lady of the Purple Bower, Corrupter of Lyonesse: a demoness (Lady of the Spirits of Deceit, Infernal Might 40) who poses as a faerie-blooded noblewoman and corrupts courtly love and etiquette.

label: Nero
summary: Roman emperor in whose last years Apollonius travelled through Rome and Iberia.

label: Nesle
summary: Picard town ruined in the Donatores' battle against undead; site of Requies Aeterna.

label: Nestor
summary: Iacob's faerie caricature, a white (albino) crow that accompanies him on his travels and identifies him as the Prophet of the God of Truth.

label: Nestor of Tremere
summary: The current curator (head) of the oppidum of Tablinum, who holds a collection of Arcane Connections used to enter its regiones.

label: Net
summary: Weapon usable to trip, grapple, disarm or unseat a rider; otherwise ineffective.

label: Netiriun
summary: Young Magus of Rellantali who refused Tamgor entry, suspecting him of spying for Magvillus.

label: Netzach
summary: Sefirah meaning 'Endurance', level 4 on the Tree of Life; understood by a kabbalist with Kabbalah 4.

label: Neustria
summary: Carolingian province that included Normandy and was overrun by Vikings in the ninth and tenth centuries.

label: Nevi'im
summary: The Prophets, second section of the Tanakh; Tractatus on Theology: Judaism and Dream Interpretation.

label: New Aristotle
summary: The body of newly translated works of Aristotle dubbed by scholastic leaders, central to the twelfth-century recovery of philosophical knowledge.

label: New Forest
summary: A royal forest in England cited as a legendary forestry income example.

label: New Temple
summary: Templar chapterhouse in London on the Thames, seat of the English Master.

label: Newcastle
summary: Seat of the king's sheriff who administers Northumberland; an English port.

label: Newid Gornest
summary: Gruagach shapeshifting duel used to settle arguments, as certamen serves the Order; the winner may cast a Geas or Curse on the loser.

label: Niall
summary: The example player who creates the magus Darius of Flambeau throughout the Detailed Character Creation worked example.

label: Nibelungenlied
summary: The great epic poem of the tragic fate of the Burgundian people, immortalizing Siegfried, Kriemhild, Gunther, and Hagen, treated as true history in Mythic Germany.

label: Nibelungs
summary: A legendary race of men from the Lower Rhine who collaborated with dwarves and giants to conquer the wild river; their lost treasure is the Rhinegold.

label: Nicaea
summary: Seat of a claimant to the Byzantine Empire.

label: Nicaea Empire
summary: Byzantine successor state pushing north, expected to reclaim Bear Island.

label: Nicaise
summary: First bishop of Rouen, martyred in the mid-third century.

label: Nicea
summary: City reached by Turks and recaptured by crusaders.

label: Nicene Creed
summary: Early Christian creed (325 A.D.); the Latin addition of 'filioque' was a point of East-West dispute.

label: Nicholas of Myra
summary: Saint to whom Magvillus's chapel is dedicated, whose altar holds a shard of the brine barrel from his miracle.

label: Nicola de Hay
summary: The elderly hereditary constable of Lincoln castle and sheriff of the shire who held the castle through a siege and is locked in a conflict with the earl of Salisbury over her position.

label: Nicolai
summary: A Lithuanian pagan summoner and merchant with the Summoning Art, who summons and bargains with spirits for a price.

label: Nidi
summary: A small covenant near Bergerac, vassal of Oleron, that hides behind the nobleman Henri and exploits niches in urbanizing land; its name changes with each leader and now means starling.

label: Night Battle Taboo
summary: Taboo forbidding nightwalkers and Infernal witches from speaking of their night battles, on pain of dream beatings.

label: Night of Tears
summary: Night when crusaders slay the inhabitants of twelve farmsteads harboring magicians.

label: Night of the Sluagh
summary: Attack of the sluagh on Loch Leglean in December 815.

label: Night Terrors
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character is plagued by horrible nightmares, requiring a Stress Roll against Ease Factor 9 to avoid terrors and Long Term Fatigue loss.

label: Nightwalkers
summary: Nightwalkers of northeast Italy, born with a caul, who battle the stregoni in dreams with fennel swords using powers of the same Infernal realm.

label: Nightwalking
summary: Supernatural Ability suggested as an alternative folk witch power.

label: Nigrasaxa
summary: A relatively new, large covenant of two shining black towers, founded by Maximianus of Bonisagus to break the cycle of invalid tribunals.

label: Nike
summary: The Daimon of victory in both battle and peaceful competition, daughter of Styx and Pallas, invoked in an Orphic Hymn used in eristic moots.

label: Nile
summary: River Chnoubis claims as his home.

label: Nimiane
summary: Young damsel to whom Merlin taught all his secrets in eight days, recorded in a secret journal.

label: Nimrod
summary: Builder of the Tower of Babel.

label: Niobe
summary: A Criamon maga who longed to be Prima but was never selected; her perfect transmission created a study pond as she faded into Twilight.

label: Niort
summary: Town.

label: Nishapur
summary: Persian city sourcing turquoise and malachite.

label: Nissila
summary: Second Pilum of Fire spirit invoked by Gunnar with high Penetration.

label: Nithael
summary: The Great Leveller, Master of the Accusers and captain of a legion of corrupt priests, who preys on those who abuse the power of their offices.

label: Nitibus
summary: A shedeh (Tempter) and personal corrupter with two faces, who encourages his victim's habit of criticism and panders to his vanity.

label: Nivelles
summary: Town in Brabant where Marie of Oignes was born.

label: Nixe
summary: A water-nymph faerie dwelling in the enchanted Mummel Lake who bewitches young men with her beauty, drawing the jealousy of the lake's elemental spirits.

label: Nixons
summary: Border family surrounding Horsingas who take tribute from raids and protect the covenant.

label: Nizar
