summary: Greek genii loci of hills and mountains.

label: Organization Lore: Brethren of Purity
summary: Organization Lore Ability known by all Brethren of Purity.

label: Organization Lore: Church
summary: Ability referenced in this text.

label: Organization Lore: Cult of Mercury
summary: Ability referenced in this text.

label: Organization Lore: Folk Witch
summary: Ability used to recognize a folk witch's mark.

label: Organization Lore: Folk Witches
summary: Lore Ability covering folk witch effects, where covens meet and the reputations of folk witches; its specialty must be a home coven.

label: Organization Lore: Franciscans
summary: Knowledge of the Franciscan organization; required with Presence for Franciscan Initiation Scripts.

label: Organization Lore: Knights Templar
summary: Knowledge of Templar rule, members, provinces, sign language and ciphers.

label: Organization Lore: Luperci
summary: An Ability that sets eligibility for each Luperci grade and replaces Magic Lore when the magister invokes the She-Wolf; it is also used to dispel curses at Lupercalia.

label: Organization Lore: Roman Empire
summary: An Organization Lore Ability; Ovid's Fasti is a summa on it.

label: Organization Lore: Students of Avicenna
summary: Organization Lore Ability focused on by Tulab Ibn Sina.

label: Oriflamme
summary: The flame-colored royal standard of France kept at St. Denis, which bolsters the king's troops and overrides other supernatural effects.

label: Origen
summary: Early Church theologian and biblical scholar whose ideas on free will and the stars heavily influence the Magoi of the Star; his tomb is at Tyre.

label: Original Research
summary: The pursuit of advancing Hermetic theory through novel investigation, which Pralicians are especially likely to undertake.

label: Original Sin
summary: Sinfulness inherited from the Fall of Adam and Eve, cleansed by baptism.

label: Orkney Islands
summary: Northern islands owned by Norway, rich in standing stones; once called the Orcades, Isles of the Dead.

label: Orléans
summary: City on the Loire, once Merovingian capital of Burgundy, famed for its cathedral school.

label: Orléans Heretics
summary: Heretical priests uncovered in Orléans in 1022, accused by Aréfast of orgies and demon summoning; some escaped.

label: Orlando
summary: A musician and magus who knows Sorcerous Music and Subtle Magic, used as an example of casting spells while singing or playing his lute.

label: Orleans
summary: French city around which the Orleans Witches operate.

label: Orleans Witches
summary: A mostly male folk witch coven around Orleans practicing a variant tradition with Premonitions instead of Shapeshifter.

label: Orlog spirits
summary: Prophetic landvaettir (Norns) whose foresight coordinates the Icelandic assault and can help set ambushes.

label: Orn
summary: The ancestor after whom the Clan Wilkis Sept of Orn is named.

label: Orogenesis
summary: Power of the Wamses (CrTe 20) adding rock to the island at the cost of permanent Might.

label: Orphan
summary: Free Social Status Virtue: the child's parents are unknown or deceased.

label: Orphan Born
summary: Humans engendered by dead parents and born beyond the veil, able to see spirits and become incorporeal.

label: Orphedra
summary: A cruel Follower of Merinita at Dankmar (age 139), the covenant's link to the dark fae who specializes in illusions, cold, darkness, and fear; she taught Schadrit Faerie Magic.

label: Orphelines
summary: A court of Parisian argotiers who slit the purses of the rich.

label: Orpheus
summary: The legendary Thracian poet, musician, and magician taught by Hermes, regarded by his cult as the first user of Hermetic magic and who descended to the Underworld for Eurydice.

label: Orphic Magic
summary: A Minor Hermetic Virtue granting Orphic magoi access to the additional Range Adelphixis, using emotional connections as Arcane Connections.

label: Orsini Family
summary: One of the great noble families holding real power in Rome.

label: Orthodox Church Lore
summary: Lore Ability of the Byzantine Priest.

label: Orthon
summary: Breton noble version of Osgood in the Bréhat variant.

label: Ortolana
summary: Mother of Clare of Assisi.

label: Orvieto
summary: City visited by the Pope.

label: Osgood
summary: Hermit abjurer living on Crumstone who is a Drowned Man serving Leviathan by luring ships onto Big Harcar, while also rescuing mariners.

label: Ossian
summary: Gaelic hero of Highland stories.

label: Ossium of Bjornaer
summary: A magus of House Bjornaer whose version of Talons of the Winds produces an eerie keening sound; his wizard's sigil makes many of his spells eerie or frightening.

label: Ossuary of St Helix
summary: Crypt corrupted into a Perfidious Infernal aura 4 tarnished with hypocrisy, used by Father Theophagus to summon demons.

label: Ostentatious
summary: Major General Virtue: the faerie gains Pretense every season; multiplier 25.

label: Ostia
summary: Cardinal-bishop town near Rome.

label: Ostracism
summary: Seven-yearly secret ballot using sherds; the magus with most votes must leave the Greater Alps or be Marched.

label: Oswald
aliases: Saint Oswald, King of the Northumbrians
summary: A most Christian king of the Northumbrians (633-642) who raised a cross before battle and won; many miracles and healings occurred at the cross and at the sites of his death and burial.

label: Othila
summary: Elder Futhark rune "Inheritance" used as a vitkir Art. Rune of inherited property such as lands and heirlooms; most often tied to Terram.

label: Otter
summary: Riverine predator hunted with disdain in summer or autumn.

label: Otto da Tonengo
summary: Master Otto, subdeacon and auditor litterarum contradictarum in 1220, succeeded in 1225 by Sinibaldus Fieschi.

label: Otto I
summary: Son of Henry the Fowler, crowned at Aachen in 936, who defeated the Magyars at the Battle of the Lech (Lechfeld) in 955 and was crowned emperor in Rome in 962.

label: Otto III
summary: German Emperor tutored by Gerbert, killed in a Roman revolt.

label: Otto von Wittlesbach
summary: Count Palatine granted Bavaria in 1180.

label: Our Lady of Haut
summary: Healing chapel with Dominion aura 5.

label: Ouranos
summary: Protogonos of Greek myth, father of the Titans with Ge.

label: Ouroboros
summary: Gnostic concept amalgamated into alchemical tradition.

label: Outcast
summary: A Minor Social Status Flaw in which normal society rejects the character and he is not attached to a covenant; he may not take the Wealthy Virtue.

label: Outdoors
summary: A Major laboratory Structure Flaw: the lab is not housed in a building and is fully exposed to the elements, taken with the Natural Environment Virtue.

label: Outer Farnes
summary: The outer group of Farne islands, haunted by demons in local belief and home to faeries and magical creatures.

label: Outer Hebrides
summary: The western group of the Western Islands, battered by Atlantic storms.

label: Outer Mysteries
summary: The most basic Mysteries known to all Initiates of a Mystery Cult, often prerequisites for more advanced Mysteries.

label: Outer Mystery of House Verditius
summary: The Verditius Mystery betrayed to the Order by an anonymous writer, leading to widespread Verditius Magic.

label: Outlaw
summary: A Major Social Status Flaw in which the character has been outlawed and must live by his wits outside society, with a Reputation at level 2 for whatever got him outlawed.

label: Outlaw Leader
summary: A minor Social Status Flaw that grants a character an agency of criminal underlings prior to play; listed with a Resistance of -1 on the Resistance of Agents Table.

label: Outlawry
summary: Icelandic legal penalty for raids and killings.

label: Outsider
summary: Social Status Flaw (Minor or Major) for members of distrusted groups such as Jews, Saracens, or Moors, giving a bad Reputation; required of Jewish grogs (Minor) and companions (Major).

label: Overconfident
summary: A Major or Minor Personality Flaw in which the character has unshakable faith in his own abilities and cannot imagine failure.

label: Overseer
summary: Manages Literatus' fief.

label: Oversensitive
summary: A Major or Minor Personality Flaw in which the character finds intolerable something others find merely unpleasant.

label: Ovid
summary: The Roman poet whose Fasti is the best source on the She-Wolf's Roman history.

label: Ovum Anguinum of Virtue
summary: Serpent's Egg formed stone containing 2 pawns of Creo vis that confers Improved Characteristics (Stamina), Improved Communication, or Tough depending on Enrichment.

label: Owein son of Uryen
summary: A figure at Arthur's court in the Dream of Rhonabwy who played gwyddbwyll with Arthur while his magical ravens battled Arthur's men.

label: Owl of Virtue
summary: A Great Beast Mythic Blood lineage granting the Silence of the Smothered Sound feat, a Focus in Ghosts, and the Nocturnal flaw.

label: Oxford
summary: A master-run English university closely modeled on Paris, with four faculties and two student nations, governed via a chancellor appointed by the Bishop of Lincoln.

label: Pépin
summary: Son of Charles Martel who seized the throne from the Merovingians in 754.

label: Pack Lore
summary: Ability used by nightwalker characters in this chapter.

label: Pack Mentality / Follower
summary: A Minor Personality Flaw making the character a follower rather than a leader who tends to stick with a decisive person.

label: Pact of Crun Clach
summary: Pact of 1189 in which Scottish magi swore not to aid kings or invaders, regulating raids and theft.

label: Pad of Crafters
summary: Confluensis pad home to tradesmen, ceramicists and paper makers.

label: Pad of Gatherers
summary: Confluensis pad housing food producers.

label: Pad of Parades
summary: Open pad used for events, Aegis rituals and Tribunal meetings.

label: Padded Armor
summary: Inexpensive armor of quilted fabric, felt, or stuffed leather.

label: Paderborn
summary: A town at the source of the River Pader, famous as the site of the 799 meeting of Charlemagne and Pope Leo III that agreed the establishment of the Holy Roman Empire.

label: Padfoot
summary: A faerie in the form of an immense black dog with glowing green eyes that protects travelers despite its fearsome reputation.

label: Padfoot Blood
summary: Faerie Blood variety granting a Perception bonus.

label: Padua
summary: City where Eccelino built eight prisons.

label: Padus
summary: Venetian city whose refugees founded Venice.

label: Pagan
summary: Major Supernatural Story Flaw for a character who does not follow the Church, has never been baptized, and may suffer supernatural consequences from Christian worship.

label: Pagan's Hill
summary: Hill above Chewstoke, site of an Imperial Mercurian temple with a Magic aura of 2.

label: Pagan Theology
summary: An Ability covering non-Christian religious doctrine; the second book of Aristotle's Metaphysics is a tractatus on it.

label: Pagan Traditions
summary: Groups of pagans following a tradition of faerie wizardry with Favored Abilities.

label: Page (Green Stone)
summary: First degree of the Knights of the Green Stone, which teaches Free Expression, Performance Magic: Music and Art of Memory.

label: Pages of History
summary: Theory of the Magic Realm as a record of past events, composed of tempora.

label: Pagus
summary: Vassal of Confluensis (840-1008) at a Roman outpost near Cherbourg, damaged by Vikings and destroyed in the Schism War.

label: Paid Rights
summary: A Virtue that is a game-mechanical way to acknowledge that an exceptional woman who holds public power in Mythic Europe is genuinely exceptional.

label: Paimpont
summary: Monastery in Brocéliande.

label: Painful Magic
summary: A Major Hermetic Flaw in which casting spells causes the equivalent of one Fatigue level in pain per spell, applying a cumulative penalty to actions.

label: Painful Magic Restriction
summary: Supernatural Flaw available to vitkir.

label: Painless Moon
summary: Minor Supernatural Virtue: the folk witch suffers no Medium Wound during her Witch's Moon.

label: Painless Witch Moon
summary: Minor Virtue gained by Eliza from the Witch Moon.

label: Pains of the Perpetual Worry
summary: A Creo Mentem spell (Level 20) that gives someone a nagging, painful recurrent emotion of anxiety and fear; described as truly a curse.

label: Painting
summary: A Craft/Profession Ability representing skill at painting, used in the example maestro Grifo's Aesthetic Quality calculations.

label: Palace of the Selkie King
summary: Undersea palace of the selkie king, possibly thatched with brides' hair.

label: Palace of Woven Grass
summary: Example story element: prison of the child stolen by the Rye-King.

label: Paladins
summary: Charlemagne's twelve companions.

label: Palatial
summary: A Major laboratory Outfittings Virtue: the lab is lavishly outfitted with the best comforts and decoration (+1 General Quality, +3 Upkeep, +2 Health, +4 Aesthetics).

label: Pale Horseman
summary: Demon of the fourth seal named Death, followed by Hell.

label: Palermo
summary: Intellectual centre of Sicily with libraries and Auras of Reason; besieged 1199.

label: Palestine
summary: Site of border skirmishes.

label: Palestrina
summary: Cardinal-bishop town.

label: Palfrey
summary: Gentle-gaited riding horse, often for ladies or inexperienced riders.

label: Pallantium
summary: City founded by Evander on the site of Rome before Rome was built.

label: Pallas
summary: A maga whose death left her lover, a nymph of unmatched beauty, in inconsolable mourning, leaving a covenant tower unused for sixty years.

label: Pallium
summary: Archbishop's symbol of office, received from the pope or a papal legate.

label: Palm of Flame
summary: A Creo Ignem spell (Level 5) in which a flame leaps up in the caster's upturned palm, casting torch-like light and igniting flammable items without burning or damaging the caster.

label: Palm Sunday
summary: The Sunday before Easter, recognizing Jesus' arrival in Jerusalem.

label: Palsied Hands
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character's hands shake uncontrollably, giving -2 to rolls involving holding or wielding objects and an extra botch die when casting.

label: Pan
summary: Wild god of satyrs and faerie revelry whose supposed death left a void demons exploited.

label: Pan Caudarax
summary: Dragon and first guardian of Iceland who destroyed Hadrianus's ship; he can shapeshift into a lindorm or kraken and commands an attendant host.

label: Pan Lykaios
summary: Deity to whom the lykaia ritual meal on Mount Lykaion was sacred.

label: Pancrestis
aliases: Pancrestis filius Occultes, Follower of Bonisagus
summary: A young journeyman of House Bonisagus at Heorot, filius of Occultes and mentored by Philippus Niger, keen to learn Norse magic but deeply fearful of the wilderness.

label: Pandion of Flambeau
summary: Magus convicted of stealing a magical horse from a Redcap.

label: Pandius
summary: Vessel of Iniquity demon who teaches secret poisoning; appears as a scorpion-man.

label: Pandora
summary: A clay woman that Hephaestus made for Zeus, listed among his famous treasures.

label: Pandulf
summary: The Papal Legate in England, elected bishop of Norwich in 1215 but not yet consecrated, who serves as regent for the young king and in theory outranks both king and archbishop.

label: Pandulf Marca
summary: Italian-born bishop of Norwich, papal legate and chairman of England's Council of Regency, known for nepotism.

label: Panes
summary: Satyrs with goat legs and tails.

label: Panic of the Elephant's Mouse
summary: A Rego Animal spell (Level 15) that makes an animal afraid of the target, causing it to flee by the quickest means.

label: Panic of the Trembling Heart
summary: A Creo Mentem spell cited as an example of a base-level-4 spell creating emotion directed at a particular person or object.

label: Panicked Horse
summary: A frightened or wounded horse that the rider must control with Presence + Ride.

label: Pannage
summary: Right, paid for by villeins, to turn pigs loose in the woods.

label: Panther of Virtue
summary: A magical panther whose lure causes mysterious disappearances of animals and can ensnare incautious investigators.

label: Papal Bull
summary: Unilateral charter issued by the Pope on any matter requiring decree.

label: Papal Camera
summary: Office of the curia controlling papal finances, directed by the camerlengo.

label: Papal Curia
summary: The papal court, enlarged and streamlined under Innocent III and Honorius III; receives up to 2,000 petitions yearly and is the final court of appeal.

label: Papal Inquisition
summary: Emerging threat to the Order of Hermes.

label: Papal Letter of Inquisition
summary: Extremely rare document granting its bearer extraordinary power backed by the papacy; only one Dominican holds one.

label: Papal seal
summary: Held by the bullatores.

label: Papal States
summary: Central Italian lands ruled by the Pope, including Rome, Florence and Bologna.

label: Paralyze a Man at R: Eye
aliases: Paralyze a Man at R: Eye
summary: The magical feat granted to magi of the Wolf of Virtue Mythic Blood lineage.

label: Parching Wind
summary: A Perdo Aquam spell (Level 20) that removes most water from an object, and with a Corpus or Animal requisite can damage humans or animals while making them thirsty.

label: Pardons
summary: Breton religious processions with feasting.

label: Parella
summary: Example maga using Major Philosophic Alchemy.

label: Parens
summary: A magus's master/teacher within the Order; the parens trains the apprentice, sets the gauntlet, and conventionally is regarded as a superior throughout life.

label: Paris Lore
summary: Area lore of Paris.

label: Paris (son of Priam)
summary: Son of the faerie lord Priam of Ilium, who holds a beauty contest during Ilium's mid-summer fair.

label: Paris Temple
summary: Templar house in Paris serving as the French royal treasury, holding Saint Ursula's skull.

label: Paris Way
summary: An alleyway leading from Devil's Lane serving as a regio entrance to its eponymous city.

label: Parish
summary: Basic unit beneath deaneries where a priest conducts Mass; virtually every covenant lies in one.

label: Parish church
summary: Church at the center of parish life, consecrated by the bishop with relics under its altar; base Divine aura 4.

label: Parish clerk
summary: Assistant to the parish priest (often an acolyte) who helps with the liturgy and rings bells, paid a yearly wage by parishioners.

label: Parish Priest
summary: Representative of the Church in the parish, reciting the liturgy, distributing alms and caring for his congregation.

label: Parish Register
summary: Book (Level 7) held by the example Village Parish.

label: Parisii
summary: A fishing tribe who first settled the island in the Seine, giving Paris its name.

label: Parks and Lodges
summary: Portions of wasteland reserved by lords for pleasure and as game reserves.

label: Parma Ablativa
summary: The 'ablative shield' Parma fold that doubles Parma Magica for resistance but loses resistance equal to the Penetration of each resisted spell; takes ten minutes to perform.

label: Parma Absorbea
summary: The 'swallowing shield' Parma fold that traps resisted spells for a round so their Penetration can empower the magus's next spell; halves Parma Magica.

label: Parma Condensa
summary: The 'thick shield' Parma fold that doubles Parma Magica against one chosen Form but halves it against all others.

label: Parma Custodia
summary: The 'guarding shield' Parma fold that protects against physical attacks, adding twice Parma Magica to Defense but giving no magic protection.

label: Parma Magica
summary: The Hermetic defense against magic, invented by Bonisagus; the personal magic resistance that made the Order possible.

label: Parma Repercussa
summary: The 'reflecting shield' Parma fold that bounces stopped spells back at a target the magus can see; halves Parma Magica.

label: Parma Restricta
summary: The 'holding shield' Parma fold that encloses a touched target in a magical cage its spells must penetrate; often used to suppress a creature's magic.

label: Parmulae
summary: A 'little shield': a lesser enchanted device such as a brooch granting its wearer Magic Resistance 30 for one year; a Minor Breakthrough based on Notatus's work.

label: Parsifal
summary: Tractatus, Magic Lore, by Wolfram von Eschenbach placing the Grail at Munsalvaesche.

label: Parsirus
summary: A Verditius magus of Ungulus, beloved of Sinead, who was killed by the dragon.

label: Parthenay
summary: Castle conjured by Mélusine for her second son.

label: Partially-fae horse
summary: Horse breed of the Burning Acorn Vexillation, tolerating Gifted riders.

label: Parting the Waves
summary: A Rego Aquam spell (Level 30) that parts a body of water, revealing a dry path five paces wide along the bottom.

label: Partitio Monaviae
summary: 1145 document by a special tribunal declaring Man neutral until a covenant is founded there.

label: Partner
summary: A major Social Status Virtue for a character with a large financial stake in a wealthy company, providing minor-noble-level income and the ability to act in any company role except capo.

label: Partridge
summary: Game bird hunted by falcons.

label: Parzival
summary: Wolfram von Eschenbach's epic poem, said to hide an allegory of the Knights and directions to their Grail Castle.

label: Pasiel
summary: Duke of Purgatory, an angel of punishment treated as a demon (Infernal Might 40) who can manipulate time.

label: Pass the Unyielding Portal
summary: A Muto Herbam spell (Level 5) that makes the wood of a door pliable, allowing the magus to bend it open regardless of most locks or bars.

label: Passau
summary: Town near the Bohemian Forest.

label: Passes for Human
summary: Free Social Interaction choice: the faerie suffers no social consequences as it can seem human, living at society's margins.

label: Passes of Saint Bernard
summary: Monasteries vital to redcaps.

label: Passion's Lost Feeling
summary: A spell that renders the target unable to feel any emotion, leaving them listless and without motivation.

label: Passion (Target)
summary: Faerie Target affecting a group through a particular emotion or desire; same level as Group.

label: Passions
summary: Strong character emotions treated like Personality Traits for the aura effects of the Resting Place of Mars.

label: Past of Another
summary: A Muto Mentem ritual (Level 35) that completely rewrites the target's memories so they cannot remember their actual life until the effect is dispelled or expires.

label: Pastille
summary: Small ignited lump of alchemical paste whose smoke carries magic to a Group target.

label: Pasture
summary: Grazing land, primarily for sheep, often marginal land at the edge of the waste.

label: Patarus
summary: Demon of the Order of Accusers serving BaalBaruth, who appears as a thin horned monk in Cluniac garb and uses powers like Whispers Behind the Back.

label: Paten
summary: Plate for bread given to sub-deacons with a chalice.

label: Pater Noster
summary: The 'Our Father', later called the Lord's Prayer, recited by Cathars.

label: Path
summary: A House Criamon tradition combining a field of study, set of values, and lifestyle, each granting different Mystery Virtues; clutches originally followed a single path.

label: Path of Aging
summary: A forest path through which Alexander of Jerbiton sought to reverse aging, requiring sacrifices and a quest to drink from the Fountain of Youth, yielding the Immortality of the Forest Virtue.

label: Path of Chance
summary: The route through the Faerie Realm that wends through Arcadia, a land of pure adventure among fragments of stories yet to be told.

label: Path of Choice
summary: The path into Eudokia, embarked upon by those entering a Faerie Aura on the verge of a major life change.

label: Path of Destiny
summary: The straighter route through Elysium, where characters relive allegorical stories whose outcomes are already established.

label: Path of Energy
summary: A forest path discovered by Terious of Flambeau to replenish spent spellcasting energy from the forest, yielding the Life Boost and Mythic Blood Virtues.

label: Path of the Founder
summary: Sympathy bonus for Initiation Scripts that imitate the life of Francis.

label: Path of Warping
summary: A forest path walked by Kleon of Criamon to influence the effect of Wizard's Twilight on his Gift, yielding the Puissant Enigmatic Wisdom and Twilight Mastery Virtues.

label: Paths through the Forest
summary: A tradition of nature magic inherited from Merinita, walked by many exsules, which may let them overcome one or more of the Lesser Limits of Hermetic magic.

label: Patriarch
summary: Rank between archbishop and pope; the Latin Church has patriarchs at Jerusalem, Antioch, and Constantinople.

label: Patriarch of Jerusalem
summary: Prelate before whom the first Templars took vows; authenticated relics.

label: Patrician monks
summary: Monks who dwelt on Inisphadraig before the Augustinian chapter and taught Divine magic to the guardians.

label: Patrick, Count of Dunbar
summary: Powerful noble with lands on both sides of the Anglo-Scottish border, claiming descent from Duncan.

label: Patrick's Island
summary: Largest island on Lough Dearg, named after Saint Patrick, home to an Augustinian chapter house with a Dominion aura of 3 (4 within the house).

label: Patrizio
summary: Patrician of a northern Italian town's ruling elite, ranked above squire and below knight.

label: Patron
summary: A sponsor who agrees to support an artist for an undetermined length of time, funding all of his work; losing one costs 12 Artist Reputation experience points.

label: Patron Angel
summary: Major General Virtue granted by the Fourth Ring of Solomon; a personal angel acting as guide and teacher.

label: Patron Saint
summary: A saint a character may invoke for intercession, often of the local church, region or profession.

label: Patron spirit
summary: A spirit each Theban covenant must bind.

label: Patronage
summary: Distribution of land, money, favors and titles, affecting Reputation and Gratitude.

label: Paul of Jerbiton
summary: Luctatio magus on the Council of Milan.

label: Pavania
summary: A self-proclaimed princess of Atlantis caught by fishermen who demands magi remove 'the taint of the surface world.'

label: Pavia
summary: Imperialist commune and former Lombard capital full of family towers.

label: Pavise
summary: A large free-standing shield behind which crossbowmen span their weapons.

label: Pawning (Magic Items)
summary: Redcap practice of lending about half an item's value in vis against a magic device that can be bought back within a set time.

label: Paxon filius Valentin
summary: Archmage of Verditius, the finest brewer of longevity potions in the Order, based at Sinews of Knowledge.

label: Paxon of Verditius
summary: Verditius magus who currently holds the right to harvest vis from Staubbach Fall.

label: Pazin
summary: Place on the Istria Peninsula in the Kingdom of Croatia.

label: Pazuzu
summary: Babylonian disease spirit whose image Lamashtu fears.

label: Peace of God
summary: Church proclamation protecting the poor, Churchmen and merchants from violence.

label: Peacocks
summary: Fourth degree: conjunction, Venus, copper; learns Hermetic Alchemy.

label: Peanhafel
summary: Pictish covenant destroyed by Druids of House Diedne in a year-long siege in 849.

label: Peasant
summary: A Free Social Status Virtue for a free (non-serf) character who lives by working the land, possibly controlling and hiring labor if wealthy.

label: Peel
summary: One of the three towns on the Isle of Man.

label: Peering into the Beastly Mind
summary: Spell (InAn 30) known by Amberitus.

label: Peering into the Mortal Mind
summary: An Intellego Mentem spell (Level 30) that lets the caster thoroughly probe and understand the contents of the target's mind, including motives, strengths, and weaknesses.

label: Peist
summary: Immense serpent-like monster of Lough Dearg banished by Saint Patrick; its blood tinges the lake red.

label: Peitho
summary: The Daimon of persuasion and charming speech, daughter of Styx and Pallas, who with her sister Bia represents forceful inducement.

label: Pelagius
summary: One of Jerbiton's allies who traveled Europe seeking further recruits for the expanding House.

label: Pelagius of Jerbiton
summary: Jerbiton magus who drew Florum's folk magicians into the House.

label: Pelican (alchemical still)
summary: Two-necked still returning distillate for re-distillation.

label: Pelican of Virtue
summary: A symbolic bird whose beak provides a Shape and Material bonus of +8 to healing and nurturing.

label: Pelicans
summary: Sixth degree: distillation, Moon, silver, red; Mystagogues who learn Philosophic Alchemy.

label: Pellam filius Cato
summary: Young Criamon who believes ball sports are remnants of pagan rituals leading toward the Enigma.

label: Pellinore (cabal member)
summary: Cabal member claiming descent from the real Arthur who manipulates churchmen against tournaments.

label: Pellus
summary: The Latin cap of liberty worn as House Mercere's red cap of office.

label: Peloponnesus
summary: Region ravens flew from, per Pliny, after the massacre of Median mercenaries.

label: Pelos
summary: Old god whose descendants may bear Faerie God Blood.

label: Pembroke
summary: Castle whose round keep is 80 feet high with walls 16 feet thick.

label: Pembrokeshire
summary: Earldom held by William Marshal.

label: Penalty for Fighting Without a Helmet
aliases: Penalty for Fighting Without a Helmet
summary: Optional rule adding an extra botch die to melee Defense and Evasion rolls for characters without head protection.

label: Penance
summary: Sacrament of confession and absolution that grants a Confidence Point and a holy connection to the confessor.

label: Pendule
summary: A legendary Provençal hedge wizard who evaded the Founder Flambeau, took four Hermetic followers (two from House Merinita), taught illusion Mysteries, and died in 854 AD.

label: Penetrate the Regio
summary: Hermetic version of a Mercurian ritual.

label: Penetrate the Regio Skin
summary: Cr(Re)Vi 25 ritual creating a new entrance through a Magic regio boundary.

label: Penetration
summary: The Ability and value determining whether a spell overcomes a target's Magic Resistance.

label: Penetration Ability
summary: An Ability that provides a Penetration bonus; creatures and characters without it have a Penetration bonus of zero.

label: Penitent
summary: Woman living a permanent religious life of penitential practices in small groups, known as bizzoca, pinzocheri or continentes.

label: Penitent Ghosts
summary: Disfigured ghosts of Bath bath thieves.

label: Penitentials
summary: Reference books for confessors listing appropriate penances for sinful acts.

label: Penitentiaria
summary: Papal judicial office handling lesser petitions, penances and dispensations.

label: Penitentiarius
summary: Cardinal who deals with appeals to penances, grants dispensations and is confessor to the cardinals, with up to 12 sub-penitentiarii.

label: Pennius
summary: Character listed in the Tribunal index.

label: Pennyroyal of Virtue
summary: Creeping mint-like herb containing 1 pawn of Corpus vis, known as Heal-All; when Enriched it confers a Greater Purifying Touch against an ailment determined by the ruling star.

label: Pentecost
summary: Feast 49 days after Easter with feasting, dancing and horse racing, often followed by a week of holidays.

label: Pentele
summary: A being who protects the Beasts of Virtue inhabiting a magical garden realm and may allow visitors to hunt there in exchange for favors.

label: Penteli
summary: The marble quarries near Athens, cited as a legendary mining income example.

label: Peon
summary: Iberian townsman who fights on foot.

label: People of the Clouds
summary: Magical sailors of a sky-sea regio who fly ships with power over winds and have insatiable wanderlust.

label: Pepin II
summary: Pepin 'the Large', Dux et Princeps Francorum.

label: Pepin III
summary: Pepin 'the Short', first Carolingian king, crowned 751.

label: Pepin the Short
summary: Frankish ruler who restored the pope to power over the Papal States.

label: Pepino
summary: Hoplite and Legion of Mithras member who introduced and taught Darius.

label: Perambulation
summary: Procession on Rogation Day in which priest and parishioners walk the parish boundary.

label: Perceive Motives
summary: An Intellego Mentem effect (InMe 10) enchanted into Falke's talisman, like Sight of the Transparent Motive but with zero Penetration to avoid affecting Hermetic magi.

label: Perceive the Afflictions of Mortal Flesh
aliases: Perceive the Afflictions of Mortal Flesh
summary: Caladrius power identifying diseases by sight.

label: Perceive the Change
summary: An InAn 14 constant enchantment effect detecting whether an item touches an animal, used to trigger linked size/shape effects when a Bjornaer transforms.

label: Perceive the Distant Truths
summary: Warders of Mystery power to perceive a place via Arcane Connection.

label: Perceive the Eyes of Knives
summary: A new Intellego Mentem spell (InMe 20) invented for Tabanus that indicates whether anyone in the target room has hostile thoughts toward the caster.

label: Perceive the Firewalker
summary: InIg 30 spell revealing creatures with Ignem-aligned Might.

label: Perceive the Magical Scent
summary: Hermetic spell (InVi 20) in a Roman Tribunal magus vocation template.

label: Perception
summary: Characteristic combined with Carouse.

label: Perception of Conflicting Motives
summary: An Intellego Mentem 15 spell known by Imanitos Mendax.

label: Perception of the Conflicting Motives
summary: An Intellego Mentem spell (Level 15) that detects the conflicting motives behind a target's actions, often cast before a Muto or Rego spell to change emotions.

label: Perceval
summary: A Redcap in his late forties contemplating retirement; tall, thin, balding, married to Lucy, with a brooch that makes him and his horse invisible.

label: Perchte
summary: Faerie leader of processions of the dead, collecting the dead and leading them to pagan underworlds.

label: Perdo
summary: Technique meaning 'I destroy'. Destroys, weakens, harms or removes.

label: Perdo Ignem
summary: Technique/Form combination that might extinguish the Ships of Flame's fire.

label: Perdo Mentem ritual (Sundering)
summary: Likely ritual used inside Coeris to break Tremere's lieutenants' minds.

label: Perdo Vim
summary: A Hermetic Technique-Form combination of destruction and magical power; Perdo Vim spells that reduce Might can kill a legendary artist.

label: Peredur
summary: A knight-hero of a Mabinogion tale who slew the Black Oppressor and the Black Serpent of the Barrow with the aid of a magic stone given by a mysterious lady.

label: Peredur's concealment stone
summary: A magic stone given to Peredur by a mysterious lady that hid him from the seeing stone pillar guarding the Black Serpent's cave, letting him slay the serpent unseen.

label: Peregrinator
summary: The wandering magi of the Rhine Tribunal, typically journeymen, who travel from covenant to covenant relying on the Laws of Hospitality; about a sixth of Rhine magi are peregrinatores.

label: Peregrine Falcon
summary: Smaller ambush-predator falcon that attacks with a swooping dive.

label: Perfect Balance
summary: A Minor General Virtue granting +6 to rolls to avoid falling or tripping, especially on narrow ledges or tightropes.

label: Perfect Eye for (Commodity)
summary: A minor general Virtue letting a character always accurately assess the value of one commodity and products made from it, granting extra Labor Points when trading exclusively in it.

label: Perfectibility of Man
summary: Origen's heretical doctrine that there is no damnation and all things will eventually be saved.

label: Perfection of the Well-Designed Chamber
summary: Re(Cr)Te(He) 20 spell reshaping one room of a building to be perfectly regular for Hermetic Geometry ceremonial bonuses.

label: Perfectus
summary: A Minor Social Status Virtue for one of the leaders of the Cathar heretics in southern France, sworn to preaching and ascetic abstinence.

label: Perfidious Aura
summary: A corrupted aura embodying sins that betray trust, such as treachery and hypocrisy, typically found within the Dominion.

label: Performance Artist
summary: An artist who performs art using a Profession Ability, such as jugglers, musicians, and minstrels, taking the Social Status Virtue Wanderer.

label: Performance Duration
summary: New spell Duration lasting as long as the caster performs the Performance Ability; equivalent to Concentration.

label: Performance Magic
summary: A Minor Hermetic Virtue letting a magus conceal spellcasting by substituting the actions or words of a specified Ability for normal Hermetic gestures and words.

label: Perfume-sorcerers of Soqotra
summary: Sorcerers sent by spirits guarding incense trees.

label: Periapt
summary: Minor Mystery Virtue allowing creation of astrological amulets as charged devices using a Periapt Horoscope as a single-use Lab Text.

label: Periapts
summary: Virtue learned at the Degree of Mars of the Magoi of the Star.

label: Peril of Excellence
summary: Listed in the Tribunal index.

label: The Peripheral Code
summary: The accumulated body of Tribunal rulings that interpret and extend the Code of Hermes.

label: Peris
summary: Demon controlling many diabolists in northern Italy's cities, patron of the Della Torre, who took flesh as Eccelino da Romano.

label: Periwinkle of Virtue
summary: Blue flower of virtue that when Enriched grants Venus's Blessing along with the Reckless Flaw; unenriched worth 1 pawn of Mentem vis.

label: Permanent Death
summary: Faeries are permanently killed only by forces outside their story, such as destruction of Might, miracles, Infernal agents, or use of anchor vis.

label: Permanent Wall of Protecting Stone
summary: CrTe 20 ritual creating a permanent 100 cubic pace wall of single unmortared stone.

label: Pernix of Merinita
summary: Magus acquitted in 1179 after covertly healing a young nobleman.

label: Perpauca Bonisagi
summary: Magus whose books became the first tomes of the Library of the Normandy Tribunal.

label: Perpetuity
summary: A Major Illusion Mystery of House Merinita granting three potentially-permanent spell durations (Might, Aura, Hidden); Merinitae usually gain the Unnatural Magic Flaw.

label: Persephone
summary: The queen of the Greek Underworld who, with Hades, was moved by Orpheus's song; the sirens felt guilt at failing to save her from Hades.

label: Perseus
summary: Fifth rank, senior Legion member of a Tribunal, carries a silver sickle and learns spirit familiars.

label: Persia
summary: The land of the Magians, original priestly caste, and home to most Mazdean communities, lying east of Mythic Europe.

label: Person
summary: A Free laboratory Outfittings Virtue: another person, such as a family member or maid, frequents the lab (-1 Safety, +1 Corpus or Mentem).

label: Persona
summary: A Supernatural Ability and deep-cover disguise technique allowing a magus to flawlessly alter his appearance and mannerisms to adopt a distinct identity; a subtle form of Muto Corpus magic.

label: Personal corrupters
summary: Tempters personifying a person's evil inclination, opposing his guardian angel.

label: Personal Faerie Power
summary: Virtue or creature Quality listed for a being (Anne, Minerva Sulis, Balneator) or setting feature described here.

label: Personal Faerie Powers
summary: Virtue appearing in faerie statistics in this text (Personal Faerie Powers).

label: Personal Hatred
summary: Flaw listed in character statistics in this text.

label: Personal Magic
summary: Flaw.

label: Personal Power
summary: A Minor Supernatural Virtue giving the character an at-will supernatural power equivalent to a Formulaic Hermetic spell of level 25 or lower.

label: Personal Powers
summary: Faerie powers affecting only the faerie itself, often tailored using intricacy points.

label: Personal Vis Source
summary: A Minor Hermetic Virtue granting exclusive access to a supply of raw vis yielding about one tenth of the player covenant's expected annual gathering.

label: Personality Flaw
summary: Category of Flaw that can be connected to a story's hook, such as a widow appealing to a Compassionate character.

label: Personality Flaws
summary: Faeries may have up to three Minor and one Major Personality Flaw, often tied to their form or role.

label: Personality Trait
summary: Short descriptors of a character's personality with scores from -3 to +3 (e.g., Brave, Loyal), used as roleplaying guides and for some rolls.

label: Perth
summary: Elder Futhark rune "Cup" used as a vitkir Art. Mysterious rune of fate, chance and secrets; tied to Vim, it targets vis and supernatural effects.

label: Perthean Compact
summary: Normandy Peripheral Code rulings drafted by Pertheus distributing vis sources as seisins, legacies, tropaea, and luctationes.

label: Pertheus of Tytalus
summary: Magus of House Tytalus who proposed the right of conquest and the Perthean Compact.

label: Pertinax of Tytalus
summary: Necromancer and the only known member of the Worm cult; he acts as its contact with other cults.

label: Perugia
summary: Town at war with Assisi in 1202 where Francis was taken captive.

label: Pesach
summary: Passover commemorating the escape from Egypt.

label: Pessimistic
summary: A Minor Personality Flaw in which the character always expects the worst.

label: Pestilential Breath
summary: Arkliss' power exhaling a disease-causing mist.

label: Peter Abélard
summary: Controversial philosopher and theologian who tutored and secretly wed Héloïse, was castrated, and later became a monk.

label: Peter Abelard
summary: A famous scholastic logician who taught at the cathedral school of St Geneviève in Paris; held two heretical theories condemned by Bernard of Clairvaux and exemplifies both good and bad Academic Reputation.

label: Peter Catanio
summary: One of the early followers of Francis.

label: Peter de Collemdio
summary: A papal auditor in 1220.

label: Peter de Roches
summary: Churchman who has care of the young king and all but rules England; hates William Longespee.

label: Peter des Roches
aliases: Peter des Roches, Bishop of Winchester
summary: The bishop of Winchester (since 1205) and member of the regency triumvirate, a wealthy French-born warrior-bishop and former tutor of the king, contemptuous of Magna Carta.

label: Peter I of Dreux
summary: Current regent of the duchy of Brittany through marriage to Alice.

label: Peter Igneus
summary: Vallumbrosan monk who led the anti-simony party in Florence and passed unscathed through a bonfire in trial by ordeal.

label: Peter Lombard
summary: A scholar who taught at pre-university Bologna and Paris and wrote the Sentences and biblical glosses, compared in a story seed to the works of a Hermetic writer.

label: Peter Mezzobarbo
summary: Bishop in Florence accused of simony who confessed after Peter Igneus survived trial by ordeal.

label: Peter of Bruyes
summary: Defrocked twelfth-century priest who preached the Petrobrusian heresy, burning crosses and denying the value of the Sacraments.

label: Peter of Montaigu
summary: Grand Master of the Templars from 1219, elected at Damietta; rumored to seek independence even from the pope.

label: Peter of Roches
summary: Bishop of Winchester who will reform the Order of Saint Thomas in 1228.

label: Peter of Uist
summary: Author of The Primal Power.

label: Peter the Lombard
summary: Author of the Sententiae (Sentences), one of the authoritative sources for the Academic Ability Theology: Christian.

label: Peter the Venerable
summary: Great reforming Cluniac abbot who led the counter-offensive against the Petrobrusian and Henrician heresies.

label: Peter von Wurzburg
summary: A master of House Verditius at Fengheld, a famed grower of grapes and maker of wine who cultivates special varieties into wine as Charged Items.

label: Peter Waldo
summary: Wealthy Lyon merchant who gave away his wealth in the late 1100s and founded the Waldensians.

label: Petit Pont
summary: Short stone bridge of 1186 connecting the Île de la Cité to the left bank.

label: Petition Total
summary: Com (written) or Pre (audience) + Church Lore + modifiers, with no die roll.

label: Petitioning
summary: Clerical activity; Templar clergy petition commanders, grand master or pope.

label: Petitioning the Church
summary: Rule for seeking Church favor, with bonuses from Cluniac, Cistercian or Vallumbrosan support.

label: Petrobrusian heresy
summary: Heresy of Peter of Bruyes denying Sacraments and burning crosses.

label: Petronilla of Leicester
summary: A woman recorded as having armed herself as a knight and fought in battles during the reign of Henry II; a namesake later haggled the right to choose her own husband. An example of absence-based female power.

label: Petrus Musandinus
summary: A great Salernitan master under whom Gilles de Corbeil trained in medicine.

label: Petrus of Verdun
summary: A tenth-century Primus of House Jerbiton who advocated magi living within mundane communities as wealthy citizens, abandoning multi-House covenants.

label: Petrus Virilis
summary: Bonisagus magus at Durenmar, all of whose offspring have been Gifted.

label: Pfalz Island
summary: An island in the center of the Rhine that formerly housed the covenant of Rheinstein (Magic aura 2), with a ruined castle, a dripstone-bearing rocky spine, and currently occupied by Lord Robert Schonburg.

label: Pfeffers
summary: Benedictine monastery with hot springs.

label: Phaethon
summary: Planetary spirit of Jupiter, ruling clergy, law and science.

label: Phaeton
summary: A young sun god of folklore who, in river myth, drowned in the Po after falling from the solar chariot, his body never recovered.

label: Phainon
summary: Planetary spirit of Saturn, ruling death, secrecy and sorrow.

label: Phalene filia Innocu
summary: Criamon who studies metamorphic animals and sees Twilight as a biological process.

label: Phantasm
summary: Major Unholy Power Virtue granting the Supernatural Ability Phantasm at 1.

label: Phantasm of the Human Form
summary: A Creo Imaginem spell (Level 25) that makes an image of a clothed, equipped person that can move, speak, and behave as a human under the caster's unspoken command.

label: Phantasm of the Skilled Musician
summary: Hermetic spell listed among the spells known by a magus in this text.

label: Phantasm of the Talking Head
summary: A Creo Imaginem spell (Level 10) that creates an illusory face on a wall or flat object that can speak during the spell's duration.

label: Phantasmal Animal
summary: A Creo Imaginem spell (Level 20) that creates an image of any animal up to pony size that moves under mental command and makes appropriate noises and smells, but has no effect on touch.

label: Phantasmal Fire
summary: A Creo Imaginem spell with an Ignem requisite that makes an image of a fire that dances, illuminates, crackles, and apparently warms but does not actually burn; popular at gatherings of House Flambeau.

label: Phantasmal Images
summary: Hermetic spell listed among the spells known by a magus in this text.

label: Phantasticum
summary: The spiritual yet corporeal form that strays from a nightwalker's body, able to become corporeal, immaterial or invisible and to take human or animal shape.

label: Phantom Magic
summary: Hermetic spell listed among the spells known by a magus in this text.

label: Pharmaceutical Theriac
summary: An experimental-philosophy product forming part of the corpus of Medicine; a medicinal cure-all preparation, often a restorative, that some empirici sell genuinely and others fake.

label: Pharmacopeians
summary: Tradition of which taltós are suggested as a regional variant.

label: Pharmocopoeians
summary: A tradition referenced as the model for the Taltos, focused on herbcraft and pharmacology.

label: Pharsalia
summary: Lucan's work of 65 A.D. describing Erictho.

label: Pheasant
summary: Typical hawking prey animal.

label: Phessallia of Merinita
summary: An old, cold Merinita maga of Voluntas connected with the faeries of winter, skilled in Perdo, who possesses faerie items obtainable only as gifts.

label: Phial of Christ's Blood
summary: Crystal phial containing Christ's blood, authenticated by the Patriarch of Jerusalem.

label: Philip Augustus
summary: King of France, called Augustus, who annexed Normandy and rules with divine mandate; target of several plots.

label: Philip Hurepel
summary: Nineteen-year-old landless son of Philip Augustus who might be appointed ruler.

label: Philip I
summary: French king who bought Bourges in 1100.

label: Philip IV
summary: 'The Fair', king from 1285.

label: Philip of Alsace
summary: Count who rebuilt Ghent castle in 1180.

label: Philip of Ex Miscellanea
summary: Donatores magus formerly of Requies Aeterna.

label: Philip of France
summary: The king of France who expelled John from Normandy in 1204 and besieged Ghent; forced to abandon plans to invade England after William de Longespee's naval action at Damme.

label: Philip of Nablus
summary: Grand Master (1169-1171), retired.

label: Philip of Oldcoates
summary: The sheriff of Northumbria who holds Mitford castle and refuses to surrender it to Roger Bertram despite royal summons.

label: Philip of Plessiez
summary: Grand Master (1201-1209).

label: Philip the Tall
summary: One of the early followers of Francis.

label: Philippus Niger
summary: An Archmage of Durenmar who uses the Holy Vehm to execute hedge magicians and at least one Marched magus, and promotes spread of the Vehmgerichte as a tool against hedge wizards.

label: Phillip Augustus
summary: The current king of France, the first of his dynasty not to have his heir acclaimed while he lives.

label: Phillipus de Grevia
summary: The chancellor of Notre Dame at Paris, who holds power to confer degrees and excommunicate university members and uses these rights to dominate the masters.

label: Philomena filia Rafe
summary: A swallow, sister-in-law of Tereus, who claimed in an interview recorded at Durenmar that Tereus' spire holds records of prayers.

label: Philosopher's Egg
summary: Special retort into which substances are distilled; the Philosopher's Stone hatches from it.

label: Philosopher's Stone
summary: Ultimate alchemical product, hatched from the Philosopher's Egg.

label: Philosophers of Rome
summary: Secretive non-Christian cult claiming descent from Simon Magus, seeking apotheosis through sensual Gnosticism.

label: Philosophers of Rome Lore
summary: Organization Lore of the Philosophers of Rome.

label: Philosophiae
summary: A Hermetic Academic Ability measuring philosophical understanding, added to Verditius Lab Totals when carving Verditius runes and limiting Items of Quality bonuses.

label: Philosophic Alchemy
summary: Minor and Major Mystery Virtue building on Hermetic Alchemy; vis extraction digests on its own or produces ready-opened enchantment devices.

label: Philosophic Magic
summary: Minor Supernatural Virtue adding Philosophiae to Kabbalah totals.

label: Philosophical Refining
summary: Major Virtue letting an elemental philosopher extract and move vis; gained via the Blood Oath of Ikhwan as-Safa'.

label: Philosophical Summoning
summary: Virtue for conjuring natural phenomena, matter, or animals of an element; taught by Ikhwan as-Safa'.

label: Philosophumena
summary: Book by Hippolytus telling of Simon Magus' burial.

label: Philostratus
summary: Recorded Apollonios's conflict with a ghula.

label: Phimosis
summary: A Minor Choleric Disease afflicting promiscuous men, caused by excess lust, usually clearing on its own.

label: Phlegethi
summary: Fire elementals ('burners') that rarefy only from naturally occurring flame; short-lived, fast-moving creatures driven to burn and consume cold, that can beguile those who stare into their flames.

label: Phoenix
summary: A legendary bird whose ashes provide a powerful Shape and Material bonus (+11) to rejuvenation and regeneration enchantments.

label: Phoibe
summary: Titaness who is the prophetic earth.

label: Pholus of Tytalus
summary: Author of the Magic Lore tractatus Commanding Spirits.

label: Phorcys
summary: Lord of the Barren Sea before Poseidon, god of death in the sea and father of sea monsters; an Aspect of him is a Magic spirit of Might 40.

label: Phouka
summary: Faerie that may become Infernal by delighting in tempting mortals to sin.

label: Phrygia
summary: Region where Dindyméné is called Kybélé.

label: Phthisis
summary: A Major Phlegmatic, epidemic Disease that pollutes the vital faculty with phlegm and spreads via putrid breath.

label: Phylactery
summary: Shape/material bonus +5 protecting the wearer.

label: Phylactery of the Cautious Maga
summary: An invested device, a hollow wooden box with a silver lid holding an Arcane Connection to a safe place, that transports its wearer to safety.

label: Phylai
summary: Political groupings characteristic of the Theban Tribunal.

label: Phyllia
summary: A master maga of House Bjornaer, the Eagle Elder at Crintera with a polecat heartbeast; a widely-traveled Harmonist and notorious gossip.

label: Phyllorhodomancy
summary: Divinatory method using rose bush leaves, listed among Ceremonial Augury Phenomena.

label: Physica
summary: Hildegard's tractatus on natural philosophy and Medicine.

label: (Physical Characteristic) of the Followers
summary: CrCo35 Ritual permanently raising a physical Characteristic by one, to no more than 0.

label: (Physical Characteristic) of the Heroes
summary: CrCo60 Ritual permanently raising a physical Characteristic by one up to +5; subject is buried under earth.

label: Physical Evil
summary: Evil that deprives a subject of some natural good, such as sickness, death, poverty, and oppression; attributed to demons by Divine religions.

label: Physical Traveler
summary: A traveler who bodily enters a dream as if crossing into a regio, subject to real Fatigue, wounds and time, and able to retrieve hidden objects.

label: Physician of Salerno
summary: A Minor General Virtue indicating attendance at the famed School of Salerno, granting a Reputation, unique medical procedures like anesthetics, and 50 experience points.

label: Physician's Eye
summary: An Intellego Corpus spell (Level 5) that determines the general health of a person, showing afflictions as yellow coloration on the body.

label: Physician's Sense
summary: A cantation (low-level formulaic spell for apprentices) listed in the book's contents.

label: Physicianing
summary: Female Daktyl power duplicating CrCo/MuCo/ReCo spells.

label: Physicians
summary: Tremere healers and corporeal necromancers.

label: Physicus
summary: A term applied to anyone with advanced education in both medicine and natural philosophy, distinguishing educated medics from educated chirurgeons.

label: Physika kai Mystika
summary: Earliest Greek alchemical text, by Pseudo-Democritus.

label: Physiologus
summary: An anonymous first-century Greek manuscript on which most medieval bestiaries are based.

label: Physis
summary: In Tytalan philosophy, the abstract force of nature or self encompassing instincts, ambition, and competition, derived from a higher divine authority and thus permanent and unquestionable.

label: Piètres
summary: A court of Parisian argotiers who feign lameness on crutches.

label: Picardy
summary: A relatively poor region bordering Flanders, Normandy, Ile de France and Champagne, under the influence of King Philip.

label: Picatrix
summary: Best known work of astral magic, translated under Alfonso the Wise.

label: Pick Locks
summary: Ability listed in a Roman Tribunal vocation template.

label: Pictish History
summary: Mundane library subject at Mac Gruagach.

label: Pictland
summary: Land of the Picts, conquered by Kenneth MacAlpin.

label: Picts
summary: Ancient tattooed people of Caledonia from whose priesthood the gruagachan descend; they ceased to exist as an independent tribe after the Battle of the False Sun.

label: Piedmont
summary: Region in the Roman Tribunal where Harco lies.

label: Pierce the Faerie Veil
summary: Spell that detects the Faerie regio.

label: Pierce the Magic Veil
summary: Variant spell highlighting the Magic regio.

label: Piercing Eye
summary: Sabaoth's Power to see through stone, wood and metal.

label: Piercing Gaze
summary: A Minor General Virtue letting a character unsettle people with an intent stare and gain +3 to intimidation rolls; faeries and demons are unaffected.

label: Piercing Lance of Bone
summary: CrAn 20 spell creating a sharpened lance of hardened bone in the caster's hand.

label: Piercing Shaft of Wood
summary: A Muto Herbam spell (Level 10) with a Rego requisite that turns a piece of wood into a barbed shaft that flies at a target and cannot miss but is resisted.

label: Piercing the Faerie Veil
summary: An Intellego Vim spell that lets the caster see through the boundaries of Faerie regiones and find the path to the next level.

label: Piercing the Magical Veil
summary: Spell (ArM5 p.158) allowing characters to see into and pass between regio levels.

label: Pierre de Beauvais
summary: Medieval bestiary author quoted on the caladrius, lion, salamander and stag.

label: Pierre de Castillon
summary: Crusader who brought relics to Aubeterre.

label: Pierre du Thillai
summary: Bailli of Caen, appointed 1205.

label: Pierres de Niton
summary: Two rocks in Lake Léman linked to Díedne sacrifices.

label: Piest
summary: Irish serpent-whale that is Cara's heartbeast.

label: Piet de Spinnen
summary: The false leader of the de Spinnen family, actually Petrus, mundane son of Calvinus of Jerbiton and former mercenary, who serves as Florum's willing spokesman.

label: Pietrine lineage
summary: Flambeau lineage founded by Pietro specializing in Auram lightning magic; its members call themselves Jovians.

label: Pietro
summary: Archmagus and most senior hoplite of the Tribunal, originally Tytalus, who won entry to House Flambeau with lightning and founded the Pietrine lineage; rumored to be the Antares.

label: Pietro Bernadone
summary: Prosperous cloth-merchant father of Francis who paid his ransom after the war with Perugia.

label: Pilate
summary: Roman governor petitioned to break the legs of the crucified.

label: Pilgrim
summary: A traveler journeying to a holy site or shrine, facing ordeals on the road.

label: Pilgrimage
summary: Journey to a holy site; major and minor pilgrimages have Target Levels 30 and 18 and can grant Virtues or remove Flaws.

label: Pillars of Hercules
summary: Islands at the western edge of the known world near Granada, thought to contain uncontrolled gateways to Arcadia and the Magical realm.

label: Pillars of Islam
summary: Five basic duties of Muslim life.

label: Pills of the Doctor
summary: Prop from the mummer's play that now cures all wounds instantly and contains Corpus vis.

label: Pilum of Fire
summary: An iconic attack spell hurling a javelin of flame; a signature of House Flambeau.

label: Pin
summary: Maneuver holding a target helpless to the ground or a wall.

label: Pine Away
summary: Faerie power causing the target to lose the will to live and vitality, treated as a major disease; glanconers use an Arcane Connection version.

label: Pinfold
summary: Pen within a messuage for impounded stray animals, which become the lord's property.

label: Pious
summary: A Major or Minor Personality Flaw in which the character is a fervent follower of his religion, avoiding what it prohibits and doing what it commands.

label: Pious Magus
summary: A magus of true faith, as Nerius is rumored.

label: Pious Warrior
summary: Grog template: a mace-wielding covenant warrior protected by a saintly relic necklace.

label: Piper Gut
summary: Wide channel separating Big Harcar from North Wamses.

label: Pipio
summary: Scribe of Harco.

label: Pirates of Rhodes
summary: Pirates against whom Tremere's new naval doctrine is to be tested.

label: Pisa
summary: A north Italian city of famed merchants, favored by the Holy Roman Emperor, which acts as the port for landlocked Florence.

label: Pisces
summary: Sign of the Zodiac with its own element, temperament and decans in astrological correspondences.

label: Pisuhänd
summary: A small dragon of the Baltic coast that acts like a brownie.

label: Pit of the Gaping Earth
summary: A Perdo Terram (PeTe 15) spell that opens a pit beneath a target's feet; no one can resist it, so it bypasses Magic Resistance, and it can also create defensive trenches.

label: Pixie
summary: Fey beings of Buckland Saint Mary who annihilated the faeries and know traditional wards.

label: Pixies
summary: Minor faeries of Somerset, jovial and rarely malicious; called pisgies in Cornwall and Devon.

label: Pléchâtel
summary: Village with caves and a vis oak.

label: Place of Power
summary: Virtue or creature Quality listed for a being (Anne, Minerva Sulis, Balneator) or setting feature described here.

label: Plague of Frogs

label: Plagued by an Angel
summary: Story Flaw Devil Children often gain when targeted by Heaven's forces.

label: Plagued by Angel
summary: A Story Flaw in which a character is troubled by the attention of an angel; held by the Priest companion and possible for Devil Children.

label: Plagued by Demon
summary: A Flaw involving demonic persecution that cannot be taken if the saga excludes demons.

label: Plagued by Olympian Faeries
summary: Dexithea's flaw reflecting enmity of Olympian faeries.

label: Plagued by Supernatural Being
summary: Flaw possessed by Elisavet.

label: Plagued by Supernatural Entities
summary: Flaw for nightwalkers or intervening magi harassed by demons seeking revenge or the dead seeking rest.

label: Plain of Wolves
summary: A battlefield of the Schism War where the Tytali fought alongside Houses Tremere and Flambeau, referenced by the Tremere Primus Cercistum.

label: Planet
summary: Astrological planets (Saturn, Jupiter, Mars, Venus, Mercury, Moon, Sun) governing effects and Green Cockerel degrees.

label: Planetary Magic
summary: Minor Hermetic Virtue granting a Lab Total bonus to enchant devices by invoking a governing planet's astral influence via a Laboratory Horoscope.

label: Plant's Withering Bane
summary: A Perdo Herbam spell (Level 20) that withers and destroys one living plant up to the size of a small tree.

label: Plantagenet
summary: Royal family of England, not known for patience.

label: Plate and Mail
summary: Mail strengthened with metal plates.

label: Plate Armor

label: Plato
summary: The philosopher whose advocacy of training women for all duties of the state, including warfare, underlies the Order of Hermes's position of equity for women.

label: Plato's Comma

label: Plaustrum Pertinax
summary: A heavily warped covenant wagon turned Magic Thing via the Transformed Thing Virtue, stubborn and disobedient towards magi.

label: Play
summary: Ability appearing in character statistics in this text.

label: Play of the Virtues
summary: Hildegard's morality play with music.

label: Play Shinty
summary: Physical Skill covering shooting, dribbling and blocking with the caman in shinty.

label: Player-Defined Pretenses
summary: Pretenses corresponding to a faerie's story role rather than human abilities, negotiated with the troupe.

label: Player-Driven Stories
summary: Stories where players decide scenery and characters met while the storyguide controls the plot.

label: Player-Influenced Stories
summary: Stories where players alter events affecting their own character using plot devices.

label: Plea
summary: The means by which noblemen raise legal issues with the Order, administered by redcaps, Guernicus or Jerbiton.

label: Pleasant Clouds in the Mind
summary: Merry Devils Power clouding a person or object in illusion.

label: Pleasing Breath
summary: Panther of Virtue power whose fragrant breath entrances humans and beasts.

label: Plentarch
summary: An ancient Mercurian high priest who gathered 38 Mercurians at Pompeii and taught them a ritual allowing them to commune with their gods in concert.

label: Plestin-les Grèves
summary: Bathhouse ruin entrance to the Yaudet regio.

label: Pliny
summary: The Roman author cited as mentioning an ancient mariner who circumnavigated Africa and found the place where much of Europe's gold originates.

label: Ploëmel
summary: Town.

label: Plot Device
summary: A secret proverb given to a player to influence the plot once in a Faerie Realm adventure.

label: Plotinus
summary: Greek philosopher whose teachings the Brethren of Purity combined in their encyclopedia.

label: Plougerneau
summary: Village.

label: Plucking the Hair from the Billy Goat's Chin
aliases: Plucking the Hair from the Billy Goat's Chin
summary: CrVi 20 creating a temporary Arcane Connection to a demon.

label: Plundering
summary: Low Crime of harvesting an undeclared vis source without an interim lease.

label: Pluralism
summary: Practice of a single priest holding several benefices, technically outlawed.

label: Plutarch
summary: Ancient writer who told of a seer proclaiming that 'Great Pan is dead'.

label: Pluto
summary: God of the Underworld and hidden wealth whom Tremere's ancestors served, symbolized by the two-pronged pitchfork.

label: Pneumonia
summary: A Serious Phlegmatic Disease, an inflammation of the lungs caused by polluted air, prone to a Crisis on the seventh day.

label: Po
summary: A river in which the young sun god Phaeton is said to have drowned after falling from the solar chariot.

label: Południca
summary: A faerie (Might 10, Auram) appearing as a maiden, crone, or girl with a scythe who appears at noon on hot days, asking farmhands difficult questions and inflicting heatstroke if they fail to answer.

label: Po Valley
summary: Northern valley occupied by the communes.

label: Poacher
summary: Illegal hunter on reserved land, sometimes of noble or clerical rank, fiercely punished.

label: Podesta
summary: Commune office created by Frederick Barbarossa, usually held by Infernally tainted outsiders.

label: Poena
summary: The Prima of House Tremere at the domus magna Coeris in the Transylvanian Tribunal, said to know the names and strengths of every member of her House.

label: Poetic Justice
summary: Rule that a geas or curse fitting the victim's past acts is harder to resist, modifying the victim's Stamina roll from -6 to +9; also the core ethic of the gruagachan.

label: Poine
summary: The titan of vengeance and retribution and mother of the Erinyes; Tytalus's Prosopopoeia names the She-Wolf as her Aspect.

label: Poison the Air
summary: Infernal dragon Power: exhaling poisonous smoke.

label: Poisoned Battlefield
summary: Arsenic-poisoned site in the Mendip Hills, Stonehenge Tribunal, once haunted by an archnecromancer, druid ghosts and dead Roman miners.

label: Poisoned Sap
summary: Vis site: the Old Oak oozes poisonous sap yielding Perdo vis sordida.

label: Poisoned Weapons
summary: Fachan power smearing its weapons with deadly poison.

label: Poisoning the Fruit of the Vine
aliases: Poisoning the Fruit of the Vine
summary: Salamander power making plants poisonous.

label: Poisoning the Well
summary: Salamander power poisoning water by touch.

label: Poisoning the Will
summary: A ritual spell that curses a place such as a valley, town, city, or covenant, gradually sapping the will and vitality from the people there.

label: Poisonous Blood
summary: Polymathes' deadly blood that stays potent for nine days.

label: Poisonous Breath
summary: Lindwurm power exhaling a cloud of poisonous black smoke.

label: Poisonous elemental
summary: Elemental liberated by disturbing the poisoned battlefield that raids the mundane world.

label: Poisonous Skin
summary: Salamander's constant contact poison.

label: Poitevins
summary: Faction who came to England with King John's wife and are currently ascendant.

label: Poitiers
summary: Ecclesiastic city with the Baptistery of St. John and Church of St. Hilary.

label: Poitou
summary: County captured by Philip in 1205.

label: Poland
summary: Area with German minorities where Hounds of God are found.

label: Polandrus
summary: A demon (Might 20, Animal) appearing as an extremely large jet-black wolf with red eyes who dominates wolves and targets livestock farmers, gradually coercing them into sin.

label: Pole Arm
summary: Two-handed weapon usable to unseat a rider.

label: Pole Axe
summary: Two-handed slashing weapon.

label: Polemic
summary: Persuasive summa or tractatus explaining a philosophical position, circulated to build support before a Tribunal debate.

label: Poleyns
summary: Knee protectors.

label: Policraticus
summary: Work by John of Salisbury complaining about diviners common at court.

label: Polissons
summary: A court of Parisian argotiers who go naked begging for clothes.

label: Political Agent
summary: A thematic covenfolk template skilled in Intrigue, Guile, and Order of Hermes Lore, employed by covenants involved in Hermetic politics.

label: Pollute Water
summary: An Aquam power of the basilisk Sordus that turns all standing water within 5 paces stagnant and putrefies other liquids; he cannot control it.

label: Polus
summary: Ninth-century magus Trianomae whose diaries are at Durenmar.

label: Polyaigos
summary: Island covenant in the Theban Tribunal running a school for Gifted children.

label: Polybius
summary: Greek historian (202-122 BC) whose analysis of mixed Roman government inspired Guernicus's three arms of the Order.

label: Polymathes
summary: An ancient, magically potent dragon who hoards rare books and scrolls in a tunnel lair of illusions.

label: Polyphemus
summary: Last Cyclops of Sicily, nearly 50 feet tall and blinded by Ulysses, now lonely; Magic Might 40.

label: Pombal
summary: Site of a major Templar fortress in Portugal.

label: Pomerania
summary: A sparsely-populated realm of Slavic peoples between the Baltic Sea and Poland, bordering the Novgorod Tribunal; part of the Holy Roman Empire since 1181 and a region of contention with werewolves and the Knights of the Sword.

label: Pomeranian Forest
summary: One of Germany's most oppressive forests, dominated by pine, fir, holly, and evergreen oak; reputedly a stronghold of witches and werewolves and home to the sacred grove of Romowe.

label: Pomeranian tradition
summary: A surviving pre-Hermetic magical tradition with which some of Bjornaer's descendants seek détente, fearing their Founder left it before learning all its rites.

label: Pompeii
summary: The Roman city where the high priest Plentarch gathered 38 Mercurians to teach them the ritual of concerted communion with their gods.

label: Pomponius Mela
summary: Roman historian who claimed nine virgin witches lived on Sein Island.

label: Pontarf
summary: Irish giant fish nursery terror.

label: Pontida
summary: Monastery where the Lombard League formed.

label: Pontifex Maximus
summary: Title of the high priest of the Cult of Jupiter taken by Augustus.

label: Pontine Islands
summary: Island group in the Tyrrhenian Sea in the Roman Tribunal, legendarily occupied by sirens.

label: Pontius Pilate
summary: Unquiet spirit for whom Mount Pilatus is named, who punishes climbers with terrible weather; harvesting vis from his ghost was outlawed.

label: Poor
summary: A Flaw representing less than average wealth for a trader; can be combined with Employed by a Company given troupe approval, and reduces a local carrier to a single pack animal's goods.

label: Poor (Characteristic)
summary: A Minor General Flaw lowering a Characteristic already at -3 or lower by one further point.

label: Poor Combatant
summary: Minor Supernatural Flaw: loses 2 Attack and Defense with one combat Pretense.

label: Poor Concentration
summary: A Minor General Flaw giving the character a -3 penalty to Concentration rolls due to a short attention span.

label: Poor Disputer
summary: A Minor General Flaw causing a character to suffer a -3 penalty on disputatio die rolls.

label: Poor Equipment
summary: Flaw appearing in a Roman Tribunal vocation template.

label: Poor Eyesight
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which bleary vision gives -3 to rolls involving sight, including attack and defense; can combine with Missing Eye.

label: Poor Formulaic Magic
summary: A Minor Hermetic Flaw subtracting 5 from every roll to cast Formulaic spells, though not Ritual spells.

label: Poor Hearing
summary: A Minor General Flaw subtracting 3 from rolls involving hearing and making hard-to-understand speech nearly impossible to follow.

label: Poor Intelligence
summary: Flaw suggested for giants.

label: Poor Living Conditions
summary: A Minor General Flaw giving an additional -1 Living Conditions Modifier, cumulative with the base modifier.

label: Poor Memory
summary: A Minor Personality Flaw in which the character has a very hard time recalling one type of thing such as names, faces, or places.

label: Poor Reader
summary: A common Flaw among the exsules, most of whom have studied from vis for their entire careers.

label: Poor Sisters
summary: Community of women following Francis' ideals under Clare at Saint Damian, living in poverty without total enclosure.

label: Poor Strength
summary: A Flaw possessed by Brother Julian reflecting weak physical strength.

label: Poor Student
summary: A Minor General Flaw subtracting 3 from Advancement Totals derived from teaching and books.

label: Poorly Insulated
summary: A Minor laboratory Structure Flaw: the lab is poorly shielded from the outside, easily overheard and a nuisance to neighbors (-1 Safety, -1 Aesthetics).

label: Poorly Trained Folk Witch
summary: Minor General Flaw: 50 fewer apprenticeship experience points.

label: Poorly Trained Gruagach
summary: Minor Supernatural Flaw reducing experience in gruagach Arts and spells.

label: Poorly Trained Magician
summary: Minor Supernatural Flaw reducing experience points for Arts and charms by 50.

label: Pope
summary: The bishop of Rome and head of the Western Church, who crowns emperors and alone can create, divide, or suppress dioceses; has Commanding Aura with Magic Resistance 25.

label: Pope Alexander III
summary: Pope who issued an 1179 decree, followed by most communities, requiring the expulsion of lepers.

label: Pope Benedict
summary: Pope whose ghost, saved from purgatory by Cluny, appeared to bless the Festival of All Souls.

label: Pope Calistus II
summary: Pope who decreed clerical marriages invalid at the First Lateran Council in 1123.

label: Pope Calixtus II
summary: Pope who signed the Concordat of Worms with Emperor Henry V in 1122.

label: Pope Celestine II
summary: Pope who proclaimed Milites Templi in 1144.

label: Pope Clement III
summary: Pope with good relations to Joachim of Flora.

label: Pope Clement IV
summary: Guido Le Gros from Saint-Gilles.

label: Pope Eugenius III
summary: Pope who accepted the truth of Hildegard's visions in Scivias after Bernard of Clairvaux supported them.

label: Pope Gelasius I
summary: Pope who abolished the Lupercalia in the fifth century.

label: Pope Gregory II
summary: Pope of legend who may have passed Vatican texts to Bonisagus.

label: Pope Gregory IX
summary: Cardinal-bishop Ugolino (born 1170), trusted ally of Honorius III famed as papal legate, who succeeds him as pope in 1227 if the saga follows history.

label: Pope Gregory the Great
summary: A pope, later a saint, at whose earnest request God allowed the Roman Emperor Trajan to be saved after death, with a warning not to ask such things again.

label: Pope Gregory VII
summary: A church reformer who decreed in 1079 that all cathedrals must make schooling compulsory for priests.

label: Pope Honorius III
summary: The pope in 1220, born Cencio Savelli in Rome in the 1140s, elected in 1216; former tutor of Frederick II, determined to reform the Church and recover the Holy Land.

label: Pope Innocent II
summary: Pope under whom the Second Lateran Council of 1139 confirmed the ban on clerical marriage.

label: Pope Innocent III
summary: The pope who established Dominic's Order in 1216, sanctioned the Franciscans, recognized subdeacons as a major order, and was himself a university man.

label: Pope Innocent IV
summary: Pope to whom Clare's completed written rule is presented in 1253.

label: Pope Leo
summary: Pope to whom some copies of the malleus epistula are attributed.

label: Pope Leo I
summary: Pope who declared the Church independent and turned Attila from Rome, reputedly with demons at his command.

label: Pope Leo IV
summary: Pope (847-855) who authored the Homilia Leonis, a popular enumeration of visitation articles.

label: Pope Leo IX
summary: Pope who in 1050 controlled no benefices outside the province of Rome.

label: Pope Martin IV
summary: Simon de Brie.

label: Pope Nicholas II
summary: Pope who excommunicated William and Matilda for being cousins.

label: Pope Stephen II
summary: Pope whose ruling about a 'seven generations' reprieve German nobles misunderstand.

label: Pope Urban II
summary: Pope who preached the First Crusade at the Council of Clermont in 1095.

label: Pope Urban III
summary: Pope with good relations to Joachim of Flora.

label: Pope Urban IV
summary: Jacques Pantaléon from Troyes.

label: Pope Zacharias
summary: Eighth-century pope who allied with Pepin the Short.

label: Pope Zachary
summary: Pope who removed Uriel from the list of angels recognized by the Western Church in 745.

label: Poplar Tree of Virtue
summary: White poplar Tree of Virtue with Creo vis in its leaves; a crown of its leaves grants the Long-Winded Virtue.

label: Popolo
summary: Political societies of wealthy tradesmen opposing the magnates in the communes.

label: Porphyrion
summary: Powerful Archmage and eremite from the Rome Tribunal, a possible third contender for Tytalus Primus.

label: Porphyry
summary: Greek philosopher whose teachings the Brethren of Purity combined in their encyclopedia.

label: Porta Salaria
summary: Gate on the eastern side of Rome near the Church of Saint Aquila.

label: Portage
summary: Faerie Power of instant travel via faerie trods, including across regio boundaries and into the Faerie Realm.

label: Portage of the Eagles
summary: Spell or effect listed in the contents of Transforming Mythic Europe.

label: Porte de Mars
summary: Roman triumphal gate at the north of Reims.

label: Portiuncula
summary: Site at Assisi of the Franciscans' first general chapter meeting.

label: Porto
summary: Cardinal-bishop town.

label: Portugal
summary: Iberian kingdom where Templars received their earliest Iberian donations.

label: Portunalia
summary: Portunes's feast on August 17th.

label: Portune
summary: Tiny brownie-like faerie, half the size of a thumb, that roasts frogs on the fire while humans sleep.

label: Portunes, Spirit of Safe Harbor
summary: A Daimon spirit (Magic Might 25, Auram) charged with ports and harbors, keys and locks, worshipped as a god in Rome; summoned by throwing keys into a fire.

label: Poseidon
summary: Olympian sea god, ally and possibly foster-son of the telechines, who usurped Phorcys' kingdom.

label: Posing the Silent Question
summary: An Intellego Mentem spell (Level 20) that lets the caster ask one silent mental question of a target and detect the answer, limited by the target's knowledge.

label: Positive Folktales
summary: Minor Social Interaction Virtue: the faerie type is in local folklore and treated with respect and caution.

label: Possess the Deceased Host
