summary: Castle in Cornwall, 40 yards across, ambiguous between shell keep and inner bailey.

label: Restricted Learning
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character can only apply experience points to five chosen Abilities and cannot learn new Abilities without Teaching or Training; required of all mundane animals.

label: Restricted Might
summary: Major or Minor Supernatural Flaw rendering the faerie nearly powerless under certain conditions.

label: Restricted Power
summary: A Minor Supernatural Flaw limiting the use of a normally at-will supernatural power, requiring a ceremony or restricting it to certain targets or circumstances.

label: Restriction
summary: A Flaw preventing magic under a circumstance (e.g., at sea, or in bright light as suffered by Ulf); imposed as a Great Beast Ordeal and a common Bjornaer flaw.

label: Restriction (True Feeling)
summary: A Major Hermetic Flaw of the Cult of Orpheus.

label: Retetarius Bjornaer
summary: Deputy chief of Clan Wilkis appointed by the prima, with a salmon heartbeast, dwelling in the River Danube.

label: Rethra
summary: A former great Slavic pagan fortress-temple housing the Oracle of the god Radegast; once a covenant of Slavic magi-priests, it was abolished by the Tribunal in 1207 and retains a Faerie aura of 4 (secretly Infernal).

label: Retiarius
summary: The certamen School of the Fisherman, which strikes swiftly, gains Initiative bonuses and evades damage.

label: Retistius
summary: Verdi magus who won the 1181 Verditius contest with a mechanical dog.

label: Retistius' Mechanical Dog
summary: Mechanical dog that won the 1181 Verditius contest.

label: Retrieve From Purgatory
summary: Option in the Purgatory chapter.

label: Retrieve That Which is Lost
summary: Forcas's Power to locate and summon an object via an Arcane Connection.

label: Return of Mental Lucidity
summary: Hermetic spell listed among the spells known by a magus in this text.

label: Return the Lycanthrope to his Native Form
aliases: Return the Lycanthrope to his Native Form
summary: General-level TaSh spell that ends a transformation and returns the target to his native form.

label: Returned Dead
summary: Faeries that are, or pretend to be, humans who died and return, often believing they died at an unnatural time.

label: Reveal the Hidden Words
summary: A MuAq 5 charged-item effect that makes any group of words written in the enchanted colorless liquid visible for a Diameter duration.

label: Reveal the Lingering Spirit
summary: New Intellego Mentem spell letting the caster see invisible ghosts.

label: Reveal the Lurking Watchers
summary: An InVi 30 spell that allows the caster to see creatures of the Magic realm within his field of view and identify them as possessing Magic Might.

label: Reveal the Magical Deception
summary: A new Intellego Vim spell (InVi 25) invented for Tabanus, designed to overcome spells that hide traces of magic such as Masking the Odor of Magic.

label: Revealed Flaws of Mortal Flesh
summary: An Intellego Corpus spell (Level 10) that finds any medical defects in a person or being touched, more specific than Physician's Eye.

label: Revealed Flaws of the Mortal Flesh
aliases: Revealed Flaws of the Mortal Flesh
summary: A spell that instantly diagnoses a disease's cause and effect and adds +3 to the Prognosis total if the character designs the follow-up treatment.

label: Revelations of the Sacred Company of Virgins at Cologne
aliases: Revelatio De Sacro Exercitu Virginum Coloniensium
Revelations of the Sacred Company of Virgins at Cologne
summary: Elizabeth's book on Saint Ursula's martyrs, a Dominion Lore tractatus.

label: Revenant
summary: A restless dead being whose only form is an animate material corpse, animated by a spirit and connected to the living world through an overwhelming personal need; difficult to harm with weapons and immune to Incapacitation.

label: Reveners
summary: Vessels of Iniquity who reanimate corpses to spread fear, sharing the Obsession of Fear.

label: Revenge of the Bitten Toad
summary: A PeAn 20 Flavor-Target spell inflicting a Heavy Wound on any creature that bites or tastes the caster.

label: Revive the Fading Amulet
summary: SuMa general charm adding one charge to one's own amulet.

label: Revoke Gifts
summary: Eiael's power to revoke any Ring of Solomon.

label: Rewriting the Mind
summary: A Muto Mentem Ritual that utterly changes the target's cognitive goals, hopes and desires to an agenda dictated by the magus.

label: Reynard the Fox
summary: Fox protagonist of a Märchen story used in an Elysian quest.

label: Rhône River
summary: River whose delta forms the Camargue.

label: Rhabdomancy
summary: Divinatory method using divining rods, listed among Ceremonial Augury Phenomena.

label: Rhaetia
summary: Castle-strewn region centred on Chur.

label: Rhaetian
summary: Listed in the Tribunal index.

label: Rhases
summary: Physician who wrote on alchemical theory and the elixir.

label: Rheinstein
summary: A former covenant founded 1123 AD on the island of Pfalz in the Rhine Gorge; attacked and destroyed in 1200 AD by an army of irate mundanes led by the archbishop of Trier.

label: Rhesus of Verditus
summary: Leader of Florum's magi, a weaver interested in the magical uses of flax, who came from the Roman Tribunal and supports the Lotharingian ideal.

label: Rhetoric
summary: Ability listed in a Roman Tribunal vocation template.

label: Rhiannon
summary: A timid maga named Prima of House Merinita at the Grand Tribunal of 997, four generations descended from Quendalon; she defended House Diedne during the Schism War and died of old age.

label: Rhine Gold
summary: Treasure cursed by a dwarf, contributing to Ragnarok.

label: Rhine League
summary: An alliance founded by Mainz and Worms (and joined by cities, archbishops, and nobles) to suppress unjust tolls by trade sanctions and destruction of robber-baron castles along the Rhine.

label: Rhine Lore
summary: An Area Lore Ability covering the Rhine region; held by several characters including Lord Robert, Wolkan, and David ben David.

label: Rhine-Main-Danube Canal
summary: A proposed canal connecting the Main (a Rhine tributary) and the Danube to create a trade corridor across the continent, around which a saga could be designed.

label: Rhinegold
summary: The lost treasure of the Nibelungs, possibly located at the Rhinefalls and jealously guarded by the powerful Rhine elemental in revenge for his entrapment.

label: Rhodes
summary: Home of the telechines, invaded by followers of Athena.

label: Rhodocrosite
summary: Semiprecious stone for memory and medical enchantments, from Coeris caves.

label: Rhonabwy
summary: A warrior of Powys who, sleeping on an ox-skin in a foul hall, dreamed of being taken by Iddawg to King Arthur's court where ravens battled Arthur's men.

label: Rhone
summary: A river that ends at the wild, inhospitable Camargue Delta where a ghostly horse keeps a larder of wicked children.

label: Rhyme of the Beast
summary: Folk witch initiation script requiring living as an animal for a season; grants Animal Ken and the Flaw Incomprehensible.

label: Ribat
summary: Sufi hospice.

label: Ricardus Caespuus
summary: A reclusive Follower of Bonisagus at Durenmar with a glass-walled laboratory specialized in Herbam, who cultivates many types of vis from exotic plants.

label: Ricella
summary: Faerie leader of processions of the dead, collecting the dead and leading them to pagan underworlds.

label: Richard de Marsh
summary: King Richard, more at home in Normandy than England, who offered to sell London at the start of the Third Crusade, executed 3,000 men at Acre, and fought Philip II with a paid army.

label: Richard, Duke of Cornwall
summary: Teenage brother of Henry III, a gifted administrator who in real history buys the title of Holy Roman Emperor.

label: Richard I
summary: King of England interred at Fontrevrault.

label: Richard I, Duke of Normandy
summary: Duke who sponsored colonization of Mont St. Michael by Benedictines in 966.

label: Richard I of England
summary: Negotiated a truce allowing pilgrims into Jerusalem.

label: Richard Mallebeench
summary: English Templar commander (1172-1180).

label: Richard of Glastonbury
summary: A diabolist monk raised by diabolist monks at Glastonbury Abbey, skilled in Incantation and Diablerie, who commits sins of blasphemy and idolatry while believing his Powers are not evil.

label: Richard of Hastings
summary: English Templar commander (1160-1171).

label: Richard Rufus the Deacon
summary: A learned theologian scholar at Schola Pythagoranis who writes tracts justifying the use of magic for virtuous ends, risking trouble with church authorities.

label: Richard the Devil
summary: Figure whose penance bell Proctor believes his talisman to be.

label: Richard the Lionheart
summary: King of England who spent most of his reign on Crusade and at war in France, repeatedly demanding money from England; died of an infected arrow wound in 1199.

label: Richenda Spinosa
summary: An atypical journeyman maga of House Flambeau at Irencillia of secret faerie heritage descended from Kupala; her scarred Gift left her unable to use fire magic, so she turned to Herbam thorn magic and seeks vengeance on her master Indulius.

label: Richildis
summary: Nun who acted as secretary to Hildegard of Bingen in recording her visions.

label: Ricohombre
summary: Iberian great men of the aristocratic upper class who hold honores from kings. They have the Great Noble Virtue.

label: Riddle of the Magus
summary: Personal enigmatic puzzle given to Criamon apprentices marking them as magi.

label: Ride
summary: An Ability used when employing an animal as a mount, which can substitute for Animal Handling and adds to Attack and Defense in mounted combat.

label: Ride in Dreams
summary: Sir Giles' power to enter the dreams of a named sleeper and torment him with nightmares.

label: Ride the Diseased Body
summary: Decani Power that possesses a victim and riddles them with incurable disease.

label: Riding the Phantom Steed
summary: Sir Giles' power to materialize his war horse when he takes physical form.

label: Righi
summary: Alpine mountain where the magi of Journeys End wish to see giants return.

label: Right Bank of Paris
summary: The largest, commercial district of Paris, also called Le Marais.

label: Right of Entry
summary: Faerie right, described in Realms of Power: Faerie, that lessens the Dominion's impact; purchasing London would grant it.

label: Right of Warren
summary: Lord's right to trap and raise small game, extending to pests and even magical monsters and vis sources.

label: Right of Way
summary: The ancient right of faeries to travel through a locale without permission.

label: Rigid Magic
summary: A Major Hermetic Flaw in which the character cannot use vis when casting spells, thus cannot boost spell rolls or cast Ritual magic, though vis can be used in the laboratory.

label: Rigid Scale
summary: Non-metallic scale or lamellar armor.

label: Ring and Circle Wards
summary: Wards traced as a ring, difficult to cast around an island.

label: Ring Armor
summary: Early medieval leather armor with rings.

label: Ring/Circle Magic
summary: The Minor Hermetic Virtue of the Columbae, letting them draw circles faster and treat any well-defined boundary as a Circle by marking it.

label: Ring of Brodgar
summary: Stone circle on Mainland in Orkney that leads to the faerie realm of Barathrum.

label: Ring of Lead
summary: Lead ring around the Graveyard's entrance invested with warding spells and The Ring of Terror.

label: Ring of Plant Mastery
summary: Caitlin's wooden ring allowing spontaneous ReHe spells up to 20 without fatigue.

label: Ring of Saint Maurice
summary: Powerful relic held by the archbishop of Salzburg, said to make one undefeatable in battle.

label: Ring of the Sea's Command
summary: Caitlin's silver ring with aquamarine allowing spontaneous ReAq spells on salt water.

label: Ring of the Sleeper
summary: A ring worn by the Ogier-like Sleeper; whoever puts it on dies instantly and is replaced by a faerie believing itself to be the wearer's spirit.

label: Ring of Warding Against Spirits
summary: A Rego Mentem spell creating a ring that only ghosts and spirits with Magic Might higher than the spell's level can enter.

label: Ring to Ward the Fire's Wrath
aliases: Ring to Ward the Fire's Wrath
summary: Caitlin's copper and ruby ring granting +15 soak against fire.

label: Rings of Solomon
summary: Seven levels of Ars Notoria wisdom, each a combination of orations and notae, learned in order.

label: Rings of Verditius
summary: Five magic rings, one for each finger and thumb, that Verditius forged from all he had learned, perhaps the most powerful magic rings in Hermetic history.

label: Ringwork
summary: Most primitive castle: ditch, packed rampart and thin stone wall.

label: Rio Tinto
summary: Iberian lead source, alternative location.

label: Ripper
summary: A Minor Supernatural Virtue with two inflexible powers: destroying cloth or disemboweling an animal at Sight range without words or gestures.

label: Rise from the Grave
summary: Revenant power opening the earth over its grave.

label: Rise of the Feathery Body
summary: A Rego Corpus spell (Level 10) that allows the target to float vertically to any height carrying up to 50 pounds, but not move horizontally.

label: Rising Ire
summary: A Creo Mentem spell (Level 15) that makes the target furious at someone or something of the caster's choice; an appropriate Personality Trait roll can hold the anger in check.

label: Rising Passion
summary: A Creo Mentem 15 spell invented by Imanitos Mendax that raises uncontrollable carnal lust in a target.

label: Risk Modifier
summary: Experimentation modifier used on the Extraordinary Results Chart, limited by Magic Theory.

label: Rite of Opening the Mind
summary: Tulab Ibn Sina Script at Ibn Sina's tomb granting Premonitions and Visions.

label: Rite of Testing the Physician's Dedication
aliases: Rite of Testing the Physician's Dedication
summary: Tulab Ibn Sina Script granting Medicinal Divining and Restriction.

label: Rite of the Scapegoat
summary: Jewish atonement rite, a Divine-aligned version of Curse-Throwing, in which a goat is loaded with a community's sins on Yom Kippur and driven into desolation.

label: Rithmomachia
summary: The philosopher's game.

label: Ritter
summary: General German term for a cavalry soldier, equivalent to knight.

label: Ritual Faerie Powers
summary: Virtue granting ritual-level faerie powers.

label: Ritual Items
summary: Minor Hermetic Virtue allowing charged items with ritual effects, from integrating folk witch potion-brewing.

label: Ritual Magic
summary: A type of elaborate spell that always requires botch dice (unless mastered) and whose effects cannot be placed in enchantments unless they are Ritual only due to level over 50.

label: Ritual of Calling the Fetch
summary: Gifted gruagach initiation fasting on a mountaintop to find the fetch; grants Fetch and Restriction.

label: Ritual of Discovering the Physician's Humor
aliases: Ritual of Discovering the Physician's Humor
summary: Tulab Ibn Sina Script granting an Elementalist Form and Vow.

label: Ritual of Improving the Physician's Character
aliases: Ritual of Improving the Physician's Character
Ritual of Refining the Physician's Character
summary: Tulab Ibn Sina Script granting Elemental Medicine and Study Requirement.

label: Ritual of Making the Soul Actually Knowledgeable
aliases: Ritual of Making the Soul Actually Knowledgeable
summary: Ikhwan as-Safa' Script granting Elemental Philosophiae and Study Requirement.

label: Ritual of Mount Lycaeon
summary: Rumored ritual turning men into wolves for nine years.

label: Ritual of Passing on the Power
aliases: Ritual of Passing on the Power
summary: Rite by which the She-Wolf solemnizes a grant of power, taking the petitioner's birth name and giving a secret name of vengeance.

label: Ritual of Twelve Years
summary: A House Bjornaer rite of passage after which a magus gains the Heartbeast Ability; experiencing it early in apprenticeship can grant Self-Confident or the Uswaurpa reputation.

label: Ritual of Uncovering the Elemental Nature of Man
aliases: Ritual of Uncovering the Elemental Nature of Man
summary: Ikhwan as-Safa' Script granting an Elementalist Form tied to humor, and the Mentor Flaw.

label: Ritual Power
summary: A Major Supernatural Virtue giving an at-will supernatural power equivalent to a Ritual Hermetic spell of level 25 or lower, costing Fatigue and Confidence.

label: Rival Magic
summary: Supplement presenting the Augustan Brotherhood.

label: River Aare
summary: River feeding Lake Brienz.

label: River Avon
summary: River on which Bath lies.

label: River Belus
summary: River in Acre where Templar and Hospitaller mills compete for water.

label: River Dordogne
summary: Southern border of the Tribunal.

label: River Nile
summary: River protected by St. Michael.

label: River Rance
summary: River.

label: River Sâone
summary: Eastern border of the Tribunal.

label: River Styx
summary: Underworld river of Charon.

label: River Vilaine
summary: Breton river whose highest sea-going port is Redon.

label: River Yonne
summary: River.

label: Road
summary: Covenant Hook: covenant lies on a major road, river or sea route guaranteeing mundane contact.

label: Road Magic
summary: Neo-Mercurian extension of Mercurian Magic adding Road and Road Network Ranges and Targets; learnable in a season or Initiated as a Minor Virtue.

label: Road Network (Range)
summary: Range reaching anyone on connected roads; equivalent to Arcane Connection, requires ritual magic.

label: Road Network (Target)
summary: Target covering a road network 10,000 paces long; equivalent to Boundary, requires ritual magic.

label: Road (Range)
summary: Range reaching anyone on the same road or path as the caster; equivalent to Voice.

label: Road (Target)
summary: Target covering a road up to 100 paces long; equivalent to Room.

label: Roane
summary: Smaller, less bloodthirsty Highland version of the selkie.

label: Robert Bruce
summary: Claimant to the Scottish throne named successor by Alexander II.

label: Robert de Boron
summary: Author of Joseph d'Arimethie, first to call it the Holy Grail.

label: Robert de Charteris
summary: Example magus who writes a polemic, sponsored by Protinus of Verditius, on the benefits of his Tribunal integrating with mundane society.

label: Robert de Courtenay
summary: Sheriff of Devon who refused to surrender the shrievalty to Falkes de Bréauté, claiming he should have had the wardship of the heir.

label: Robert des Ablèges
summary: Theologian bishop of Bayeux, elected 1206.

label: Robert Grosseteste
summary: A brilliant scholar and official of the bishop of Hereford, born 1170, who is an unGifted natural magician acquainted with the magi of Schola Pythagoranis though he declined to join.

label: Robert Guiscard
summary: Norman mercenary who conquered southern Italy with magic items bought from Roman Magi.

label: Robert I
summary: Brother of Odo, crowned king in 922, died in combat in 923.

label: Robert II
summary: French king whose confidante was Abbo.

label: Robert of Arbrissel
summary: Charismatic hermit and preacher who founded the Abbey of Fontrevrault in 1100.

label: Robert of Chester
summary: Translated the Liber de Compositione Alchemiae into Latin in 1144.

label: Robert of Craon
summary: Grand Master of the Templars (1136-1149).

label: Robert of Sabloel
summary: Grand Master (1191-1193), formerly King Richard's admiral.

label: Robert Poulain
summary: Archbishop of Rouen, a theologian elected 1208, who believes the Order of Hermes heretical.

label: Robert the Bruce
summary: Grandson of the claimant Robert Bruce who leads armies against the English after 1298.

label: Robert the Frisian
summary: Made Bruges his capital in 1093.

label: Robert the Strong
summary: Ninth-century ancestor of Hugh Capet.

label: Robert Wood
summary: An outlaw of Yorkshire in the late 1100s, presumed a rustic-magic hedge wizard and exceptional archer/bowyer/fletcher with magic in his craft, registered as a vis source by Voluntas covenant.

label: Robes of Dusty Dawn
summary: Enchanted lavender-rose robes covered in chalk markings that protect against natural and supernatural threats; the symbol of the Primus Ex Miscellanea, given to Pralix by the Columbae.

label: Robes of Puissant Might
summary: Caitlin's protection 15 robes with no encumbrance.

label: Robin Hood
summary: Cited as a legendary example of crime income, operating with demonic assistance.

label: Robyn Redcap
summary: Demonic familiar of Lord Goulis in the form of a redcap, who keeps his cap red with fresh blood and guards Monksend.

label: Rocamadour
summary: Shrine of Our Lady.

label: Rock of Eternal Life
summary: Rock in Brude's tower said to make its owner live forever.

label: Rock of Viscid Clay
summary: A Muto Terram spell that softens rock so it can be dug out, molded, and manipulated like hard river clay.

label: Rock Swimming
summary: Hagbui power (MuCo 40) to swim through stone or earth.

label: Rod of the Primus
summary: Enchanted rod of Fudarus controlling rooms' environment; symbol of House Tytalus leadership, held by Harpax.

label: Roddam and Green
summary: Two rocky pillars in Piper Gut; once per year Roddam gains a Magic aura and a present person can judge the Wamses' contest for Intellego vis.

label: Rodopi Mountains
summary: Mountains marking the southern extent of the Transylvanian Tribunal in Bulgaria.

label: Roe Deer
summary: Deer considered too small for serious attention.

label: Rogation Blood
summary: Story seed in which blood of virgin boys on a stone feeds an almost-forgotten pagan god that stirs when Rogation grows lax.

label: Rogation Day
summary: April 25th, the day of the perambulation.

label: Rogation Days
summary: Days beginning forty days after Easter when villagers walk the boundaries and boys are abused to remember the landmarks.

label: Roger
summary: Jerbiton magus of Literatus teaching the Humanities.

label: Roger Bacon
summary: Eight-year-old boy near Ilchester foreseen as a new Bonisagus.

label: Roger de Jouy
summary: Flemish knight who shared tournament ransom profits with William Marshal for a year.

label: Roger of Howden
summary: Chronicler who reported Joachim's prophecy to Richard about Saladin.

label: Roger the Great
summary: Robert Guiscard's nephew, named King of Sicily.

label: Rogitien
summary: Mercere alchemist at the Rorschach Chapter who brews longevity potions for redcaps and hoplites; he has the Gentle Gift.

label: Rognvald Kolsson
summary: Earl of Orkney who crusaded in 1152 and was canonized in 1192; a poet boasting of nine skills.

label: Rogues
summary: Mercere magi who pose as Redcaps for their own purposes.

label: Rogziel
summary: An Avenger of Evil whose angel-like name means Wrath of God.

label: Roh-en-Aod
summary: Stone yielding Auram vis.

label: Rok
summary: A storm giant (Might 28 Auram) about 15 feet tall who conjures winds and hail; allied with a ship captain to raise storms against rival merchants.

label: Roland
summary: A great Frankish knight, one of Charlemagne's 12 peers, slain at the Battle of Roncesvals in 778, who wielded the magic sword Durendal forged by Wayland with Verditius as apprentice.

label: Role
summary: The series of symbols and rules a faerie cannot change or break through which it interacts with humans.

label: Role Requires Suffering
summary: Minor Supernatural Flaw: the faerie feels pain and suffers wound penalties like a human.

label: Roll, you clouds, and thunder cry / And strike with flames from empty sky
aliases: Roll, you clouds, and thunder cry / And strike with flames from empty sky
summary: Debauchery/Effusion 25 thunderstorm.

label: Rolling Stone
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character has moved so often that she finds it hard to form community attachments, giving -1 to social rolls within a community.

label: Rollo
summary: Viking chieftain interred in Rouen Cathedral; distant relative of Haland and Harivald.

label: Rollright Stones
summary: A thirty-meter stone circle of twenty-five stones in Oxfordshire, said to be a petrified army and its king; includes the King Stone whose chips ward against demons, watched over by a witch in the form of an elder tree.

label: Roma Nova
summary: A covenant of traditionalist Latin magi founded in Kent in 946, unpopular with Bjornaer, Díedne, and Ex Miscellanea; destroyed by the Díedne in 1008.

label: Roman Army Lore
summary: Ability referenced as used or valued by Tremere magi or creatures.

label: Roman Astrological Correspondences of Mercury
summary: Tractatus attributed to Mercere with a horoscope of Augustus' investiture.

label: Roman Emperor Trajan
summary: A Roman emperor whom God allowed to be saved after death at the request of Pope Gregory the Great.

label: Roman Empire
summary: The ancient empire whose legionaries garrisoned the temple town; its records can be studied as Organization Lore: Roman Empire.

label: Roman Law
summary: Ability appearing in character or covenant library statistics in this text.

label: Roman Lore
summary: Ability appearing in character or covenant library statistics in the Roman Tribunal.

label: Roman Penitential
summary: Halitgar's penitential listing penances for magical and sacrilegious acts.

label: Roman Ritual
summary: Instructions for performing exorcism.

label: Roman roads
summary: Roads that seem to form a great magical network created with the Cult of Mercury.

label: Roman Scribe
summary: Companion vocation: a scribe's second son from Rome copying magical documents for magi.

label: Roman Tribunal Lore
summary: Ability appearing in character or covenant library statistics in this text.

label: Rome Lore
summary: Ability appearing in character or covenant library statistics in the Roman Tribunal.

label: Romer
summary: A young giant of Romerstein castle who fell in love with and secretly married Ruma, daughter of the dwarf king.

label: Romowe Oak
summary: A surviving magical forest spirit of Pomerania in the Eastern Marches; it is likely to possess seekers who attempt communion with it.

label: Romulus
summary: Founder of Rome, suckled by a she-wolf, who slew his twin Remus.

label: Ronan
summary: Irish hermit who settled at St. Renan; St. Ronan's walk is retraced at Locronan.

label: Roncesvalles
summary: Pass where Roland was slain.

label: Room of Stale Air
summary: A Perdo Auram spell (Level 15) that makes the air in a room stuffy and uncomfortable, penalizing physical exertion of breathing creatures.

label: Roots of the Arts
summary: Basic summae texts for nine of the Arts, accepted as the preferred primers for a magus seeking competence to train an apprentice, widely and cheaply available.

label: Rope of Bronze
summary: A Muto Herbam spell (Level 15) with a Terram requisite that turns a piece of plant-fiber rope into superior bronze that does not break under normal circumstances.

label: Rorschach Chapter
summary: A tiny chapter house of the Covenant of the Icy North near Rorschach, home to two Mercere magi and linked by Hermes Portal to the Motherhouse.

label: Rosalba
summary: Covenant founded by Flavia of Jerbiton in 820 in the Yorkshire Dales; destroyed in 899 when all its magi were killed in a Wizards' War with Blackthorn.

label: Roscius
summary: Filius of Verditius who stole the sword Durendal and took it to Verdi; by studying it he and his filii became famous makers of magical swords, founding the Confraternity of Roland.

label: Rose Coast
summary: Pink granite coast.

label: Rose of Jerbiton
summary: A magus of House Jerbiton credited with a version of Flash of the Scarlet Flames that leaves a faint odor of roses where the flash explodes.

label: Rosegarten
summary: Place listed in the Tribunal index.

label: Rosemary Sprig of Rego Vis
summary: Rosemary vis protecting a home from weak wood faeries.

label: Rosh Beth Din
summary: A Major Social Status Virtue for the head who presides at the Beth Din rabbinic court, requiring high Hebrew, Rabbinic Law, and Theology: Judaism.

label: Rosh ha-Shanah
summary: Jewish new year on 1 Tishri when all are judged.

label: Rosmert
summary: Handri's faerie caricature, the imperious-looking Queen of Irencillia's fae and monarch of the Faerie Court.

label: Ross
summary: Remote region where isolated clans speak Gaelic with Pictish elements.

label: Rostock
summary: An expanding Baltic trading town and port, chief town of the Mecklenburg dynasty of Sorbian princes, overshadowed by neighboring Lubeck.

label: Rostrenen
summary: Hawthorn source.

label: Rote
summary: Small numerological spell-like formula cast without die roll, as with Quiet and Still Casting.

label: Rotgiers de Gerberoy
summary: Senior Tremere magus of Montverte, knightly warrior and Tourney champion responsible for martial affairs and raiding.

label: Rotgiers' Talisman Mace
summary: Ornate bejewelled mace enchanted as Rotgiers' talisman.

label: Rothelin
summary: Legendary Tytalus magus who converted, contracted leprosy and joined the Order of Saint Lazarus.

label: Rothiger
summary: Hound of God companion, an itinerant laborer werewolf with red hair who loves to kill in wolf form.

label: Rotomagus
summary: Covenant near Rouen (875-892) founded by apprentices of Sinapis and destroyed when Vikings sacked Rouen.

label: Rottweil
summary: A town of Roman origin (Arae Flaviae) on the eastern edge of the Black Forest, overlooking the upper River Neckar, where butchers trained Rottweilers to pull carts.

label: Rouen
summary: Capital of Normandy on the Seine, Roman Rotomagus, captured by Philip II in 1203; has a cathedral and a declining Jewish community.

label: Rouen Cathedral
summary: Seat of the archdiocese at Rouen, holding saints' writings and the tombs of Norman nobles including Rollo.

label: Roughting Linn
summary: A rock face in Northumberland carved with over sixty cup-and-ring markings, thought to be maps or faerie memorials and possibly carved by Gerfallon of Semitae.

label: Rouncey
summary: Utility horse with courser combat training, favored by squires.

label: Round Shield
summary: Inexpensive shield.

label: Round Shield Parry
summary: Ability listed in a Roman Tribunal vocation template.

label: Round Table
summary: The Arthurian Round Table that rises from a bog each midsummer near Tintagel, which a king might seek to seize.

label: Routed Group
summary: A group that has lost its will to fight and tries to disengage and flee; results from a disordered group failing a Morale check.

label: Rowan Gild
summary: A secretive Rhine political gild formed by Diedne magi who split from the Hawthorn Gild, later joined by Waldherz Bonisagus; its members were exiled and largely destroyed in the Schism War.

label: Rowan of Virtue
summary: Tree from which an Enriched protective amulet grants a ward against creatures of one supernatural Realm for seven years.

label: Rowan Sisterhood
summary: Informal group led by Jacinta, founded during the purge of the Shadow Flambeau, watching for diabolic or vampiric corruption.

label: Roxburgh
summary: Site of a royal mint.

label: Royal Burghs
summary: Towns granted special privileges by the crown, with tollbooth and market cross.

label: Royal Charter
summary: Charter by which a town holds directly from the king, placing it beyond the agricultural aristocracy.

label: Royal Courts
summary: Courts dealing with the king's rights and crimes punishable by death, such as murder and arson.

label: Royal Forest of Dartmoor
summary: An English royal forest composed of moorland, showing that a 'forest' is a hunting reserve rather than woodland.

label: Royal Prise
summary: A special low price that royalty expects when buying at fairs, effectively a tax on the seller; King Henry III's Westminster fair promised to drop these prises.

label: Royal Touch
summary: Power of French kings to cure the King's Evil, possibly from the Holy Oil or Merovech.

label: Roznov
summary: An Autumn covenant in eastern Moravia combining two traditions: a pagan priesthood of Radegast (House Ex Miscellanea at Roznov Castle) and an archconservative House Tremere stronghold (at Roznov Fort).

label: Roznov Castle
summary: The castle housing the Rhine covenant of Roznov on the side of Mount Radhost, with Igor Rastvan's great-hall laboratory at one end.

label: Ruach
summary: Evil spirits (imps) of the Tempters causing misfortune and ill luck, appearing as vermin with twisted human faces; one is released with every freely committed sin.

label: Rubaton Ex Miscellanea
summary: One of the two heads of Vardian's Tomb, associated with its necromancer faction.

label: Rudesheim
summary: A Rhine town on the right bank opposite Bingen, site of the ruined covenant of Rudiaria and the Bromserburg castle; named after the covenant or archbishop Rudbrecht.

label: Rudiaria
summary: A former covenant affiliated to House Flambeau, founded 892 AD on the right bank of the Rhine opposite Bingen; charged with diabolism and destroyed in 969 AD by an apparent catastrophic magical accident.

label: Rudolph, Duke of Burgundy
summary: Took the Frankish throne in 923.

label: Rudolph of Bonisagus
summary: A magus of House Bonisagus and the brainchild behind plans to establish a Fengheld chapter at Durenmar.

label: Rudolph of Wadenschwyl
summary: Knight allied to the Zähringers who eloped with Ida of Unspunnen.

label: Rudolphus of House Bonisagus
summary: One of the most infamous Venatores, Wizard's Marched in 1151 A.D. for persecuting demons so much that they turned their wrath on the Order.

label: Rudophus of Durenmar
summary: Magus convicted of endangering the Order after a demon he pursued attacked the Rhine Redcaps.

label: Rue de la Tabletterie
summary: Paris street where Mathieus's house, an ivory-carving business, stands.

label: Rufino
summary: Early Franciscan follower, a priest and cousin of Clare.

label: Rufus
summary: Example character who takes Inherited Virtue: Large to have a growth spurt around age 10.

label: Ùruisg
summary: Tiny satyr of Scotland that serves as a brownie, with a taste for dairy products and dairymaids.

label: Rule of Clare
summary: Rule devised by Clare, the first written by a woman, based on Francis' ideas and not requiring total enclosure.

label: Rule of Saint Augustine
summary: Monastic rule followed by Augustinian canons, Premonstratensians and many canonesses; fashionable after 1215.

label: Rule of Saint Benedict
summary: The most widespread monastic rule in Mythic Europe, laying down detailed regulations and a daily timetable for monks and nuns; most religious orders follow variants of it.

label: Rule of St. Benedict
summary: Rule established by Benedict governing monastic life of opus Dei, lectio divina and opus manuum.

label: Ruler of (Form)
summary: Spirit power duplicating spells pertaining to a specific substance, e.g. Ruler of Lava, Smoke, Sandstorms, or Fog.

label: Ruler of Nature
summary: Wyzwanie's power duplicating natural weather, water, plant and earth spells.

label: Ruler of Plants
summary: Herbam spirit power used by Lise.

label: Ruma
summary: Daughter of the dwarf king and a mermaid, able to transform into a stream of water; she surfaced to create the Rumaquelle while searching for her husband Romer.

label: Rumael
summary: Demon posing as Neptune, creator and destroyer of Atlantis; Lord of the False Gods, patron of a kingdom that no longer exists; Infernal Might 40.

label: Rumplestiltzkin
summary: Fairy-tale figure who provides service and the chance to marry a prince, but becomes a threat; an example of a faerie playing several roles.

label: Rune Casting Variations
summary: Modifiers to rune casting such as hidden or no name, hidden or no description, extra effort, emphasis and vis (Makt).

label: Rune Duration
summary: A new Hermetic Duration from integrating rune magic, working like Ring but not requiring penetration.

label: Rune Magic
summary: Magic of the Order of Odin that might be integrated into the Children of Odin's repertoire.

label: Rune Scripts
summary: Vitkar formula like formulaic spells.

label: Runes
summary: The 24 runes of the vitkir, Accelerated Abilities used to craft magical effects.

label: Runic magic
summary: Magic of Gifted Viking shape-changers.

label: Runild
summary: Youngest Tremere member of Montverte's inner council, overseeing its library, vis and junior labwork; her familiar is a black cat.

label: Running Dog
summary: Pack hound that pursues prey in pairs by scent, resembling the foxhound.

label: Running Water Weakness
summary: A demonic weakness preventing the demon from crossing running fresh water deriving directly from the earth.

label: Runnymede
summary: Where Magna Carta was signed.

label: Rupertsberg
summary: Abbey near Bingen where Hildegard was abbess from 1150.

label: Rus
summary: One of the three legendary founding brothers of the Slavic peoples, who settled at the River Dnieper with his tribe, the Russians.

label: Rusalka
summary: A type of water nymph, returned dead who come back so their tragedy can be replayed.

label: Russia
summary: Cold northern land where the gyrfalcon lives.

label: Rusted Decay of Ten-Score Years

label: Rusted Decay of Ten Score Years
aliases: Rusted Decay of Ten Score Years
summary: Hermetic spell (PeTe 15) in a Roman Tribunal magus vocation template.

label: Rustem
summary: Slayer of dragons and demons.

label: Rusticus
summary: Assistant of St. Denis, martyred with him.

label: Rye-King
summary: Example story element: a faerie king who has stolen a child.

label: Saïr
summary: Islamic degree of Hell for Sabians.

label: Saadia Gaon
summary: Gaon of Sura (882-942), opponent of the Karaites.

label: Sabaoc
summary: Angel named in Aldebert's heretical prayer. Derived from Sabaoth.

label: Sabaoth
summary: A Fury in the form of an eagle-sized raven with mismatched eyes, able to split into a murder of crows, who ensures long-standing feuds continue.

label: Sabastien filius Luise
summary: Tytalus 'professional intruder' who disarms wards in dead magi's sancta and has one of the highest Parma Magica scores in the Order.

label: Sabath
summary: Ruler of Zebul.

label: Sabaton
summary: Foot armor.

label: Sabbat
summary: A meeting of a folk witch coven held on traditional festival dates, used to trade vis, brew potions cooperatively, Open the Gift and perform initiations.

label: Sabbath (Duration)
summary: Holy magic Duration lasting until dawn of the next day of rest; equal to Sun.

label: Sabbatinus
summary: One of the early followers of Francis.

label: Sabeans
summary: Star-worshipping cult of Harran, Syria, once granted dhimmi status.

label: Sabina of the Seine
summary: A relatively young maga who leads the Viticulturalists league and keeps its collection of casting tablets for agricultural rituals.

label: Sabinus
summary: Lingones chieftain who hid in the cave for nine years.

label: Sabouleux
summary: A court of Parisian argotiers who daub themselves with blood and froth with soap.

label: Sabrina filia Maura
summary: Maga who first improved Bonisagus's longevity potions and became third Primus of House Bonisagus.

label: Sacar
summary: Islamic degree of Hell for Zoroastrians.

label: Sachiko of Merinita
summary: A probably-female Merinita magus of Burnham whose sigil appears at tribunals but who is otherwise unknown to the tribunal.

label: Sack of Constantinople
summary: The 1204 sack of Constantinople.

label: Sacramentals
summary: Minor folk rituals and prayers, versions of invoking a saint.

label: Sacraments
summary: Seven holy ceremonies with supernatural effects that often impart Faith Points and only affect willing participants.

label: Sacred Precepts of Pythagoras
summary: Precepts vowed in a Minor Ordeal Vow of the Fraternity.

label: Sacrifice of Power
summary: Taking a Hermetic Flaw as an Ordeal, considered mythically very appropriate for Initiation.

label: Sacrifices
summary: A Minor laboratory Supernatural Flaw: animal sacrifices are needed for the lab to function (+2 Upkeep, -1 Safety, +1 Warping, -1 Health, -3 Aesthetics).

label: Sacrist
summary: Official responsible for vestments, candles, incense and upkeep of the church.

label: Sacristan
summary: Monk who rouses the others with a bell for Matins.

label: Safeguard the Clandestine Conversation
summary: Mu(Re)Im 10 spell muddling the images and sounds of those within a circle to outside observers and scriers.

label: Saga
summary: The ongoing campaign that discoveries like the Resting Place of Mars can alter.

label: Saga Speed
summary: Rules concept for the pace of a saga (slow, fast, pulsed) affecting how transformations manifest in play.

label: Saggitarius
summary: The Technique of the Archer, a certamen style introduced by a Merinita magus to humiliate a Tremere rival; it adds heavily to Attack but can do only one Fatigue level of damage, and many Tremere dispute its legitimacy.

label: Sagitar of Tremere
summary: A Tremere magus who falsely claimed the Criamon Primacy, discovering it was voluntary mystical slavery; his contrite ghost haunts the Cave of Twisting Shadows.

label: Sagittarius
summary: Sign of the Zodiac with its own element, temperament and decans in astrological correspondences.

label: Sahir
summary: A type of non-Hermetic wizard of the Mythic Middle East; an Infernally-aligned sahir bound the Buran of Yenghissar within his ancestral sword using the Goetic Art of Binding.

label: Sail the Wind
summary: People of the Clouds power to fly on winds and lift ships.

label: Sailor's Foretaste of the Morrow
summary: An Intellego Auram spell (Level 15) that tells the caster precisely tomorrow's weather and gives a general impression of the week ahead at the casting location.

label: Saint
summary: Holy dead accepted into heaven who intercede and grant miracles; greater, area and local saints.

label: Saint Alban
summary: Martyr whose shrine inspired Christina of Markyate to vow virginity.

label: Saint Almeric
summary: Canonized Cistercian saint.

label: Saint Alphege
summary: Under whom Bath Abbey adopted the Benedictine Rule.

label: Saint Ambrose
summary: Patron saint of Milan whose rite is used by its Church.

label: Saint Andrew
summary: A saint whose relics were stolen from Constantinople by the bishop of Amalfi in 1210, prompting Andru's personal grudge.

label: Saint Andrew's
summary: Scottish archdiocese raised to primacy.

label: Saint Anne
summary: Mother of the mother of God, much revered in Brittany; Nolwenn took her name.

label: Saint Anthony's Fire
summary: A Minor Sanguine Disease from possession by a minor demon in the intestines; cured by exorcism.

label: Saint Barbara
summary: A patron saint of French masons, whose feast day is December 4.

label: Saint Bartholomew
summary: Saint whose day is August 24th; example target of Devotion.

label: Saint Basil the Great
summary: Saint whose devotees are immune to Patarus' powers.

label: Saint Beatus
summary: British saint who converted the Jungfrau region and evicted a dragon from his cave.

label: Saint Beatus' Cave
summary: Cave listed in the Tribunal index.

label: Saint Bernard Pass
summary: Alpine pass listed in the index.

label: Saint Brendan
summary: Patron of Irish sailors and arguably intercessor for islands in the Ocean.

label: Saint Bruno
summary: Author of the Statutes followed by the Carthusians.

label: Saint Christopher
summary: Patron of travelers; those who see his likeness and call on him are believed not to die that day on the road.

label: Saint Crispin
summary: One of the patron saints of shoemakers, a third-century Roman preacher who made shoes; feast day October 25.

label: Saint Crispinian
summary: One of the patron saints of shoemakers, a third-century Roman preacher who made shoes; feast day October 25.

label: Saint Croix
summary: Castle of a sympathetic noble in the Dordogne where the Illuminati inner circle meets.

label: Saint Cuthbert
summary: Seventh-century hermit and later bishop who lived on Inner Farne, performed miracles there, and drove the demons out to Megstone; the most popular saint in Northern England.

label: Saint Cuthbert's Gut
summary: Channel between West Wideopen and Inner Farne, dangerous in stormy weather.

label: Saint Cyprian
summary: Pre-Hermetic magus saint to whom Valnastium's main church is dedicated, often confused with Saint Cyprian of Carthage.

label: Saint Cyprian of Antioch
summary: Sorcerer and perhaps diabolist who tried to seduce a Christian virgin with magic, then forsook evil; patron of the church at Valnastium.

label: Saint Denis's Lendit Fair
summary: A fair near Paris founded by King Dagobert in the seventh century for the benefit of the Abbey of St. Denis; once the most important fair in France until the Champagne cycle took over.

label: Saint Dominic
summary: Founder of the Order of Preachers (Dominicans), a trained scholastic from the cathedral school of Palencia preaching against heresy in Lombardy; historically dies 6 August 1221.

label: Saint Dunstan
summary: The patron saint of blacksmiths, whose feast day is May 19.

label: Saint Edmund
summary: King and martyr whose day is November 20th, with a power to Bestow Fertility invoked at Bury Saint Edmunds.

label: Saint Eligius
summary: The patron saint of armorers, whose feast day is December 1.

label: Saint Elisabeth
summary: Daughter of the king of Hungary and wife of the landgrave Louis IV of Thuringia, who devotes her life to the needy; subject of the miracle of roses and later canonized as patron of Marburg's poor.

label: Saint Elizabeth of Hungary
summary: A saint to be adopted as patron of bakers, who will die in 1231 and be canonized four years later; feast day November 17.

label: Saint Eugenia
summary: Early Roman martyr who, in legend, wore men's clothing and became an abbot; patron for women seeking religious life as men.

label: Saint Euphemia of Chalcedon
summary: Martyr venerated by the Templars; her heart and body are kept at Castle Pilgrim.

label: Saint-Evroult
summary: Chartered village outside an abbey in Normandy.

label: Saint Francis
summary: Founder of the Franciscans, born 1181 to a cloth-merchant family, who embraced absolute poverty and preaching; possesses True Faith and supernatural Abilities.

label: Saint Francis of Assisi
summary: Saint who recently tamed the Wolf of Gubbio.

label: Saint Gallen
summary: Place whose abbots own a palace near Rorschach; Valnastium has a chapter there and the abbot is an ally of Valnastium.

label: Saint Gertrude of Nivelles
summary: The patroness of the recently dead who appeared in visions to many (often unGifted) Donatores, with souls in her care for their first night after death.

label: Saint Gilbert
summary: Founder of the Gilbertines, died 1190 and canonized 1202; feast on February 4th.

label: Saint Godric
summary: A historical peddler, merchant, pirate, hermit, and saint of northeastern England who settled at Finchale near Durham; renowned for austerity, hymns, and prophecy, he died in 1170 at age 105.

label: Saint Gotthard Pass
summary: New pass opened around 1220, its bridge said to be built by the Devil.

label: Saint Guthlac
summary: Saint who saw his cell filled with black troops of unclean spirits, quoted from the Life of Saint Guthlac.

label: Saint Hildegarde
summary: Abbess of Zurich who gave Saint Meinrad a figurine of the Virgin.

label: Saint Homobonus
summary: The recently canonized patron saint of clothiers, a tailor from Cremona who gave free clothes to the poor; his feast day is November 13.

label: Saint Honoratus of Arles
summary: The patron saint of bakers, whose feast day is January 16.

label: Saint James
summary: Saint whose tomb and relics are at Santiago de Compostela.

label: Saint Jerome
summary: Saint after whom Bonosus named an island (Sveti Jerolim).

label: Saint Joan
summary: Legendary woman said to have held the papacy as Pope John VIII in the mid-ninth century; the story was initiated by a demon.

label: Saint John Gualbert
summary: Founder of the Vallumbrosans who spared his relative's murderer and saw a crucifix bow its head.

label: Saint John of the Cross
summary: Future systematic mystic whose works are not yet written in 1220.

label: Saint John's Eve
summary: Time when faerie hills and barrows open; characters climbing there usually return at dawn.

label: Saint John the Evangelist
summary: Saint with whom Marie of Oignes frequently conversed.

label: Saint Justina of Antioch
summary: Christian virgin whom Cyprian tried to seduce; shares the feast of 26 September with him.

label: Saint Keyne
summary: Pious virgin saint whose well and prayers produce miracles near Keynsham.

label: Saint Keyne's chair
summary: Magical chair on Mount Saint Michael.

label: Saint Keyne's Well
summary: Miraculous well; whichever spouse drinks first gains the upper hand in marriage.

label: Saint Luke
summary: One of the patron saints of glassmakers, whose feast day is October 18.

label: Saint Malachy
summary: Irish Cistercian saint, friend of Bernard; obscure prophecies are falsely attributed to him.

label: Saint Marina the Monk
summary: A medieval saint, used as a character-concept example, who lived disguised as a monk, accepted false blame for a pregnancy, and was revealed to be a woman only after death.

label: Saint Mark
summary: One of the patron saints of glassmakers, whose feast day is April 25.

label: Saint Mark's Square
summary: Square in Venice above which a benandanti militia meets its rivals in immaterial form.

label: Saint Martin
summary: Bishop of Tours and founder of the Abbey of Ligugé.

label: Saint Martin of Tours
summary: Saint at whose tomb a miracle swayed Clovis.

label: Saint Mary of the Angels
summary: Little chapel in Francis' valley near the original Franciscan settlement.

label: Saint Maudez
summary: Sixth-century saint who cleared Maudez Island of vermin; can substitute for Saint Cuthbert.

label: Saint Maurice
summary: Christian soldier martyred in 302 for refusing to worship Roman gods; his ring is a powerful relic.

label: Saint Meinrad
summary: Hermit saint murdered at Einsiedeln in 861, whose tamed ravens followed his murderers.

label: Saint Nicholas
summary: A saint venerated in northwestern Mythic Europe for miraculously resuscitating three children murdered and pickled by an innkeeper; the planned Kolding church is dedicated to him.

label: Saint Nicholas of Myra
summary: Saint to whom each house of Saint Bernard was originally dedicated.

label: Saint Norbert
summary: Founder of the Premonstratensians with 12 disciples.

label: Saint Odilo
summary: The Abbot at Cluny who created the Feast of All Soul's Day and promoted the Truce of God; patron saint of souls in Purgatory who appeared to Donatores in holy orders.

label: Saint Patrick
summary: Saint who banished the peist and all serpents from Ireland and was shown the entrance to Purgatory by Christ.

label: Saint Paul
summary: An apostle cited regarding slavery, counseling slaves to obey their masters while requiring masters not to abuse them.

label: Saint Paul's Nunnery
summary: Benedictine nunnery near Bastia, Umbria, where Clare first took refuge.

label: Saint Paulus
summary: Founded the monastery at the bottom of Cennet.

label: Saint Pierre
summary: Place listed in the Tribunal index.

label: Saint Polycarp
summary: Saint whose relics sanctify Templar woolen cords.

label: Saint Rémi
summary: Archbishop of Reims who baptized and anointed Clovis; possible source of the Royal Touch.

label: Saint Riquier
summary: Saint whose body Hugh Capet recovered.

label: Saint Robert
summary: Named as founder of the Vallumbrosan order, who ordered Peter to face trial by ordeal.

label: Saint's Island
summary: Saint's Island on Lough Dearg, with an Empyreal aura of 4 and a small church whose crypt cell holds the entrance to Purgatory.

label: Saint's Thigh Bone
summary: A relic with Faith Score 3 and a Cure Blindness power, kept at the example Covenant Chapel.

label: Saint Sabina
summary: Titular church of Tommaso da Capua.

label: Saint Severus of Ravenna
summary: Married fourth-century archbishop of Ravenna chosen by God through a dove; a saint for married priests and their wives.

label: Saint Stephen
summary: The first Christian martyr and patron saint of masons, whose feast day is December 26.

label: Saint Stephen of Hungary
summary: Geza's son, who married Gisela of Bavaria in 996.

label: Saint Stephen the founder
summary: Canonized Cistercian saint and founder.

label: Saint Sylvester
summary: Saint said to have slain the Leviathan dragon on New Year's Day 1000, possibly Pope Sylvester II.

label: Saint Thaddeus
summary: Patron of penitent thieves whose sacred places ward the Privy Counselor.

label: Saint Ursmar
summary: Saint whose relics were placed on the church floor at Blaringhem in 1060 to plead for mercy.

label: Saint Ursula
summary: Fourth-century English princess martyred with her companions at Cologne, whose bones were discovered in 1155.

label: Saint Ursula of Cologne
summary: Saint whose silver-covered skull is kept at the Paris Temple.

label: Saint Valéry
summary: Saint whose body Hugh Capet recovered.

label: Saint Victor
summary: Church in Paris to which the legate James is linked.

label: Saint Wolfgang
summary: Priest who founded a church in the Abersee valley in 976 where his axe fell and defeated the Devil.

label: Saint XII Apostoli
summary: Titular church of Stefano di Cecanno.

label: Saintes

label: Saintly Reputation

label: Saints' Miracles
summary: Supernatural deeds performed by saints expressed as powers channelled from God.

label: Sal Albrod
summary: One of the seven salts in Bladud's fermenter.

label: Sal Alkine
summary: One of the seven salts in Bladud's fermenter.

label: Sal Almelke
summary: One of the seven salts in Bladud's fermenter.

summary: One of the seven salts in Bladud's fermenter.

summary: One of the seven salts in Bladud's fermenter.

label: Sal Gemmce
summary: One of the seven salts in Bladud's fermenter.

label: Sal Petrce
summary: One of the seven salts in Bladud's fermenter.

label: Saladin
summary: Muslim leader said by Joachim to be the sixth of seven persecutors of the Church; some regard him as the Antichrist.

label: Salamander
summary: A small poisonous magical salamander that seeks warmth, extinguishing fires, and can pass through a weak Aegis of the Hearth.

label: Salat

label: Salerno

label: Salgfräulein
summary: A wood-wife who dresses in white and sits under old larch trees, singing.

label: Salian Franks

label: Salii

label: Salisbury Plain
summary: Plain around Stonehenge.

label: Sallet
summary: Late medieval rounded helmet with visor.

label: Sally

label: Salmo
summary: A descendent of Ilfetu who became primus after the Schism War and refocused House Bjornaer toward a more traditional Hermetic mould.

label: Salome
summary: Herod's daughter at whose request John the Baptist was beheaded.

label: Salomon
summary: King of Brittany who took the throne by assassination; martyred in the ninth century.

label: Salterello
summary: Leaping dance from Naples.

label: Salutem
summary: Learned magician Form governing health of humans, animals and plants; broader yet narrower than Corpus.

label: Salvani
summary: Tribe of gnomes who wove moonlight into the Dolomites, turning them white.

label: Salvirius
summary: A subtle faerie courtier of the Boar King who can teach Virtues, including Diedne Magic, to the Boar King's magus allies.

label: Salzburg
summary: City listed in the Tribunal index.

label: Sama'
summary: Sufi group meditation of listening to music or poetry composed for God to reach an ecstatic state.

label: Samaria
summary: Native land of Simon Magus.

label: Samein Guernicus
summary: Zoroastrian holy magus of House Guernicus who destroyed an evil spirit at Tribunal.

label: Samhain
summary: Sabbat on 31 October/1 November, also All Hallow's Eve; the Stonehenge grand sabbat is held then.

label: Sammael
summary: In Jewish demonology the personification of evil and true Devil, who sent the serpent to tempt Eve; husband of Lilith.

label: Samnium of Bjornaer
summary: Member of Sansaron.

label: Samos
summary: Ionian island, birthplace of Pythagoras and site of his Semicircle school.

label: Samovily
summary: Bulgarian mystical maidens, mostly faeries (one infernal), including woodland archers who ride deer, water and air spirits, and breath-stealing ghosts of brides.

label: Samovily Blood
summary: Minor Supernatural Virtue granting Faerie Blood bonuses plus one bonus (archery, riding, music, Presence or underwater) from descent from samovily.

label: Samson
summary: Hero of the Book of Judges, cited as an example of the hero role.

label: Samuel ben Judah ibn Tibbon
summary: Translator of Maimonides living in Marseilles until 1230.

label: Samuel ibn Tibbon
summary: The translator who rendered Maimonides' Guide for the Perplexed from Arabic into Hebrew.

label: Samuel, King of the Bulgars
summary: Bulgarian king who died of shock on seeing his blinded army in 1014.

label: Samuil
summary: Samuil, Angelic Guide, a Cherub who with Raguel transported Enoch through the Seven Heavens and now delivers visions to saints and prophets.

label: Samur
summary: Town grown around a monastery for St. Florent's relics, hosting tournaments in July.

label: San Damiano Crucifix
summary: Byzantine-style crucifix in San Damian from which a voice told Francis to repair God's house.

label: San Pietro
summary: Cathedral in Bologna around which university instruction occurs; some clergy join the Mathematici.

label: San Silvi
summary: Vallumbrosan monastery burned during the simony conflict.

label: Sancia filia Sabrina
summary: Perdo Corpus archmage awarded the Sinews site at the Grand Tribunal of 865, who founded the Longevity Project.

label: Sanctuary
summary: The church, churchyard and cemetery are places where fugitives may shelter for up to 40 days.

label: Sanctuary of the Alps
summary: One of the original Tribunals created at the Second Grand Tribunal in 865.

label: Sanctuary of Virginity
summary: Saint Power available through invoking Muslim holy forbears or relics.

label: Sanctum

label: Sanctum Law
summary: Grand Tribunal rulings protecting sanctums and texts marked with a sanctum mark or House symbol; reading such texts is a low crime.

label: Sandalphon
summary: One of the three largest beings in existence, who carries the prayers of the faithful to Heaven; his tears fell to earth when Muhammad died.

label: Sanguine Humor's Blessing
summary: A Major General Virtue granting bonuses to rolls based on a character's True Feeling Story Flaw, drawing on emotional bonds; the defining Virtue of Orphic magoi.

label: Sansaron
summary: Reclusive covenant founded 951 in carved passages under the ruins of Carthage, studying ancient Carthaginian magic and selling items to mundanes of Tunis.

label: Santiago de Compostela
summary: Site of the shrine and tomb of Saint James, a major pilgrimage destination.

label: Saoshyant
summary: The Savior, Seed of Zoroaster, from whom the elixir of eternal life was handed down.

label: Saoshyant's Elixir
summary: CrCo50 Zoroastrian ritual requiring ordeal by molten metal and sacrifice of a holy bull; the drinker need not make aging rolls and cannot die while following Zoroastrianism, gaining Warping instead.

label: Sap the Griffin's Strength
summary: A general Perdo Vim spell invented by Philippus Niger, like Demon's Eternal Oblivion but working on creatures with Magic Might.

label: Sapphire of Virtue
summary: Gem containing 1 pawn of Intellego vis that can be Enriched by full moonlight to confer the Intuition Virtue.

label: Saracen Sorcerers
summary: Non-Hermetic Muslim magicians of Africa and the Saracen armies.

label: Saracens
summary: Muslims to whom Francis sought to preach; the Franciscans in Morocco stirred dissent between Christians and Saracens.

label: Sarah
summary: A young Gifted girl with Entrancement and Magic Sensitivity in the example.

label: Sarcophagus of the Resting Place of Mars
aliases: Sarcophagus of the Resting Place of Mars
summary: A huge empty sarcophagus for a being 50 feet tall in the tomb's center; any damage to it repairs on the next new moon.

label: Sardinia
summary: The Mediterranean island, dotted with nuraghi and magic auras, where Hephaestus built his famous forge and House Verditius's domus magna Verdi stands.

label: Sardinia Lore
summary: Ability appearing in character or covenant library statistics in the Roman Tribunal.

label: Sarmatian Sea Snail
summary: Pony-sized magical snails of the North Sea that eat magical stone and fight in swarms; Magic Might 7 (Aquam).

label: Satan
summary: The tempter who led Adam and Eve to sin in the Garden of Eden, bringing about Original Sin; the devil to whom an evil lord might sell his soul for infernal powers.

label: Satanim
summary: A group of angels ruled by Satan in Jewish belief, assisting him in opposing man.

label: Satqiel
summary: An angel named in some lists of the archangels.

label: Saturn
summary: Planet influencing age, time, wisdom and resisting distraction; governs Perception.

label: Satyr
summary: Smaller, cowardly faun-like faeries with donkey ears and horse tails, notorious for sexual violence.

label: Satyr Blood
summary: Faerie Blood variety granting Communication and Presence bonuses with sexually compatible characters.

label: Satyriskoi
summary: Child-satyrs.

label: Satyrs of the Black Forest
summary: Satyrs denied entry to Devil's Lane.

label: Saulpatrick
summary: Site on the Circuit of Saint Patrick.

label: Savantism
summary: A Minor General Flaw in which the character is simpleminded with halved experience but exceptionally gifted in one favored Ability with a +3 specialization bonus.

label: Savelli Family
summary: Roman family controlling the ruined temple to Jupiter used as a fish market.

label: Savoy
summary: Region with many ruined Hermetic settlements.

label: Sawm
summary: Fasting during Ramadan.

label: Saxons
summary: Historical Germanic people whose history, by Widukind of Corvey, is a cited period source.

label: Saxony
summary: A large and important duchy of fertile lowlands and cities in the Rhine Tribunal, ancestral home of the Welf family and rival to the Hohenstaufens.

label: Scale Armor
summary: Small overlapping plates on backing.

label: Scales of Magical Weight
summary: Hermetic spell listed among the spells known by a magus in this text.

label: Scales of the Heart
summary: A Power held by the She-Wolf that a lupercus can acquire as a Lesser Power Virtue. It costs one Fatigue level and needs no words or gestures.

label: Scales of the Magical Weight
summary: An Intellego Vim spell used to weigh an unknown amount of vis against a known amount to determine the number of pawns present.

label: Scan
summary: Ability appearing in character or creature statistics in this text.

label: Scandinavia
summary: Northern lands where hunters pursue reindeer and gyrfalcons live; produces fine rounceys.

label: Scapulomancy
summary: Divinatory method using roasting shoulder blades, listed among Ceremonial Augury Phenomena.

label: Scarecrow
summary: Straw manikin invented in a story seed after a plague; faeries are drawn to them and they can take on faerie roles, even forming armies.

label: Scarf of Healing
summary: A wondrous scarf that copies the effects of the spell Bind Wound (Craft Level 14).

label: Scartaris
summary: Vindolanda's Icelandic complex and sanctum beneath glacial ice, target of Julius's assault.

label: Scattering Like Light
summary: A MuTe(Im) Level 30 spell that changes metal in an object into iconic species carried off by passing light, disintegrating objects; originally created for metal plating.

label: Scent of Peaceful Slumber
summary: A spell that makes everyone in a room fall asleep over a few seconds, with the smell of lilacs in their nostrils.

label: Scent of the Predator
summary: A CrMe 20 Scent-Target spell that fills anyone smelling the caster with a sensation of menace, cowing or intimidating targets.

label: Scent of Water
summary: Anonymous Dowsing Summa in the Reims coven library.

label: Schönau
summary: Site of the Benedictine nunnery of Elizabeth and a Cistercian monastery where Hildegund lived.

label: Schöne Lau
summary: A beautiful reclusive water faerie of Blautopf Pool with webbed feet and powers of divination, banished there by her faerie-king husband because she could not laugh; she foretells visitors' futures.

label: Schadrit
summary: The ancient maga of Ex Miscellanea who leads Dankmar with malice; a former Bonisagus apprentice cast out with her mistress Aschlaranda, she is an expert in Faerie Magic.

label: Schism War
summary: A Hermetic war (also called the Sundering/Domination) during which a pagan-filled House was annihilated and a tyrannical House (Tremere) was shattered; House Jerbiton withdrew and later aided reconstruction.

label: Schism War Lore
summary: Ability appearing in character or covenant library statistics in this text.

label: Schleswig
summary: A Holstein town by the fjord of the River Schlei, grown next to a Benedictine cloister of St. Johannis near the ruins of the old Viking city of Haithabu.

label: Schola Pythagoranis
summary: A Hermetic covenant sited on the edge of Cambridge whose magi disguise themselves as a scholarly organization; it invited fleeing Oxford masters to Cambridge and was visited by Robert Grosseteste.

label: Scholae Magicae
summary: Schools of magic for training apprentices, mostly failed attempts since the 10th century.

label: Scholasticus
summary: Chapter office (or chancellor) responsible for the church school.

label: Scholastus
summary: A magus of House Jerbiton, the sole surviving member of Treverorum, who announced his covenant's abolition in 1172 AD and departed for the Greater Alps, held liable for its unpaid fine.

label: Scholomance
summary: A covenant in the Transylvanian Tribunal that is a school for future apprentices, agents, and companions, set in an intermittently accessible regio and reputed to be a school for sorcerers run by the devil.

label: School of Apromor
summary: A versatile school of magical combat within House Flambeau built on the Technique of Perdo, emphasizing destruction, indirect attacks, and multiple Forms; one of the most study-intensive schools.

label: School of Boreas
summary: A narrowly defined Flambeau combat school relying on the single Perdo Ignem combination, using cold and darkness; developed by the magus Boreas to bridge the Flambeau and Apromor lineages.

label: School of Chartres
summary: A medieval cathedral school whose writers (Thierry the Breton, William of Conches, Bernard Silvestris) produced foundational works on cosmology and natural philosophy still taught in Mythic Europe's universities.

label: School of Ebroin
summary: A minor combat school within the Schools of Sebastian family, based on conjuring animals.

label: School of Marosa
summary: A minor combat school within the Schools of Sebastian family, based on Herbam attacks.

label: School of Ramius
summary: A Flambeau combat school that ignores Magic Resistance by using mundane physical attacks supported by magical enhancements, emphasizing defense and Parma Magica; created by Ramius.

label: School of St Geneviève
summary: A cathedral school in Paris where the scholastic luminary Peter Abelard taught.

label: School of the Founder
summary: A Flambeau combat school based on the magic of Flambeau himself, broader than Boreas and favoring the Form of Ignem, requiring penetration of Magic Resistance.

label: School of the Swordsman
summary: Balanced certamen school of the Founder Tremere, reflected in the basic rules.

label: School of Vilano
summary: The most commonly used Flambeau combat school in the Order, relying on indirect attacks that bypass Magic Resistance; created by the magus Vilano and requiring no specific Arts.

label: Schooled in Crime
summary: A Minor General Virtue granting 50 extra experience to spend on Abilities related to thievery such as Stealth, Legerdemain, and Guile.

label: Schools of Magical Combat
summary: Informal styles of fighting magic recognized within House Flambeau, each named after the pioneering magus who invented it, used to classify combative approaches.

label: Schools of Sebastian
summary: A catch-all family of minor Flambeau combat schools that conjure harmful objects or substances using Forms other than Ignem; named for the hedge-wizard magus Sebastian.

label: Schwall
summary: An eccentric elderly Bjornaer magus and Wilderist of the Hawthorn Gild, formerly of Rheinstein, living at the Rhinefalls; he plots to release the Rhine elemental and merge with its spirit.

label: Schwarzburg
summary: A Rhine covenant in the Swabian Jura (857-885) that warred with neighboring Arae Flaviae, causing the Tribunal to abolish both covenants.

label: Schwarzholz
summary: A dark faerie prince who, in a variant, takes over the Cursewood and mimics the Infernal taint to torment Wyzwanie.

label: Schwytzers
summary: People of Schwyz whose sudden appearance is linked to the Vanishing Away of Tarragon Vale.

label: Schwyz
summary: Region near which Tarragon Vale lies.

label: Scilly Isles
